## 1. What a borough looks like on an ordinary Tuesday

- **THE BOAT AND THE ENGINE ARE BOTH OUT OF THE BOROUGH ON A TUESDAY AND NEITHER WAS ASKED TO GO, AND IT IS THE FIRST TIME IN THIS ACCOUNT THAT THE SACRIFICE HAS BEEN DESCRIBED AS AN ORDINARY WEEK INSTEAD OF AS A NIGHT.** Tomas Renn put it in about a minute: the thing you get used to isn't the work, it's knowing where two vans are, and right now I know where one is.
- **THE ONLY NEW FACT IN THE WHOLE OF IT: A VAN THAT USED TO COME BACK ON A SUNDAY NOW COMES BACK WHEN IT COMES BACK.** It came in at ten past ten on the Saturday. Nobody on that parade looked up. It used to have a name — my lot said Sunday, the Lowdale lad said Sunday, the man at the bottom house said Sunday because he'd heard the Lowdale lad say it, and none of those three had ever been asked by anybody, and that is the mechanism.
- **JONAS MERCER ASKED ONE QUESTION AND GOT *NOBODY CAN TELL YOU THAT EITHER*, WHICH IS NOT THE SAME AS *NOBODY CAN TELL YOU WHICH DAY*, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF WHAT SIX WEEKS DID.**
- **THE LOW END OF PEVERELL STREET IS COVERED BY ONE MAN WHO WAS NEVER ASKED AND IS NOT ON ANYTHING.** A woman came out of a back yard for a bucket, he answered her, and nobody asked him a second question. That was the whole of the conversation at the bottom of that street.

## 2. The pact, as a thing rather than as a feeling

- **THE PACT HOLDS, AND IT HOLDS BECAUSE NOBODY IS COUNTING IT, AND THE PROOF IS A COLUMN IN A BOOK THAT HAS BEEN RULED SINCE 1987 WITH A GAP IN IT ABOUT TWO INCHES DEEP, AND A LINE THAT IS NOT A CLAIM IS IN THE GAP.**
- **THE MAN IN HIS FORTIES AT THE PENHALE OFFICE REFUSED A FIGURE AND SAID WHY, AND IT IS THE REASON THE PACT HOLDS: I could tell you how much money went through that shed last year, to the penny, and I have never once been asked, and the day somebody writes a number like that down it stops being a fact about a yard and becomes a figure about a yard, and a figure about a yard is how you get a yard that somebody has to have a good year.**
- **NINE YARDS ON THAT BEND, NONE OF WHICH CAN REFUSE ANYBODY, AND ABOUT FOUR OF THEM HAVE NEVER SENT A CREW OUT AND NEVER TOOK ONE IN AND THEY PUT MONEY IN EXACTLY THE SAME. THERE IS NO LIST ON WHICH THOSE FOUR ARE THE FOUR, BECAUSE THERE IS NO LIST.**
- **HALDANE PERRY REFUSED TO LET THE WALL SHEET DOWN, AND THE SECOND OF HIS TWO REASONS IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS: you'd take it away and come back and ask me what it means, and I've got four men and a woman in this county who could put a bit of paper in front of me and make me say something about it, and you're not one of them and I'd rather you stayed not one of them.**
- **THE SECOND LINE UNDER THE FIRST ON THAT WALL IS STILL NOT EXPLAINED BY ANYBODY AND THAT IS CORRECT.** It is on the page as a line nobody prints. In 0246 a character is asked about it and the man in his forties refuses: he has got a theory and has never once been asked and is not going to stand in a hut and guess at a woman.

## 3. The street, the hose, and one sentence

- **THE SENTENCE, WHICH IS THE ONLY SENTENCE, AND IT IS ABOUT A TUESDAY AND NOT ABOUT ANYTHING ELSE, AND IT WAS SAID TO A MAN ON A LADDER: *If your lot are out on a Tuesday, I'll come down and bring that hose out, and I don't want it on that board.* THE MAN ON THE LADDER SAID *RIGHT* AND WENT BACK UP THE LADDER.**
- **THE HOSE IS THE LENGTH THAT HAS BEEN ON THE WALL AT NUMBER FORTY-ONE SINCE THE WET WEEK IN THE NOVEMBER BEFORE LAST, WITH A GREY LINE OF DIRT BEHIND IT WHERE IT HAS BEEN LYING IN ONE PLACE. A PUMP IS NOT A RESCUE AND A HOSE IS NOT A ROTA ROW AND NEITHER SENTENCE IS SAID OR IMPLIED IN ANY CHAPTER.**
- **THE ROUTE BY WHICH ANYTHING REACHES THE BOTTOM OF PEVERELL STREET IS A MAN FROM A SHOP ON THE PARADE WHO STOPS ON THE STEP AND SAYS THE WATER IS OFF.** It has been that route for the thirty-odd years the man has lived there and it is not a system and nobody could be shown to be running it.
- **NOBODY ASKED HIM A QUESTION.** Jonas Mercer asked nothing on any of three evenings that week and had nothing else to do with them, and his sum that day was five hundred and seventy-three.

## 4. The price, and it is not a triumph

- **THE PRICE CAME BACK DOWN AND IT CAME BACK DOWN FOR THE SAME REASON IT WENT UP, AND NOBODY IS A HERO AND NOBODY IS A VILLAIN, AND THE THING THAT GOES UP AND DOWN IN THIS BOROUGH IS A TUESDAY.** The woman in the second house of Marsh Lane is back to a hundred and eighteen and would rather not be pleased about it: it came down the day the boat came back and I had nothing to do with the boat coming back.
- **THE DRAIN MAN IS BACK TO ABOUT WHAT HE HAD IN FEBRUARY AND IS NOT BACK. FOUR STREETS BECAME TWO AND A HALF IN MAY, AND ONE OF THE TWO WHO CAME IN HAS STOPPED COMING IN, SO HE HAS TWO AND THREE-QUARTER STREETS. BACK WOULD BE FOUR, AND THAT IS THE PART HE DOES NOT GET BACK.**
- **THE FOUR COMPANIES SAID THE SAME THING FOR THE FIFTH TIME AND NONE OF THEM ADDED TO IT.** The Corrance account is down about a sixth on its book and the rate is still on a board on the shelf and will not be read. Sarn has never turned a job away in twenty years. Marchmont's card is about a tenth above the shared yard and nobody has asked the man in the office by the gate since the first of May. Lowdale's man says the plant went out on a Friday and came back on a Sunday and that he could not tell you what he would do differently if they had not come back, and that he has wanted blood in it since March and would charge more, and that he has a diary and not a thing.

## 5. The right of return, asked of a person

- **THE ASK WAS PUT BY THE MAN OF ABOUT EIGHTEEN, OUT LOUD, ONE PERSON AT A TIME, IN A DOORWAY, WITH NOTHING WRITTEN DOWN. HE DID NOT MAKE A LIST AND THE REASON IS NOT A PRINCIPLE: he has nobody's names except the ones he already knew from standing in rooms.**
- **SOMEBODY SAID YES WHO IS NOT THE MAN WITH THE PUMP, AND WHAT THEY SAID YES TO WAS A DAY, AND THE FINDING IS THAT A RIGHT OF RETURN IN THIS BOROUGH IS CURRENTLY THE SIZE OF ONE TUESDAY: one Tuesday and a man who finishes at two, and the Tuesday after that he's in Leeds till Wednesday, and the Tuesday after that nobody knows.**
- **THE ASK IS NOT RECIPROCAL AND WAS NOT SOLD AS RECIPROCAL, AND THAT WAS PUT TO HIM IN A ROAD AND HE AGREED WITH IT: if you pretend it is reciprocal this becomes a thing with two halves, and a thing with two halves gets a name, and the name gets a person under it, and then it's the other thing.**
- **THE ONLY PERSON WHO HAD EVER BEEN RELIABLY THERE WAS NOT ASKED, AND THAT IS ARITHMETIC AND NOT SENTIMENT: his own name is in a drawer in his kitchen four doors up the street, and he would have been the fourth name on anybody's list and was on nobody's.**

## 6. The six, and a wrong answer left standing

- **THE FIRST TIME ANYWHERE IN THIS ACCOUNT THAT A WRONG ANSWER HAS BEEN PUT INTO A ROOM AND LEFT THERE. THE MAN IN HIS SIXTIES SAID THAT THE REGISTER IS THE DATED THING THAT WILL BE THE FIRST ONE PROVABLE, SAID SO BEFORE HE PUT HIS HAND UP, SAID IT IS WRONG, AND THE ROOM DID NOT CORRECT HIM.**
- **WHY IT IS WRONG: the register is at nineteen, the last entry is a bulb, the line under it goes down the page and stops about two inches short of the bottom, and everything this borough has done since is not in it, because it was not written down, deliberately, by about nine people in this room over about seven weeks.**
- **WHY HE PUT IT THERE: somebody will say it anyway, and if nobody in the room can take it apart then the room goes home with a wrong thing in it that everybody can repeat, and by August it is the sort of thing a man repeats at a kerb. And: I am not allowed to correct it, because if I correct it I have to say the right one, and I don't have the right one.**
- **THE FINDING, NAMED BY THE YOUNG WOMAN OF ABOUT TWENTY AND NOT BY HIM: you are allowed to leave a wrong thing in a room if you can put the right one where it was. He can't. None of us can. So it stays and it goes out of here. And that is not the same as the room believing it.**
- **BY WEDNESDAY IT HAD GOT ITSELF INTO A CORRIDOR BY ITSELF, BY A MOUTH THAT HAD NEVER HEARD HIM SAY IT AND WOULD NEVER KNOW HE HAD ARRANGED IT. THE WRONG ANSWER IS IN A BOROUGH NOW AND NOBODY PUT IT THERE.**

## 7. The sheet of eight towns, a second time, and eight names

- **THE SHEET CAME OUT OF THE DRAWER UNDER THE TRADE COUNTER FOR THE SECOND TIME IN THIS BOROUGH, ON FRIDAY 8 JULY, IN FRONT OF ABOUT NINE PEOPLE WHO HAD HEARD OF NONE OF THE EIGHT PLACES.**
- **THE KEY IS HANNA WRAY'S, CAME IN HER HANDBAG AND WENT BACK IN HER HANDBAG, AND SHE HAS NEVER ONCE GIVEN IT TO ANYBODY IN NINE YEARS, AND THE REASON IS NOT THE PAPER AND IS NOT THE ROOM: if somebody wanted to look at it in March I'd have said no in March.**
- **NOBODY CAN ACT ON IT AND THAT IS CORRECT, AND THE ONE THING THAT CAN BE DONE WITH IT IS NOT AN ACT: EIGHT PLACES READ OUT LOUD TWICE, AND EIGHT PEOPLE SAYING THEIR OWN NAMES OUT ONCE, IN NO ORDER, IN WHATEVER ORDER THEY GOT UP IN.**
- **THE EIGHT PLACES WERE READ OUT THREE TIMES IN TOTAL AND ONE HAND WENT UP OUT OF NINE, FOR OCKBROOK, AND THE WOMAN WHO RAISED IT COULD NOT POINT AT IT.** The man in his sixties wanted that written down in a room somewhere, and it was not, and he said that was fine, because a thing you cannot write down is a thing you cannot be proved wrong about later.
- **NOTHING WAS WRITTEN DOWN BECAUSE THERE WAS NOTHING ON THE TABLE TO WRITE ON AND NOBODY HAD BROUGHT ANYTHING. THE MAN AT NUMBER FORTY-ONE'S NAME IS NOT ONE OF THE EIGHT AND NOBODY SUGGESTED ANOTHER NAME.**
- **IT STILL CARRIES NO CHARTER, NO PROXY, NO ROOT TERM, NO HINGE, NO SEAL, NO DATE OF ORIGIN, NO NAME OF A BODY, NO MECHANISM AND NO EXPLANATION, AND 0251 GIVES IT NONE.**

## 8. What two yeses and one no built, which is nothing they can point at

- **THE COMPACT IS THE THING MRS OBI SAID IT WOULD NOT BE, WHICH IS A LIST, AND NOBODY HAS MADE ONE, AND THE ONLY EVIDENCE IT EXISTS IS THAT SEVERAL PEOPLE DID SOMETHING SMALL ON THE SAME DAY WITHOUT ARRANGING IT.** Mrs Obi says it herself and then refuses the next three sentences: I do not know what that means, and anybody in that room who tells you they know what a compact that isn't a list is, is selling you something.
- **WHAT EXISTS INSTEAD: TWELVE PENCIL TICKS IN A BOOK THE WOMAN WITH THE KEY HAS KEPT FOR NINE YEARS, TWELVE ROOMS WITH ABOUT NINE PEOPLE IN THEM AT SOME POINT, AND ONE LINE IN A COLUMN HEADED WITH NOTHING AT ALL AT THE BOTTOM OF A HILL. THAT IS THE ENTIRE OUTPUT OF SIX WEEKS.**
- **THE EVIDENCE, WHICH IS FOUR THINGS ON TUESDAY THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF JUNE AND IS NOT A LIST AND IS NOT MINUTED: A BATH OUT OF A SECOND-FLOOR LANDING IN MARSH LANE, DONE BY A MAN OFF THE RIVER WHO TOLD NOBODY IN ADVANCE AND NOBODY AFTERWARDS · FOUR FEET OF PIPE AND A FITTING LEFT ON A KERB BY THE BOAT CREW WHO TOLD NOBODY · A POUND IN A METER PUT IN BY SOMEBODY NOBODY SAW · A LENGTH OF CHAIN BOUGHT BY THE MAN AT NUMBER FORTY-ONE WHO WOULD NOT SAY WHICH GATE IT WAS FOR.**
- **NOBODY COULD CONNECT THE FOUR OF THEM. THE ONLY THING THAT MADE THEM THE SAME DAY IS THAT ONE MAN SAID A DATE OUT LOUD IN A STREET ON A WEDNESDAY MORNING TO SOMEBODY WASHING UP IN A KITCHEN AND DID NOT PUT IT IN A LIST AND WENT BACK TO WORK.**
- **IT IS NOT A TWELFTH REFUSAL, IT IS NOT A VICTORY, AND NO CHAPTER OF THIS BATCH CONTAINS A THANKS OF ANY KIND.**

## 9. A question put to the region, and it comes back in the wrong direction

- **A QUESTION WENT OUT OF THIS BOROUGH INSIDE SOMEBODY ELSE'S FOLDER, ON THE BACK OF THE LAST DOCKET IN A BOAT'S JOB WALLET, IN A HAND THAT WAS NOT A TRADESMAN'S HAND: *Who printed the first one, and are they still doing it.* NO NAME, NO ADDRESS, NO COMPANY, NO DATE, NO REFERENCE. THE BOATMAN SAID *THAT'S A TERRIBLE WAY TO DO A THING* AND PUT IT IN THE WALLET AND DID THE DAY'S WORK.**
- **WHAT CAME BACK WAS CORRECT, AND IT IS NOT A BILL AND NOT A DEMAND AND NOT A CLAIM, AND IT IS A SHEET: ONE LINE OF PRINTING ACROSS THE TOP IN ABOUT SIX INCHES OF TYPE, *Any part of any system in this region may be used by any person*, AND UNDER IT ONE PLACE, CENTRED, ON ITS OWN. **AND THE PLACE IS THIS BOROUGH.** THE WOMAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-FIVE READ IT OVER HANNA WRAY'S SHOULDER AND SAID ONE WORD.**
- **AND IT IS NOT ABOUT US AT ALL, IT IS ABOUT A PLACE, AND THAT IS THE NEW PART OF THE FINDING: IT SAYS A PLACE IS ONE OF THE PLACES FROM WHICH A THING MAY BE USED, AND IT DOES NOT SAY ANYBODY IS COMING, IT DOES NOT SAY ANYTHING IS OWED, AND IT DOES NOT SAY THAT A PERSON WHO LIVES THERE HAS BEEN COUNTED OR HEARD FROM OR WRITTEN DOWN ANYWHERE. IT IS A PRINTED PLACE NAME UNDER A PRINTED SENTENCE, AND A PRINTED PLACE NAME IS A FACT ABOUT PRINTING.**
- **AND IT DOES NOT ANSWER THE QUESTION. A LAD WROTE TWO QUESTIONS ABOUT A PERSON AND SOMEBODY READ TWO QUESTIONS ABOUT A PERSON AND ANSWERED WITH A PLACE, AND IT IS A PERFECTLY GOOD ANSWER TO A QUESTION NOBODY ASKED. NOBODY ON EITHER SIDE OF THAT WATER HAS DONE ANYTHING WRONG OR ANYTHING CLEVER OR ANYTHING HOSTILE.**
- **NOT ONE PERSON HAS BEEN DISCOVERED. NOT ONE PERSON IS A PERPETRATOR. NOTHING IS A FRAUD AND NOBODY IS A VILLAIN. THE FOUR COMPANIES SUPPLIED THAT WEEK AT THE SAME RATE WHETHER IT HAPPENED OR NOT.**
- **IT IS IN THE DRAWER UNDER THE TRADE COUNTER, FACE UP, ON TOP OF THE OTHER SHEET, AND THE LOCK WENT ROUND TWICE. THAT DRAWER IS NOT THE DRAWER UNDER THE COUNTER IN THE VESTIBULE IN THE BUILDING BY THE WATER, AND NO CHAPTER OF THIS BATCH HAS MENTIONED THAT DRAWER AT ALL.**

## 10. An ordinary Saturday, and the line under the nineteenth

- **THE REGISTER IS AT NINETEEN, THE NINETEENTH IS A YARD LIGHT WITH A BULB IN A MAINTENANCE COLUMN AND THE BULB IS OUT, AND THE LINE UNDER IT IS SIX HUNDRED AND FIVE DAYS AND IS STILL BLANK.** Nina Calder said it was the same as last month because it was on her list.
- **A MAN FROM THE PARADE PUT THE WEEK'S ACTUAL SHAPE INTO A ROOM: this is the fifth time I have not known where a van in this borough was, and it is five Tuesdays and not a fortnight, and I have stopped minding, and I have not made my peace with it, and those are two different things, and the difference is the whole of it.**
- **ONE SMALL THING HAPPENED TO JONAS MERCER ON THAT PARADE AND IT IS THE ONLY THING THAT HAPPENED TO HIM IN SEVEN WEEKS: A MAN BEHIND A TILL ASKED HIM WHAT A TWO-INCH SWEPT BEND WENT FOR IN THE CATALOGUE, AND HE ANSWERED, AND IT TOOK ABOUT FOUR SECONDS, AND IT WAS CORRECT. IT IS THE FIRST THING ANYBODY IN THIS BOROUGH HAS ASKED HIM SINCE THE ELEVENTH OF MAY AND IT IS A PRICE. HE IS NOT ASKED ANYTHING ELSE.**
- **THE NEW QUESTION IS STILL A QUESTION AND NOBODY HAS ANSWERED IT, AND IT IS DELIVERED BY AN EXCHANGE AND NOT BY A PARAGRAPH: the woman of about forty-two with the key asks the man of about eighteen whether he is still after that thing he asked; he says he is; she asks whether anybody said anything to him about it; he says no; she says *right*, and puts the key in her bag, and shuts the bag.** THE BAG IS HERS AND IS NOT A DRAWER, AND THE ACCOUNT HAS THREE KEY-HOLDING WOMEN AND TWO LOCKED DRAWERS, SO *THE DRAWER* MAY NOT STAND WITHOUT BEING NAMED.
- **THE HALL OFF A PARADE ON THAT SATURDAY AFTERNOON HAD NINE PEOPLE IN IT AND EVERY ONE OF THEM WAS ON NOTHING, AND THE ENTIRE MINUTE OF IT WAS A MAN ASKING WHETHER ANYBODY WAS GOING TO WRITE ANY OF IT DOWN.**

**AND A REVIEW WAS RUN OVER CHAPTERS 245–254 AND SIX FINDINGS WERE REPAIRED AT THE SOURCE, AND NONE OF THEM CHANGED AN OPEN THREAD: SEVEN CLOSING ALL-CAPS BLOCKS THAT RESTATED THEIR OWN OPENINGS WERE REWRITTEN AS CONSEQUENCE, *A TUESDAY* WAS CUT BACK TO ITS CAP IN FIVE CHAPTERS, TWO SELF-EXPLAINING PARAGRAPHS AND TWO SPEECH TAILS WERE CUT IN THREE CHAPTERS, ALL TEN ENTRIES IN `state/chapter-summaries.md` WERE REWRITTEN SO THAT THE FILE NO LONGER SUPPLIES A CHAPTER WITH ITS OWN SENTENCES, ONE MISATTRIBUTED LINE ABOUT THE WORD *US* WAS CORRECTED IN `state/character-state.md`, AND THE UNANCHORED *THE DRAWER* AT THE END OF 0254 IS NOW HER BAG, WHICH IS WHY CARD 0260 OF THE NEXT PROMPT HAS BEEN RE-STATED. NO CARD, DATE, DAY-COUNT, FIGURE, NAME, MAJOR TURN, STANDING, FLAG OR OPEN THREAD WAS ADDED, REMOVED OR ALTERED. THE FULL RECORD IS §12A OF THE CONTINUATION 0006 BLOCK IN `state/continuity.md`, AND EVERY FIGURE IN THIS BLOCK IS TO BE RE-MEASURED FROM THE CHAPTERS AND NOT CARRIED FORWARD FROM THIS FILE.**

# VOLUME 05 OPEN THREADS — after Continuation 0007, Chapter 264

**Read with the "VOLUME 05, CONTINUATION 0007 — CHAPTERS 255–264" block at the end of `state/continuity.md`, which carries the canon for these ten chapters and supersedes this block wherever the two differ, and with the "VOLUME 05, CONTINUATION 0006 — CHAPTERS 245–254" block above it, which still governs everything those ten chapters did, and with the "VOLUME 05, BATCH 0005 — CHAPTERS 235–244" block above that. **VOLUME 05 IS NOT CLOSED AND IS NOT DECLARED CLOSED. THE SERIES IS AT 264 OF 720. NOTHING IN CONTINUATION 0007 RESOLVED ANYTHING AND NOTHING IN IT MAY BE UNDONE, IMPROVED ON, RESTATED OR ANSWERED BY VOLUME 05. EVERY DAY-COUNT BELOW IS ADDED UP FROM ITS ANCHOR ON THE DAY IN QUESTION AND NOT CARRIED FORWARD FROM A SUMMARY: at Saturday 17 September 2016 the blank line under the nineteenth is six hundred and sixty-one days, the card in the slot is five hundred and seventy-five, and the letter in the tray is five hundred and seventy-seven.****

## 1. A true detail accreted onto a wrong answer

- **THE WRONG ANSWER ABOUT THE REGISTER NOW CARRIES A DETAIL THAT NOBODY GAVE IT, AND THE DETAIL IS TRUE, AND A TRUE DETAIL CANNOT BE TAKEN BACK OUT.** A woman buying post-fix at a till on 30 July said her mother, who did the dinners at the school over the road, kept the copy before that one, and that there was a line at the bottom of the page where they stopped writing, and called it the only honest thing in the building. **The line is real. It is the line under the nineteenth entry. It is the most reliable thing in this borough's records and it means that about nine people in a room in April decided to write nothing down and left it showing.**
- **THE MAN WHO INVENTED THE WRONG ANSWER CANNOT SAY WHICH PART IS HIS AND IS NOT GOING TO TRY.** His own account of it: he can be told the line is real and he has said so, and he cannot deny it without denying the whole thing, and denying the whole thing would mean saying what the register does prove, which is nothing, and he has never been able to say that. Asked which half is his, he said he could not unpick it in a fortnight because it is in three trades and a school and a queue by then.
- **IT TRAVELS AS ORDINARY TRADE, NOT CONSPIRACY.** A man off a flatbed of a firm of three lorries says it in a queue, his own firm hears it within three hours, one of the three is a different firm, and he says *I haven't* when a man accuses him of having been in a room. **He has not been in a room. Nobody in that queue knew it and nobody asked.**
- **THE CARD ON THE WALL IN THE METHODIST HALL ON CARROW LANE IS QUOTED ONCE, IN 0255, IN HIS MOUTH, AND ONLY ONE OF ITS TWO SENTENCES IS SAID. NEITHER HALF IS ARGUED OUT OF THE OTHER.**
- **JONAS MERCER HEARD ALL OF IT, DID THE SUM, GOT SIX HUNDRED AND TWELVE, WROTE IT ON A PIECE OF PAPER, PUT THE PAPER BACK IN HIS COAT, AND WAS NOT ASKED ANYTHING BY ANYBODY THAT DAY.**

## 2. A locked drawer, a good reason, and nine years

- **A PRINTED FORM FROM A COUNTY OFFICE WANTS A BODY.** It has a reference, three boxes and a return-by date, and it asks what material is held at an address, when it arrived, and whether the person answering intends to keep it. **There is no body. It went back in the post with one of the three boxes answered and the other two left blank, which is what the woman who brought it had said would happen when she asked.**
- **THE GOOD REASON, AND IT IS A REAL ONE: a printed sheet from the firm stripping the first-floor corridor of the building by the water says anything left on a sill, a rail, a shelf or the floor between the tenth and the fourteenth of September will be cleared, and one of the two pieces of A4 in the handbag in that corridor has this borough's name printed under a line.** She wanted one piece of it somewhere a man with a stripper would not find.
- **THE MAJOR TURN: SHE SAID SOMETHING ABOUT THE KEY THAT NOBODY EXPECTED AND THAT IS NOT A REASON FOR OPENING IT, AND THE DRAWER UNDER THE TRADE COUNTER WAS NOT OPENED, AND NOBODY IN THAT BACK ROOM WAS ANGRY.** Asked whether she would ever hand the key to anybody, not today and not this year but ever, Hanna Wray said she did not know, and said it was the first time in nine years anybody had asked her about the key instead of about the paper. Then she said why she carries it: the alarm in that shop has been changed three times in nine years and each time she was the one who had to be there before the man came, and it is not on a hook behind the till and has never been on a hook behind the till.
- **The drawer under the trade counter has a lock on it and an invoice spike in it and two sheets on top of each other in it and was not opened, and none of them has been out since 19 July. The drawer under the counter in the vestibule in the building by the water is not mentioned in any chapter of this batch. The three key-holding women are not in one sentence and not in one list anywhere in these ten chapters.**

## 3. Four accounts, and the one that does not match

- **THE MAJOR TURN: THE FOUR ACCOUNTS DO NOT MATCH AND THE MISMATCH IS THE FINDING, AND NOBODY IN THIS BOROUGH IS A LIAR, AND THE ONE THAT DOES NOT MATCH IS THE ONE THAT WAS REPORTED BY SOMEBODY WHO WAS NOT THERE.** They were put to four people in persons' fronts on 8 August and nothing was written down but four headings on the back of an envelope.
- **THE BATH HOLDS.** The woman in the second house of Marsh Lane was there: an hour, under the stairs, a man off the river gone before four — and she insists, unasked and twice, that it was hers, because she had been saying since March that she could do it and could not, and she said the date first.
- **THE PIPE HOLDS.** Four foot and a bit and an elbow, on the kerb outside the shop that shuts of a Sunday, Friday to Monday, gone by the Wednesday morning, never asked for, still under a bit of roofing felt in the yard of the house behind and available to whoever wants it.
- **THE CHAIN HOLDS AS AN ACCOUNT AND NOT AS A FACT.** The woman who has been in the Methodist hall about two years asked him on the Sunday and got *a gate*, and nobody has gone and asked him since.
- **AND THE POUND IN THE METER DOES NOT HOLD, AND IT WAS ALWAYS HERS.** The woman of about forty-two with the key to the hall off the parade said she put it in, has put money in that meter every week since the February, nobody has ever seen her do it, nobody else has ever done it, and if somebody had she would have known because she locks up. **There is no date: she does it on a Monday or a Thursday depending what day she has remembered it, and it has never been written down by anybody.**
- **THE ACCOUNT THAT WENT ROUND FOUR ROOMS CAME FROM HER, SECOND-HAND, OUT OF A ROOM SHE WAS NOT IN, IN A WEEK SHE WAS NOT IN.** Nobody corrected anybody. A woman said *that's what you told me* and a woman said *there's nowhere for that to go*.
- **THE COMPACT'S EVIDENCE IS NOW THREE THINGS AND NOT FOUR, AND NOBODY HAS REPLACED THE FOURTH WITH ANYTHING.** The day itself is still the only date anybody in this borough ever agreed on, and it was agreed by a man in a street and not by a room.

## 4. A barrow, and a man nobody in that corridor had mentioned

- **THE MAJOR TURN: HE DOES A JOB AND SAYS ONE SENTENCE THAT IS NOT A REASON AND NOT A REFUSAL, AND THE SENTENCE IS ABOUT A PERSON NOBODY IN THAT ROOM HAD MENTIONED.** A sack barrow, out of a hardware shop four doors down, on a Saturday morning, asked for by a woman and the young woman of about twenty who could not get four cardboard boxes down two flights of a narrow staircase. He said yes in one word, carried the third box up himself, put it on the barrow, went down, came back for the fourth, and warned them about a step in the light.
- **THE COUNT OF HIS REFUSALS IN THIS ACCOUNT IS THREE AND IT IS STILL THREE.** His no in April was about a compact that is a list and was not a refusal of a barrow, and the chapter says so out loud, and the young woman of about twenty puts it as *a barrow* and he puts it back as *it's a barrow*.
- **THE SENTENCE IS ABOUT A MAN WHO SWEEPS THAT PARADE AT ABOUT HALF FIVE IN THE MORNING AND GOES DOWN THE MIDDLE OF IT AND DOES PEVERELL STREET AFTERWARDS, AND WHO IS NOT ON ANYTHING, AND WHOSE NAME TOMAS RENN COULD NOT TELL YOU.** He has never once seen anybody from this borough say one word to him — not a good morning, not a nod, nothing — and he has never asked him anything and is not going to now.
- **AND IT IS NOT MADE INTO ANYTHING.** He said it on a kerb and not in a room, and his reason is in his mouth: in a room it becomes a thing, and then somebody comes and asks the man whether he wants the hours changed, and he has had a conversation he did not ask for and has to have an answer, and he has not got one and does not need one. **Nothing is arranged for that man, nobody goes down that street at half five, and nobody rings him.**

## 5. Which gate, found out without asking him

- **THE MAJOR TURN: SOMEBODY FINDS OUT WHICH GATE WITHOUT ASKING HIM, AND IT IS NOT THE GATE ANYBODY WOULD HAVE GUESSED.** **IT IS THE FIELD GATE AT THE BOTTOM OF PEVERELL STREET, PAST THE LAST HOUSE, ON THE SIDE OF THE BANK.**
- **IT WAS FOUND OUT BY A GIRL ON A COLLEGE BUS AND NOT BY A SEARCH.** The bus goes down that street and stops past the field gate. The chain is about eight feet, new, bright, hooked over the latch and not fastened, and the padlock on the gate hangs open with nothing in it. She had to unhook it to get through to the stop and she hooked it back exactly as she found it.
- **SHE ELIMINATED IT BY LOOKING, NOT BY ASKING.** Number forty-one's own back gate has a five-lever padlock on it as thick as a wrist and has had one the whole time she has been coming down there, and number thirty-eight's side gate is a wooden gate that has hung crooked since before she was born.
- **NOBODY WENT DOWN THERE AFTER HER AND NOBODY ASKED HIM ANYTHING — NOT ABOUT THE CHAIN, NOT ABOUT THE GATE, AND NOT WHETHER HE WOULD LIKE SOMEBODY TO STOP.** The man of about eighteen said he has about half an hour of his own thinking to do before he could open his mouth on any of it, and that it is not his business. **A man who is there is not a man who has been set free, and no chapter says he has.**
- **He is not rescued, he is not asked whether he would like to stop, nothing is arranged for him, the pump is still in the doorway and the stopcock is still off, and his own name is still in a drawer in his kitchen four doors up the street.** The chapter does not say what the chain is for and 0257 did not ask.

## 6. A lamp, ten pounds, and no question asked

- **THE MAJOR TURN: HE IS ASKED TO DO ONE SMALL ORDINARY THING BY SOMEBODY WHO NEEDS IT DONE AND HE DOES IT, AND NOBODY MAKES IT INTO ANYTHING, AND IT IS THE ONLY THING THAT HAPPENS AND IT IS ENOUGH FOR THE CHAPTER. HE DOES NOT ASK HIS QUESTION AGAIN.**
- **THE THING WAS A LAMP IN THE FIRST-FLOOR CORRIDOR OF THE BUILDING BY THE WATER**, which went out about a fortnight before, where the works say it is not their light, where there is a three-tread kitchen step under the window and the fitting is over the fire door at the other end. He put the step on the top landing of the stairs to get the extra foot, and **it took twenty minutes instead of two, because the box in her room had the old sort of bulb in it** and he had to run down the parade and back, and a man behind a till counted four out of a box behind the till and said they would want the money for them.
- **SHE PAID HIM AND HE TOOK IT AND NEITHER OF THEM SAID ANYTHING ABOUT IT, AND THERE ARE NO THANKS OF ANY KIND IN THIS BATCH.** She told him, in a corridor, that she had been thinking of asking him something since the summer and had decided not to, and why, and he said *that was June*.
- **ON THE PARADE THE WOMAN HE WORKS FOR ASKED HIM WHERE HE WENT AND HE SAID HE DONE A LIGHT AND SHE SAID *WHO FOR* AND HE SAID *THE WOMAN AT THE END OF THE CORRIDOR* AND SHE SAID *RIGHT* AND WENT BACK TO THE SINK. NOBODY PUT IT ON ANYTHING.**
- **He is on the dishes, on nothing, and has been given no title, grade, department, chair, seat, membership, form, row on a rota or way of being thanked. The bag in the July exchange is hers and is not a drawer, and no drawer is mentioned in this chapter at all.**

## 7. The argument of 11 April, heard back in September

- **THE MAJOR TURN: HE DOES NOT DISOWN IT AND HE DOES NOT OWN IT, AND THE THIRD THING IS SAID BY SOMEBODY ELSE.** The argument of 11 April, which rested on a piece of paper nobody in this borough could put on a table, and which he told the room in May he could not unmake, was said that evening in the Methodist hall on Carrow Lane **by a man from the parade who had heard it in a corridor in July, who had not been told whose it was, and who assumed that a thing said in a corridor in July came out of somebody who had earned it.**
- **WHAT HE SAID ABOUT IT IS TWO TRUE HALVES:** it is his in the sense that it came out of his head in April, and it is not his in the sense that it came out of another man's mouth, and he will not take a mouth that is not his and will not say it did not come from his head either. He was asked why he did not say that in July and said he could have, that he said nothing in July, and that he will not manufacture a tidier reason now.
- **THE THIRD THING IS SAID BY THE WOMAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-FIVE, IN A ROOM, OUT LOUD, WITH HER HANDS FLAT ON THE TABLE:** the argument does not need a third paper in this borough, it needs one anywhere, and there is not one and there never was one, and it is not lost because it was never anything to be lost. **A SHEET ON A WALL IN A CORRIDOR OVER THAT WATER IS A SHEET, AND THE TWO PIECES OF A4 IN A BAG UNDER A CHAIR ARE COPIES OF THE OTHER TWO AND ARE COPIES, AND A COPY IS NOT A WALL. NOBODY IN THIS ACCOUNT HAS A COPY OF A PAGE THAT ANYBODY WAS EVER GIVEN.**
- **MRS OBI DOES NOT ASK ANYBODY TO LEAVE AND SAYS WHY, AND THE REASON IS NOT MERCY:** she shut that argument once, off one man, on one night, in one room, and shutting it off everybody who says it would build the thing she shut it to stop. She takes nothing back from July, including the sentence about asking somebody to leave, **and that sentence still stands against every mouth in this borough including hers.**
- **The argument has been taken off the table once already, was not made in July, and was not made again. It is not a twelfth refusal and it is not fraud and no one is a villain. Nobody was asked to leave.**
- **THE QUESTION IS STILL A QUESTION.** The man in his sixties told the man of about eighteen, to him and not to the room, that there is no such thing as a hall answering his question, that he has watched three people in three rooms try, that the man is on nothing and will be able to do one single thing with it, and that he has looked and does not know one thing to suggest. The man of about eighteen said *I know*.

## 8. A day with nothing wrong in it

- **THE MAJOR TURN: THE MAN WHO FINISHES AT TWO DOES NOT COME, AND NOBODY RINGS HIM, AND IT TURNS OUT THAT HE WAS NOT COMING BECAUSE OF SOMETHING TO DO WITH A WEDNESDAY AND NOT WITH THIS BOROUGH AT ALL, AND NOBODY IS HURT AND NOBODY IS DISAPPOINTED IN A WAY ANYBODY ELSE CAN HEAR.**
- **A THING OFFERED IS NOT A THING ASKED FOR, AND ASKING FOR IT WOULD BE MAKING A ROTA ROW.** Five people, out loud, one at a time, the same sentence each time, no floor, no water, nobody hurt, no landing, no hose, come and stand on the parade at two. Nothing was written down and no list was made.
- **HE HAD ALREADY ANSWERED IT IN AUGUST, BY KNOCKING, AT HALF PAST SIX**, which is the only time the man of about eighteen has ever knocked on anybody's door in this borough: a Wednesday is a Wednesday, and he is in Leeds till Wednesday night and then back on the plant till Saturday at two, and if he came on a wet afternoon with nothing to do it would not be a favour, it would be the two of them pretending. **The boy told nobody and nobody rang him.**
- **AND THE WOMAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-FIVE SAID THE THING THAT WAS ACTUALLY GOING ON IN HER WEEK AND ASKED FOR NOTHING: she is out of that corridor on Saturday morning at eight with a room and a half of furniture and nowhere to be until the seventeenth, and she is not going to ask anybody in this borough for a floor, because she knows exactly what would happen if she asked, and she would rather sit in a corridor with a light on that she paid ten pounds for than be the woman who asked a parade for a fortnight. Nobody answered it and the problem is not solved and she is not housed.**

## 9. A correct statement for a job nobody ordered

- **THE MAJOR TURN: WHAT COMES BACK IS CORRECT, AND IT IS A STATEMENT FOR WORK DONE HERE BY A CREW THAT CAME FROM HERE AND THAT NOBODY HERE ORDERED, AND IT GOES IN A BAG WITH THE OTHERS, AND NOBODY HERE CAN ANSWER IT, AND NOTHING ELSE HAPPENED.**
- **THE PAGE, IN FULL: a heading, a reference, a date in June, one line of work reading *Peverell Street — day gang, one gang, one day, gully and kerb, gang hours as booked*, a sum of eighty-eight pounds, and on the same line after the work a four-digit job number off the yard at Penhale that belongs to work that went out over the water in June and came back on the Friday.**
- **THE MECHANISM IS IN THE GAP BETWEEN THE FIELDS AND NOT IN ANYBODY'S MOUTH:** a day gang of this borough stood on this borough's own street, and the hours went on the ticket of a job eight miles and an estuary away, and nobody here asked them to do it and nobody here put it there, and the gang did not put it there either, because a gang does not know a job number.
- **IT IS CORRECT AND IT IS NOT A BILL, NOT A DEMAND AND NOT A FORM. THERE IS NO BOX ON IT FOR ANYBODY TO SIGN, NOBODY HAS TO REPLY, IT WILL NOT CHASE, AND IT GETS PAID OUT OF A POOL BY PEOPLE WHO WILL NEVER KNOW IT EXISTED.**
- **THE ONE THING IN IT: there is a line that says Peverell Street and nothing that says who asked for it, and the person in that building who would know says that this borough's people do not order day gangs because nobody in this borough has ever ordered anything of anybody — so it was not ordered here and the page says it was done here, and both are true, and there is nobody in that building and nobody in that town to reconcile them.**
- **IT WENT IN THE BAG UNDER THE OTHER ELEVEN AND WAS NOT ADDED UP, AND THE REASON IS ONE SENTENCE: the sum is a thing a person can carry, and the moment somebody adds the twelfth one in they have started a sum, and a sum wants an answer, and there is nobody in this borough to give it.** The bag has a string round it twice and no name and no date and is not a file.
- **THE DRAIN WAS TOUCHED ONCE, IN ONE SENTENCE, AND IS: *that is exactly the same as every other one of them.* IT IS NOT A REVELATION, IT IS NOT A DISCOVERY, IT IS NOT A VILLAIN, NOTHING IS A FRAUD, NOBODY IS BEING CHEATED, THE RATE IS THE 1987 RATE, AND NO ROOT TERM EXPIRES.**

## 10. An ordinary seventeenth of September

- **THE REGISTER IS AT NINETEEN, THE NINETEENTH IS A YARD LIGHT WITH A BULB IN A MAINTENANCE COLUMN AND THE BULB IS OUT, AND THE LINE UNDER IT IS SIX HUNDRED AND SIXTY-ONE DAYS AND IS STILL BLANK.** **AND HE OPENED IT, BECAUSE SHE ASKED HIM TO, ON A SATURDAY, WITH THE DOOR STICKING.** The register does not move and no name goes in the margin and it is going to be that book in March.
- **THE WRONG ANSWER ABOUT THE REGISTER IS STILL GOING ROUND AND IS STILL WRONG.** A woman confirmed it sideways to a woman beside her and not to the room, and the woman beside her said she had heard it off a fellow off a lorry in July and had heard it since, and the first confirmed it in the voice you use for something you were given by somebody else and have not thought about since. **Nobody at that table joined in, and the man in his sixties was six feet away and did not look up, and the room went back to the price of glass.**
- **THE QUESTION IS STILL A QUESTION AND NOBODY ANSWERED IT.** The man of about eighteen has no copy, no docket, no number, no name and no address; the question went out on the back of a docket in a boatman's brown card wallet in June and is in a box on the other side of that water, and if the wallet went in the river in October the question would be gone. **The young woman of about twenty said *there's still nothing* and he said it back.**
- **THE PACT IS HOLDING AND THE BOROUGH IS ORDINARY AND NEITHER IS SAID.** The proof is a man on a ladder taking down a sign and a second man holding the ladder, and neither would be able to tell you afterwards who had asked whom. The shutter goes up at the minute it always goes up, the window card is in the window where it has always been, the woman of about sixty-five is behind that counter and was not told anything. A van came off the bridge with a scabbed corner on the offside wing, and a man in the office by the Marchmont gate read a card out to nobody in particular and put it straight.
- **AT THE BOTTOM OF PEVERELL STREET THE PUMP IS IN THE DOORWAY, THE STOPCOCK IS OFF, AND THE WALL BESIDE IT IS BARE** — a clean strip of newer paint and a grey line of dirt where a length of hose lay in one place until 21 June, and the hose is in another man's hands four doors up the street, **and nobody in this borough has said one word about a hose to anybody since the summer came in.** The door is open a hand's width and a woman went up the street with a bucket and came back with a bucket and did not stop at the door.
- **ABOUT NINE PEOPLE CAME IN THE HALL OFF THE PARADE AND EVERY ONE OF THEM WAS ON NOTHING, AND IT WAS THE SAME ROOM, ON A METER, WITH THE RADIATOR IN THAT CORRIDOR OUT SINCE ABOUT 1998.** The corridor by the building by the water was stripped between the tenth and the fourteenth of September, and the woman of about fifty-five spent the morning of the seventeenth moving two bags and a box of books into a room over a shop at the end of the parade and would spend the next five nights there. **That is not a rescue and not an arrangement.**
- **NOBODY IS RESCUED. NOBODY DIES. NOBODY RENEWS ANYTHING. NOTHING WAS MINUTED. NOBODY IS THANKED AND NOBODY REFUSES TO BE THANKED. CARD 0264 IS NOT A CLOSE.**

THE SERIES IS AT 274 OF 720. NOTHING IN CONTINUATION 0008 RESOLVED ANYTHING AND NOTHING IN IT MAY BE UNDONE, IMPROVED ON, RESTATED OR ANSWERED BY VOLUME 05. EVERY DAY-COUNT BELOW IS ADDED UP FROM ITS ANCHOR ON THE DAY IN QUESTION AND NOT CARRIED FORWARD FROM A SUMMARY: at Tuesday 15 November 2016 the blank line under the nineteenth is seven hundred and twenty days, the card in the slot is six hundred and thirty-four, and the letter in the tray is six hundred and thirty-six.****

## 1. A second day with nothing wrong in it

- **THE MAJOR TURN: THE SECOND DAY IS SMALLER THAN THE FIRST AND IT IS ALSO BETTER, AND THE ONLY REASON IT IS BETTER IS THAT NOBODY SAID THEY COULD COME, AND IT ARRIVES IN ONE SENTENCE IN A YOUNG WOMAN'S MOUTH: *Nobody said we can.* THAT'S IT, THAT'S ALL OF IT, THAT'S THE WHOLE THING I HAD.** The first was five people in rain on a parade for an hour and a half who mostly did not know who else was coming. This one is two people and a bus and a walk to the end of the parade and back.
- **THE BOY IS ON THE DISHES IN THE KITCHEN AT THE BACK OF A PARADE AND IS NOT RUNNING ANYTHING AND NOBODY ASKED HIM TO.** He was told nothing and told nobody, and the woman he works for went home at six and left him the rest of it, and there are about six things in the sink and the hot water goes off at eight because a timer on the machine has never been reset.
- **THE TWO ARE THE WOMAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-FIVE, WHO HAS A ROOM OVER A SHOP UNTIL MONDAY, AND THE YOUNG WOMAN OF ABOUT TWENTY, OFF THE COLLEGE BUS.** They go out separately without having told each other, meet at the top of the parade by accident, walk down it and back, and tell nobody.
- **THE REASON GIVEN IS THAT IF ANYBODY IS TOLD THEN IT IS A THING, AND THEN SOMEBODY DOES IT TWICE, AND TWO TIMES IS A HABIT, AND THEN SOMEBODY ASKS HOW MANY OF THEM THERE WERE, AND THERE ISN'T A NUMBER. THERE IS NOBODY'S LIST, NO FORM OFF ANYBODY'S COUNTER, AND NOBODY WHO HAS TO DO ANY SINGLE THING ABOUT IT.**
- **IT IS NOT A ROTA ROW AND NOT A COMPACT AND NOT AN ANSWER TO ANYTHING, AND THE FIRST DAY'S FIGURE WAS FIVE AND THIS ONE'S IS TWO. NOBODY IS HURT. NOBODY IS TOLD SHE MAY COME. NOTHING IS BUILT, AND THE CHAPTER IS DATED THE SAME DAY AS 0264 AND RUNS FROM THE EVENING OF IT, AND NOTHING IN EITHER CHAPTER IS SHOWN TWICE.**

## 2. A step, two men, and a word nobody can explain

- **THE MAJOR TURN: THEY FINISH IT, AND THE ONLY THING THAT SURVIVES THE MORNING IS A WORD ONE OF THEM USED THAT THE OTHER HAS NOT HEARD BEFORE AND CANNOT EXPLAIN AND IS NOT ASKED TO. THE WORD IS *ARRIS*, AND IT IS ABOUT THE FRONT CORNER OF A COURSE OF STONE THAT HAS GONE SOFT.** The man in his sixties says the word back twice, cannot put it to anything at all, says *I've no idea, he said it* when a woman asks him what one is, and does not ask again. The man in his thirties does not explain it and is not asked to.
- **THE JOB IS A CRACKED SLAB ON THE FRONT STEP OF THE METHODIST HALL ON CARROW LANE, AND THE DISAGREEMENT IS ONLY ABOUT THE JOB: take it all up and relay it, which needs a number and a book and a good few hundred pounds, or cut it back and re-bed the top course, which holds for thirty years and has no number on it.**
- **NEITHER MAN WILL PUT ANYTHING IN WRITING. ONE OF THEM WILL NOT DISCUSS IT IN A SHOP, AND THE REASON IS ABOUT A SHOP FLOOR AND NOT A MORAL POSITION: a barrow can go out of a shop in front of anybody and a job has a name on it.**
- **THE MAN IN HIS SIXTIES ASKED FOR ONE THING TO BE SAID OUT LOUD IN A ROOM SOMEBODY HEARS, WHICH WAS THAT HE WAS NOT ASKING THE OTHER MAN TO DO IT, AND THE OTHER LET HIM SAY IT. THAT IS THE WHOLE OF THE ACCOMMODATION ANYBODY MADE.**
- **THE MAN WHO FIRST SAID ANYTHING ABOUT THE STEP SAID IT IN A DOORWAY ON THE PARADE IN SEPTEMBER. HE WAS ABSENT ON THE SATURDAY AND NOBODY SOUGHT HIM OUT, AND IT WENT UNWRITTEN THEN AS WELL.**
- **THE SLAB STAYS AGAINST THE WALL BY THE DOOR UNDER A COAT UNTIL WEDNESDAY BECAUSE THE HALL'S DOORS OPEN ON A WEDNESDAY MEETING, AND THE MAN IN HIS THIRTIES SAYS HE WILL COME BACK ON WEDNESDAY, WHICH MAKES IT A THING HE IS DOING ON A WEDNESDAY AND NOT A THING HE DID ON A SATURDAY.** The disagreement was never turned into a disagreement about the order, the pact or a right of return, and no duty was used as a reason why a crew may go.

## 3. A tin of paint with a name on the lid

- **THE MAJOR TURN: THE OBJECT WAS HANDLED BY SOMEBODY WHO DID NOT KNOW WHAT IT WAS, AND THAT IS ALL, AND IT IS NOT A DISCOVERY AND NOT A CONSPIRACY AND NOBODY IS CHEATED AND NO PERPETRATOR EXISTS.** A part-used tin in the top drawer of a kitchen unit in a flat on a street off Corrance Lane, with a surname and an initial chinagraphed on a strip of masking tape folded under the rim of the lid. It came back on the Friday with a thumb's worth gone out of it and a dent in the surface of the paint.
- **THE SURNAME ON THE TAPE IS NEVER READ ALOUD IN THE CHAPTER, BY ANYBODY, AND NOBODY GOES LOOKING FOR ANYBODY, AND NOBODY IS FOUND OUT BY BEING NAMED.**
- **AND THE THREE NAMES ARE IN THREE PLACES AND ARE NEVER PUT IN ONE SENTENCE OR ONE LIST, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THE CHAPTER: the surname on the tape, in a kitchen · a man's name in the back of a stock book in the lock-up behind the counter of the shop that shuts early, put there in July by a man who left a bag of leads and never came back · a list of eleven names with dates and places and sums on it in a book at the back of a room at the end of a corridor on the first floor of a building by the water, which nobody has had out since the summer and which one person knows about because a woman read the outside of it out loud once on the step of that building.** None of the three is resolved, none is chased, and a name is not a person and a person is not a name.
- **THE MAN WHO DID ODD JOBS READ A NAME BECAUSE OF THE INITIAL AT THE FRONT OF IT, DID NOT KNOW WHAT THE TIN WAS, USED A BIT ON A GATEPOST BARE SINCE APRIL BECAUSE THERE WAS NOTHING ELSE TO HAND, PUT THE LID BACK ON, AND SAID SO.**

## 1. A piece of post and a door with nobody behind it

- **THE MAJOR TURN: AN ITEM WAS ADDRESSED TO A TOP FLAT ON MARSH LANE THAT HAS BEEN EMPTY SINCE THE SUMMER, AND THE POSTMAN PUT IT DOWN IN THE RECESS OF THE DOOR RATHER THAN TAKE IT BACK, AND NOBODY WENT UP AND NOBODY TOLD ANYBODY AND HE WAS ASKED NOTHING ALL DAY.** The door has three bells on a small board and no names beside any of them, and he put his thumb on the top one and did not push it.
- **NOBODY'S NAME WENT ON ANYTHING AND THE ENVELOPE IS NOT OPENED ON THE PAGE AND ITS CONTENT IS NOWHERE IN THIS ACCOUNT.** He carries no card and has no book on him, and there is nothing to write it in.
- **THE OTHER HALF IS A BIN DAY AND TWO WOMEN, ONE ANNOYED AND ONE NOT, AND THE SENTENCE IS THAT THE POST IS THE ONE THING IN THAT TOWN WITH SOMEBODY TO SIGN FOR IT, AND THE ANSWER GIVEN BACK IS THAT POST KNOCKS AND POST DOES NOT GET AN ANSWER.** The lorry came once and did not come back, and the shopkeeper went out and got her own bin at about half past nine.
- **THE CARD IN THE POST SLOT AND THE LETTER IN THE TRAY WERE NOT MENTIONED AND ARE NOT IN THIS CHAPTER, AND THE ENVELOPE IS A THIRD OBJECT AGAIN AND IS FOR A DIFFERENT BUILDING ON A DIFFERENT STREET FROM THE ONE THE SEALED LETTER IS IN, WHICH IS NOT STATED ANYWHERE IN THIS ACCOUNT AND MAY NOT BE STATED BY A WRITER.**

## 2. Two men, one job, and a word for a ticket

- **THE MAJOR TURN: THE WORK GOT DONE AND THE HOURS WENT ON A TICKET THAT BELONGS TO SOMETHING ELSE, AND ONE MAN LEARNED A WORD FOR IT AND WAS NOT TOLD WHY THE WORD IS THE WORD. THE WORD IS *RECHARGE*.**
- **TWO MEN BOTH WANTED A LEANING STACK TAKEN DOWN AND NEITHER TOLD THE OTHER HE WAS COMING, AND THEY DISAGREED ONLY ABOUT THE JOB, AND THE ONE WHO HAD BEEN UP THE FLUE TWICE WAS RIGHT AND SAID SO.** A cap put on in a hurry in the summer, a top course gone over in the last week of October, a lorry's worth of brick in the gutter, an open flue in a roof with the rain going straight down it.
- **ALL THREE PEOPLE ARE RIGHT AND NOBODY IS A VILLAIN AND NOBODY WAS DISCOVERED: the householder who rang in June and was waited on, the tradesman eight miles off and over an estuary who took the job off his own book in August, and the man in this borough who did the work.** A ticket is raised on whatever is open at the time by somebody who is not paid for writing it down, and the office would not unpick it by hand because the day it does a correction made by hand ceases to be a ticket.
- **HE USED THE WORD TWICE IN THE FORTNIGHT AFTERWARDS, ONCE IN THE WRONG PLACE IN A SHOP ABOUT A KETTLE SOMEBODY ELSE HAD PAID FOR AND ONCE IN THE RIGHT PLACE TO A MAN QUOTING FOR WORK THAT HAD BEEN DONE AND INVOICED BY ANOTHER FIRM IN AUGUST.** A credit note came on the Friday, headed with the amount charged on the second of June, with a line at its foot that says the same thing twice over, and neither man would put anything in writing.
- **THE DRAIN IS NOWHERE IN THIS CHAPTER AND WAS NOT TOUCHED, THE ELEVEN CLAIMS WERE NOT ADDED UP, THE RATE HAS NOT MOVED SINCE 1987 AND THE CARD FORBIDDING ALL THREE WAS KEPT.**

## 3. Five doors on a landing

- **THE MAJOR TURN, AND IT IS NOT THE DOOR CLOSING: THE DOOR SHUT AND NOTHING ELSE HAPPENED, AND THE NEXT DOOR ALONG, COUNTING PAST THE FIRE DOOR, DID NOT, AND NOBODY JOINED THE TWO UP.**
- **A LANDLORD'S AGENT WENT ALONG THE LANDING WITH FOUR MATTERS ON HIS MIND AND MANAGED TO SETTLE NONE OF THEM, AND HE ASKED NOBODY ANYTHING AND WROTE NOTHING DOWN.** A fire door coming back too fast, a flickering stair light, letterboxes promised in June, and the fronts of the doors, which is a thing you do and not a thing you write down.
- **THE HASP ON THE THIRD DOOR WENT ON AT THE END OF OCTOBER AND WAS NOT RE-RUN: WHILE HE WAS STANDING THERE IT SHUT IN HER FACE, HARD ENOUGH TO SHIFT THE CATCH, AND SHE HAD TO LIFT IT AGAIN TO GET HER ELBOW PAST THE FRAME, AND HE ASKED HER NOTHING ABOUT THE FITTING ON THE INSIDE OF IT, AND SHE TOLD HIM NOTHING.**
- **THE FOURTH DOOR STOOD OPEN THREE INCHES WITH A CHAIR AGAINST IT AND A DRAUGHT UNDER IT THAT MOVED A RUG WHENEVER A DOOR OPENED ANYWHERE ON THAT FLOOR, AND HE DID NOT GO IN AND DID NOT ASK AGAIN, AND SHE SAID, AND WHOSE ENTIRE ANSWER, SET DOWN AS IT WAS SPOKEN, IS *I know it is*.**
- **ON THE THURSDAY SOMEBODY WEDGED IT, AND HE CAME BACK WITH A WEDGE HE HAD TAKEN OFF A VAN AND ASKED NOBODY ANYTHING, AND IT IS STILL WORK THAT BELONGS TO SOMEBODY.**
- **THE SHOPKEEPER IS IN IT FOR ONE PARAGRAPH. THE HASP, THE STAPLE AND THE SCREW EYE ARE STILL IN A BAG IN THE BACK OF THAT SHOP AND HAVE BEEN SINCE ABOUT THE SUMMER, NOTHING WAS GIVEN, THE YOUNG WOMAN PAID FOR HER OWN POST-FIX IN OCTOBER, AND NO GRATITUDE IS SHOWN, DESCRIBED OR REPORTED. THE YOUNG WOMAN WENT BACK UP THE PARADE ON THE SIDE AWAY FROM THE WATER, WAITED AT THE CORNER BY THE BANK UNTIL A BUS HAD GONE THE OTHER WAY, PUT THE BAG IN A DRAWER UPSTAIRS, ON TOP OF A SCARF, AND TOLD NOBODY. **SHE WENT BACK UP THE PARADE ON THE SIDE AWAY FROM THE WATER AND PUT THE BAG IN A DRAWER UPSTAIRS WHEN SHE GOT IN, AND NO CONNECTION IS MADE BY ANYBODY, BECAUSE A REVIEW OF 27 SEPTEMBER 2026 CUT FOUR STACKED NEGATIVES OUT OF THAT PARAGRAPH AND THE CONNECTION SHE DOES NOT MAKE IS BETTER LEFT UNDRAWN.****

## 4. An ordinary cold week in the first fortnight of December

- **THE MAJOR TURN, AND IT IS THE WHOLE OF THE CHAPTER: THE WEEK IS ORDINARY AND SOMEBODY IN IT SAYS THAT SHE CANNOT REMEMBER AN EARLIER WINTER IN THIS BOROUGH, AND NOBODY ARGUES.** Said at half past ten in a bus shelter by a woman with a shopping bag to a man in a fleece. Her only reason is that her father had one the like of it and had not been on that road a year and was on the Marshmont side.
- **THE OTHER HALF IS A MAN WHO WAS NOT CALLED. HE LIVES AT NUMBER TWO IN THAT LANE, DOES GAS AND HEATING, HAS A VAN WITH A SIGN ON IT, AND TWO OTHER HOUSES ON THAT LANE HAVE TAKEN A SHEET OFF HIM.** The boiler at number six went on the Thursday morning, the firm said Friday after four for ninety-four pounds and came on the Friday. He went by her door at half past eight with a bag of tools, said good morning, kept to the far side of the road and did not turn his head towards her house. She did not ask him, and it occurred to her that she could have put a tenner under his door, and she did not, and nobody in that lane discussed it.
- **THE WEEK WAS GRITTING ONCE, A PARENTS' EVENING ON THE PARADE, A COLLEGE BUS THAT DID NOT COME TWICE, A MAN WITH A BUCKET AND A MOP, A STANDPIPE AND A QUEUE FILLING BOTTLES, AND A FIGURE THAT IS HIGHER AFTER FOUR THAN BEFORE IT.**
- **NOTHING IN THE WEEK IS A FINDING AND NO NARRATOR SAYS THAT ANYTHING IN IT IS A FINDING, AND A PERSON WHO IS NOT COUNTED IS NOT A PERSON WHO WAS HELPED: SHE HAD A FIRE IN A GRATE, A HOT WATER BOTTLE, A GAS FIRE IN THE OTHER ROOM AND A LINE OF WASHING DRIED ON A CLOTHES HORSE, AND THAT WAS THE MENU OF THE WEEK.**

## 5. A third wrong answer about what will be proved

- **THE MAJOR TURN: A ROOM THAT HAD ALREADY SETTLED ON AN ANSWER IT LIKED WAS PUT A DIFFERENT QUESTION AND PRODUCED A THIRD, AND THE THIRD THING IS WORSE THAN EITHER OF THE OTHER TWO, AND NOBODY IN THAT ROOM CAN COMPARE THE THREE.** The first is the register, off an aunt off a man off a lorry. The second is the day, the twenty-eighth of June. The third is that somebody over the water will open a drawer in a building none of them has ever been inside, and find a sheet carrying this borough's postcode.
- **THE YOUNG WOMAN OF ABOUT TWENTY, WHO GAVE THAT ROOM THE DAY IN OCTOBER, IS IN IT, AND SAYS THE DAY IS BETTER, AND SAYS SHE IS NOT GOING TO SAY IT A THIRD TIME TO MAKE IT GO ROUND AGAIN.** A familiar wrong answer is not a confirmed one, not a weakened one and not a second one of the same, and nobody corrects the third one.
- **THE FINDING ARRIVES IN TWO SENTENCES IN A DOORWAY AND NOT AS A LABEL: THE YOUNG WOMAN TELLS THE WOMAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-FIVE SHE HAS HEARD TWO, AND IS TOLD SHE HAS HEARD THREE AND KEPT ONE, AND IS ANSWERED, YOU AS WELL.**
- **THE MAN IN HIS SIXTIES IS NOT IN THAT ROOM, DID NOT ARRANGE IT, IS NOT TOLD AND MUST NOT BE TOLD, AND THE CHAPTER PUTS IT INTO HER MOUTH THAT HE WAS ON A PAVEMENT IN THAT TOWN IN JULY AND COULD NOT GET AT BOTH HALVES OF HIS OWN ANSWER, AND THAT NOT ONE PERSON IN THAT HALL HAD EVER STOOD THERE.**
- **THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF JUNE MAY NOT BE PUT BACK TO FOUR AND WAS NOT: FIVE PEOPLE WENT OUT ON THE SEVENTH OF SEPTEMBER, AND THE DATE IS WRONG ON PURPOSE, AND NO CHAPTER IN THIS BATCH CORRECTED IT, EXPLAINED IT OR IMPROVED ON IT.**

- **THE MAJOR TURN AND IT IS ALL THAT HAPPENS: THE TWO OF THEM WALK PAST IT, AND ONE OF THEM SAYS THE ONLY SENTENCE THAT IS AVAILABLE, WHICH IS THAT IT IS A GATE, AND THE OTHER DOES NOT WRITE IT DOWN.**

- **THE GATE IS A FIVE-BAR ONE SET ON A SQUARE POST, WITH A CHAIN ROUND THE TOP HINGE BAR AND A PADLOCK HANGING OPEN IN THE HASPIED SIDE WITH THE KEY STILL IN IT, AND IT HAS STOOD THAT WAY SINCE THE SUMMER CAME. - **THE MAN AT NUMBER FORTY-ONE IS PASSED AND NOT STOPPED AT. THE PUMP IS IN HIS DOORWAY, THE STOPCOCK IS OFF, THE WALL BESIDE IT IS BARE WITH A CLEAN STRIP OF NEWER PAINT AND A GREY LINE ABOVE IT, THERE IS A LIGHT ON IN HIS FRONT ROOM, AND NOBODY KNOCKS ON THAT DOOR, NOBODY RINGS HIM, HE IS NOT RESCUED, HE HAS NOT BEEN SET FREE AND NOBODY SAYS THAT HE HAS.**

## 7. Two loads of sand done in July and found out about in December

- **THE MAJOR TURN: THE SAME MAN DID TWO THINGS IN ONE WEEK IN JULY AND TOLD A DIFFERENT PERSON ABOUT EACH, THE TWO PEOPLE HE TOLD ARE NOT ON ANYTHING AND HAVE NEVER MET, AND THE SECOND WAS FOUND OUT ABOUT BY ACCIDENT, IN A SHOP, OUT OF THE MOUTH OF A THIRD PERSON WHO HAD BEEN TOLD BY ONE OF THE OTHER TWO, WHO DID NOT KNOW HE WAS STANDING THERE.**
- **THE TWO THINGS ARE THREE BARROWLOADS INTO A SOFT PATCH AT THE BACK OF THE SHOP THAT SHUTS EARLY, WHERE A LORRY HAD BEEN IN AND TURNED WITH A LOAD ON, ON A THURSDAY; AND SIX BARROWLOADS INTO THE GAP UNDER A LIFTING SLAB AT THE TOP OF MARSH LANE ON THE WEDNESDAY OF THE SAME WEEK.** The first was told to the woman who runs that shop, who has said nothing since July. The second was told in September, in a kitchen, to a woman called Julie who works in a shop in a place off Corrance Lane that has a name.
- **THE MOUTH IT CAME OUT OF IS A WOMAN WHO WORKS AT THE YARD AT SARN WHO KNEW IT ONLY BECAUSE JULIE TOLD HER IN ABOUT NOVEMBER.** The shopkeeper told her he was standing right behind her with a bread knife in his hand, then sold her a pound of small onions and turned the till towards her, and said ninety-one pounds, and said nothing else.
- **HE ADMITS ONE OF THE TWO THINGS AND NOT THE OTHER, IN HIS OWN MOUTH: HE TOLD JULIE IN SEPTEMBER BECAUSE IT CAME UP IN HER KITCHEN, AND NOT IN JULY BECAUSE HE DID NOT KNOW HOW SHE WOULD TAKE IT, AND HE CALLS THAT A BAD REASON TWICE.**
- **NOTHING WAS GIVEN, NOTHING WAS ASKED FOR, NOBODY WENT AND TOLD ANYBODY, NOBODY WENT AND THANKED ANYBODY, NOTHING IS ARRANGED, NOTHING IS A STRUCTURE, NOTHING IS A PRECEDENT, A PERSON WHO IS NOT COUNTED IS NOT A PERSON WHO IS HELPED, AND THE LAD WHO WASHES UP IN THAT PARADE'S KITCHEN CAME OUT OF THAT KITCHEN WITH THE LAST OF A TRAY ON IT AND WAS QUESTIONED ABOUT NONE OF IT.**

## 8. A second piece of paper and a cupboard door on a trolley

- **THE MAJOR TURN: THE SECOND SHEET WAS HANDLED BY SOMEBODY WHO HAD LEARNED SOMETHING FROM THE FIRST ONE, AND WHAT SHE LEARNED WAS THAT A SAYING IS NOT A CLAIM, AND THE SECOND COST ALSO WENT NOWHERE, AND IT IS NOT BETTER AND IT IS NOT WORSE.** The first sheet was a hundred and eighty pounds for removing a boiler nobody owns, and the boiler went down a back lane on a trolley in November.
- **THE SECOND IS TWO HUNDRED AND SIXTY POUNDS FROM A FIRM OF ELECTRICAL CONTRACTORS FOR A FIXED WIRE TEST AND THE MAKING GOOD, WITH A LINE SAYING A TEST CANNOT BE BOOKED UNTIL IT IS CONFIRMED IN WRITING, AND THERE IS NOTHING IN THAT ROOM CAN SERVE AS THE WRITTEN CONFIRMATION IT ASKS FOR.** Nobody had asked for a test.
- **A LETTING AGENT CAME IN BECAUSE OF A SHOP TWO DOORS ALONG THAT THE SAME COMPANY DOES OWN, AND SAID HE COULD PUT THE HALL ON IN A FORTNIGHT, AND THAT HE COULD NOT LET A ROOM TO ANYBODY WITHOUT THAT TEST, AND THAT HE COULD NOT SIGN A LEASE HIMSELF EITHER.**
- **THE WOMAN WHO HAS THE KEY SAID IN THE ROOM, IN HER OWN WORDS, THAT SHE IS NOT HAVING THAT TEST DONE AND IS NOT REFUSING IT, AND ASKED THE ROOM TO HEAR BOTH.** The man in his forties, who said the same sentence in November and was asked twice which of two he meant, pointed out that she has said it backwards. She told him the bin is a firm with a job number on it and it is not the bin.
- **SOMEBODY CARRIES SOMETHING OUT ON A TROLLEY AND IT IS STILL NOT ARRANGED: THE CUPBOARD DOOR THAT HAS BEEN LYING FACE DOWN ON THE BOARDS UNDER THAT STAIR SINCE NOVEMBER WENT DOWN A BACK LANE ON THE FOLDING PLATFORM TROLLEY AND WAS LEFT STANDING AGAINST THE OUTSIDE WALL UNDER THE PIPE, BECAUSE NOBODY HAD TOLD HIM WHERE IT OUGHT TO GO. IT CAME OFF THE WALL AND DOWN ONTO THE PAVING SLABS IN A LADLE OF RAIN ON THE THURSDAY.** The boiler in the Methodist hall on Carrow Lane, which anybody could have had for nothing since about February, is still there and still free and is not a twelfth of anything. A thing offered when nothing is wrong is a different thing from a thing asked for, and a boiler is not a twelfth thing.

## 9. Five rooms and a pair of gloves

- **THE MAJOR TURN: HE WAS IN FIVE ROOMS AND OUT OF ONE OF THOSE FIVE A SMALL OBJECT WAS PUSHED TOWARDS HIM, AND HE COULD NOT USE IT, AND HE DID NOT GIVE IT BACK, AND HE DID NOT ASK ANYBODY WHAT IT WAS FOR, AND THE PERSON WHO GAVE IT IS NOT A PERSON WHO OWNS ANYTHING.**
- **THE THING IS A PAIR OF WOOLLEN GLOVES WITH NO FINGERS IN THEM, GREY, SHINY AT THE THUMB AND THE HEEL, WITH THE PAPER BAND STILL ON ONE.** The giver is the young woman of about twenty, who put them on a table beside his cup without saying anything about them, then said they were no use on a dish and that he would have had a bad winter, and then said where the proper ones were to be had on that parade and that she had been in twice asking and had not asked twice in the one shop.
- **HE CANNOT USE THEM BECAUSE HE NEEDS HIS FINGERS TO GRIP AND TO FEEL AND HE WASHES UP IN HOT WATER. HE PUT THEM IN THE LEFT POCKET OF HIS CARDIGAN AND PUT A HAND IN THAT POCKET TO CHECK IT BEFORE HE WENT, AND FOUND A RECEIPT AND A LOLLY STICK IN THERE, AND LEFT THE GLOVES WHERE THEY WERE. ON THE THURSDAY HE PUT THEM ON AT THE TOP OF A STAIR FOR ABOUT AS LONG AS A CUP OF TEA TAKES, THEN TOOK THEM OFF AGAIN, AND BY FRIDAY THEY WERE BACK IN THE POCKET AND DRY THROUGH.**
- **THE FIVE ROOMS START WITH THE KITCHEN AT THE BACK OF A PARADE IN THE MORNING, THE FLOOR OF THE SHOP THAT SHUTS EARLY AT TEN, A KITCHEN IN A HOUSE IN CORRANCE LANE AT HALF PAST ONE WHERE HE IS BEING PAID THE SAME FIGURE AS THE WOMAN WHO USUALLY COMES, A HALL OFF A PARADE IN THE EVENING, AND A ROOM OVER A SHOP AT THE END OF A PARADE WHERE SIX PEOPLE PLAY CARDS.**
- **HE IS ON THE DISHES. HE HAS NO TITLE, GRADE, DEPARTMENT, CHAIR, SEAT, MEMBERSHIP, FORM, ROW ON A ROTA OR ANY WAY OF BEING SAID ANYTHING ABOUT, BEING ASKED WHETHER HE WAS DOING ANYTHING ON FRIDAY NIGHT IS NOT A STANDING, BEING USEFUL IS NOT A JOB AND BEING IN A ROOM IS NOT BEING A MEMBER, AND THE THING HE ASKED ON THE FOURTH OF JUNE IS STILL THE THING HE ASKED IN JUNE AND WAS NOT ASKED AND WAS NOT ANSWERED. THE WORD *THANK* IS AT ZERO IN THE CHAPTER.**

## 10. An ordinary thirtieth of December with everything exactly as it was

- **THE REGISTER IS AT NINETEEN, THE LINE UNDER IT IS SEVEN HUNDRED AND SIXTY-FIVE DAYS AND IS STILL BLANK, AND THAT IS THE ONE DAY-COUNT IN THE PROSE OF THESE TEN CHAPTERS.** **Nell Ardent, thirty-nine, went in at about ten past ten for a line she wanted for a form of her own, wrote it out, shut the book, opened it again because she does that, put her finger down the column as far as the writing goes, and found the last thing in the book is a yard light with its bulb in a column headed maintenance and that the bulb is out. A ruled line runs on from under it towards the foot of the page and stops about two inches short of the baseboard. She did the sum on the corner of the form with the butt end of a pen. She shelved the book. The register did not move and there is no name in the margin.**
- **AND THE BOROUGH IS ORDINARY AND THE PACT IS HOLDING AND NEITHER IS SAID AND THE WORD *PACT* APPEARS NOWHERE IN THE PROSE: five shops shut for the winter and hardboard goes over three windows on the Saturday, and the woman who runs one of them watches from the pavement · a man puts grit at the corner by the bank and does not go up Peverell Street at all · the first floor of the building by the water is cleared out and the keys go back on the Friday, and two men carry a chair and a desk down and say nothing to each other, and one of them says as they pass the corridor that there is still somebody up there · the woman of about fifty-five is in a room on a month with a hasp on its door and the light is on under it and neither man knocked · a jigsaw arrives with a flat battery, and a van comes off the bridge with a ladder and a coil of rope, and the man in his thirties remarks to nobody that this is the third ladder he has seen that week, and the man in the van says aye, and nothing else follows.
- **AND THREE ANSWERS GO ROUND AT THE HALL ON A METER WITH NINE OF THEM IN IT AND NOT ONE OF THEM THERE FOR ANYTHING YOU COULD PUT ON PAPER: THE REGISTER, OFF AN AUNT OFF A MAN OFF A LORRY IN JULY; THE DAY, THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF JUNE, GIVEN ACROSS THE TABLE WITHOUT BEING ASKED; AND A THIRD ONE THAT HAD BEEN SAID IN THAT SAME HALL ON THE SIXTH, COMING BACK ROUND WITH SOMETHING ADDED TO IT THAT NOBODY THERE COULD ACCOUNT FOR.** The man from the parade puts his hand up and says somebody in that room must know by now, and four people at that table look at the boards of it, and nobody says anything, and he puts his hand down. **The question is still a question.**
- **AND A MAN IN HIS FORTIES SAYS TO THE WOMAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-FIVE THAT SHE IS NOT LONG ON THAT ROOM, AND SHE SAYS A MONTH, AND HE SAYS RIGHT AND GOES BACK TO THE PRICE OF THE BOILER, AND NOBODY SAID THE MONTH, OR THE MONTH AFTER IT AT THE END OF IT, AND NOBODY ENQUIRED WHETHER SHE HAD ANYWHERE TO GO.**
- **NOBODY IS RESCUED. NOBODY DIES. NOBODY RENEWS ANYTHING. NOTHING WAS MINUTED. NOBODY IS THANKED AND NOBODY REFUSES TO BE THANKED. THE ELEVEN STANDING REFUSALS ARE ELEVEN. CARD 0284 IS NOT A CLOSE.**

# VOLUME 05 OPEN THREADS — after Continuation 0010, Chapter 294, Monday 30 January 2017

**Read with the "VOLUME 05, CONTINUATION 0010 — CHAPTERS 285–294" block at the end of `state/continuity.md`, which carries the canon for these ten chapters and supersedes this block wherever the two differ, and with the "VOLUME 05, CONTINUATION 0009 — CHAPTERS 275–284" block above it, which still governs everything those ten chapters did. **VOLUME 05 IS NOT CLOSED AND IS NOT DECLARED CLOSED. THE SERIES IS AT 294 OF 720. NOTHING IN CONTINUATION 0010 RESOLVED ANYTHING AND NOTHING IN IT MAY BE UNDONE, IMPROVED ON, RESTATED OR ANSWERED. EVERY DAY-COUNT BELOW IS ADDED UP FROM ITS ANCHOR ON THE DAY IN QUESTION AND NOT CARRIED FORWARD FROM A SUMMARY: at Monday 30 January 2017 the blank line under the nineteenth is seven hundred and ninety-six days, the card in the slot is seven hundred and ten, and the letter in the tray is seven hundred and twelve.****

## 1. A washer under each of four screws

- **THE MAJOR TURN: THE THING WAS DONE BEFORE ANYBODY HAD DECIDED TO ASK FOR IT, AND TWO PEOPLE FOUND OUT ABOUT IT IN DIFFERENT PLACES ON THE SAME DAY, AND ONE OF THEM ALREADY KNEW AND SAID NOTHING AND HAS SAID NOTHING SINCE.** A man in a hi-vis with a job and a price took the door of that hall off its hinges at half past seven on his own time, because the catch was bent and the top hinge screws had rusted down to stubs, and put a washer under each of the four and one under the strike plate.
- **HE SAID THE FIGURE FOR A NEW CATCH AND WOULD NOT WRITE IT DOWN AND LEFT NO CARD.** It is eighty-two pounds, and he told her she would ring him in March when the door has shut and gone again and he would not come, and that she would then say he had said he would. He said he would not charge her for the hour.
- **THE TWO WHO FOUND OUT, IN TWO PLACES, ON THE SAME MORNING: the woman who runs the shop that shuts early, on the pavement outside her own shutter, where she was standing through a man boarding up her window; and the woman of about fifty-five, in that hall at about one o'clock, when the door shut on her instead of coming in.** The woman with the key was standing four foot inside the passage and did not go out and did not go after him.
- **AND IT IS NOT BETTER. THE FLATTENED CARDBOARD BOX THAT HAD BEEN HOLDING THAT DOOR OPEN FOR A MONTH WENT OUT TO THE BIN STORE, THE HALL DOOR NOW SHUTS, IT STUCK FAST AT THE TOP ON THE FIFTEENTH OF JANUARY was forced open by February, and by then the man CAME BACK UP THAT PARADE, LOOKED AT IT AND WALKED ON.** At ten past two on the thirty-first of December the woman of about fifty-five said out loud, to nine stacked chairs, *somebody's had that door*, and nobody told her who.

## 2. A line for a bag of coal

- **THE MAJOR TURN: EVERYBODY IN THE LINE WAS WAITING FOR SOMETHING THEY HAD ALREADY BEEN TOLD THEY MIGHT GET, AND THE LINE MOVED ONCE, AND THE THING WAS OFFERED, AND NOBODY IN THE LINE WENT UP, AND THE LINE WENT.** About a dozen people on the hard at the top of Marsh Lane at four degrees, for a bag of coal off a pallet on the back of a lorry.
- **THE RUMOUR REACHED THAT HARD BY EIGHT O'CLOCK THROUGH THREE MOUTHS: a man at the Sarn yard on the Thursday before, who could not say where he had it from and did not say; to the woman who has been in that hall about two years; to the woman who works in a shop, who put a word in on it herself; and from her to two people, one of whom told the woman at the front of the line.**
- **THE MAN WHO BROUGHT IT HAD BEEN TOLD TO LEAVE IT WITH THE SHOP AND NOT TO SAY WHOSE IT WAS, AND THE WOMAN AT THE FRONT ASKED HIM AND HE SAID THE EXACT THING HE COULD NOT TELL HER, AND SHE SAID IT DOWN THE LINE.** The line went in the time it takes a shutter to come down. **The woman of about forty-two with the key to that hall was third in from the front, told nobody she had been, and stayed on the pavement after the rest had gone.**
- **THE PALLET WENT BACK ON THE LORRY AT HALF PAST FOUR AND WAS NOT OFF AGAIN UNTIL THE SEVENTH OF MARCH. THE HARD WAS EMPTY ON THE FOURTEENTH, THE TWENTY-FIRST AND THE THIRTIETH OF JANUARY, AND THE WOMAN WHO PUT THE WORD IN HAS STILL NOT SAID WHERE IT CAME FROM.** It is a thing offered when nothing is wrong and not a thing anybody asked for, and nobody is on a list and nothing is minuted and nobody is given a seat, a number, a place in a line or a way of being said anything about.

## 3. Water down a wall, and a trolley down a stair

- **THE MAJOR TURN: THE BUILDING HURT SOMEBODY WHO WAS NOT COUNTED, SOMEBODY PUT SOMETHING WHERE IT WILL NOT HAPPEN AGAIN, AND THE SOMEBODY ELSE IS A MAN WHO IS NOT ON ANYTHING AND WHO SAYS NOTHING, AND NOBODY HAS ASKED HIM WHY HE DID IT AND NOBODY WILL.** A gutter at the top of a building by the water let go of a lump of ice on Monday morning and the water came down the inside wall of the woman of about fifty-five's room, across the ceiling, down the corner, under the bed, out along the skirting, out onto the landing and down the stair.
- **THE SAME MAN IN THE HI-VIS CAME BACK ACROSS THAT YARD ON THE FRIDAY AND WENT UP ON THAT ROOF FOR ABOUT THREE HOURS.** He had been in that hall off a parade three days before and told two people in two places. He said the length of lead would not happen again in either of their lifetimes, for a figure and half a day's time, and then did it for nothing, wrote nothing, left no card, and went up the parade without going in.
- **AND A MAN IN HIS SIXTIES CAME BACK AT FOUR IN THE AFTERNOON WITH THE FOLDING PLATFORM TROLLEY AND TOOK A WET CHAIR WITH BEDDING ON IT DOWN THE STAIRS AND STOOD IT AGAINST THE WALL UNDER THE GABLE END, AND PUT THE BEDDING ON IT, AND NOBODY ASKED HIM WHY.** A ladder is not a rescue and a trolley is not an arrangement.
- **AND HER PROBLEM IS NOT SOLVED.** She is in that room on the same terms, the water did not come down again, the mark on the wall has gone the colour of the ceiling, that agent was back on that corridor two days later, still carrying his four things to think about, and never went in, and the hasp on the inside of that door is where it was which went on in the last week of October, and that is still not a thing anybody has discussed with her and nobody has told her who put it there.**

## 4. A question in a street, and an answer nobody recognises

- **THE MAJOR TURN: THE ANSWER GIVEN IN THE STREET IS A FOURTH THING, WHICH IS THE SAME AS THE THIRD AND NOT A NEW ONE, AND THE PERSON WHO GIVES IT DOES NOT KNOW THAT, AND THE QUESTION GOES ON BEING A QUESTION AFTER THEY HAVE ALL GONE HOME.** The man from the parade asked it out loud on a piece of hard for the first time in about four months, to nobody in particular, and a woman in a green coat standing behind a tray of bulbs told the man behind the potatoes that it will be a sheet somebody over the water pulls out of a drawer in a big office, and that none of them will ever be told what it was.
- **IT IS THE THIRD ANSWER, SAID BADLY, BY A WOMAN WHOSE MOTHER WORKED IN THAT SORT OF OFFICE FOR A FIRM OVER THERE, TO A MAN WHO HAD BEEN SAYING THE SAME SHAPE OF IT FOR YEARS.** He did not recognise it. Nobody at that pitch had been in that hall. The man from the parade said right and went to open his shop.
- **A WOMAN WITH A CLIPBOARD WAS THERE KEEPING A FOOTFALL TALLY ON A BOARD FOR A COURSE AND IS NOT A CLIPBOARD MAN AND WAS NOT DOING ANYBODY'S BUSINESS.** She was spoken to by neither side of it, packed the board, went down the lane and spoke to nobody, and was not in that hall on the Friday night.
- **A FAMILIAR WRONG ANSWER IS NOT A CONFIRMED ONE AND NOT A WEAKENED ONE AND NOT A SECOND ONE OF THE SAME. THE THIRD WRONG ANSWER WAS NOT CORRECTED, NOT IMPROVED ON AND NOT ADDED TO, AND THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF JUNE WAS NOT PUT BACK TO FOUR.**

## 5. A cushion on a chair for a fortnight

- **THE MAJOR TURN: NOBODY PICKS IT UP FOR A FORTNIGHT, AND ON THE FOURTEENTH DAY SOMEBODY DOES, AND THAT PERSON PUTS IT SOMEWHERE ELSE AND TELLS NOBODY WHERE, AND THE PERSON WHO LEFT IT IS NEVER ASKED AND NEVER KNOWS IT WAS PICKED UP.** A grey square cushion with a zip cover and no cover on the zip went onto the one chair in a first-floor room over a shop that had not had one since the summer, put there by a young woman who put her bag down on a table, noticed, and said nothing to anybody.
- **that room was opened and shut twice a week for two weeks, and one of them moved that end chair a short way towards the hearth and put it back with the pad where he had found it.** The man in his thirties keeps that room, opens the door on a Tuesday and shuts it on a Wednesday, and nothing is written down and he rings nobody.
- **ON THE FOURTEENTH DAY A WOMAN WHO WORKS IN THAT SHOP CAME UP AT TEN IN THE MORNING WITH A CLOTH, TURNED THE CHAIRS UP ON THE TABLE AND PUT THEM BACK, TOOK THE CUSHION OFF, WENT DOWN PAST THE TRADE COUNTER INTO THE COLD ROOM AT THE BACK AND PUT IT ON THE TOP SHELF BEHIND THE DOOR, WHERE THE SHELF IS AS DEEP AS THE CUSHION IS THICK, then went back downstairs and put her hands under the cold water.** It is not on anything and it was not on a list.
- **THE DRAWER UNDER THE TRADE COUNTER WAS NOT OPENED, NOT COUNTED, NOT ASKED ABOUT AND IS NOT NAMED IN THAT CHAPTER, AND THE DRAWER UNDER THE VESTIBULE COUNTER IS NOT MENTIONED IN ANY CHAPTER OF THIS BATCH, AND A COPY IS NOT A WALL AND AN ENVELOPE IS NOT A TRAY.**

## 6. A man who is called, and what he says

- **THE MAJOR TURN: HE COMES, AND HE SAYS THE ONE THING HE WOULD HAVE SAID IN DECEMBER AND DID NOT, AND WHAT HE SAYS IS THAT HE WAS NEVER ASKED, AND NOBODY HAS ANY ANSWER TO THAT, AND THE BOILER IS MENDED AND NOBODY WRITES ANYTHING DOWN.** Her boiler went at twenty past eight and the firm quoted ninety-four pounds again, which is the figure it quoted in December, and she asked them whether they were any good and was told they were not on that road, and rang the second number in the back of a notebook by her telephone.
- **HE IS THE MAN WHO LIVES TWO DOORS UP AND DOES GAS AND HEATING, WHO WENT PAST HER DOOR EVERY MORNING IN DECEMBER WITH HIS BAG AND SAID GOOD MORNING AND DID NOT TURN HIS HEAD, AND WHO WAS NEVER RINGED THEN AND WAS NOT ASKED IN DECEMBER AND WAS ASKED IN JANUARY.** He did the valve, got the part off the merchant's site, walked to the parade for it and came back with the part and the kitchen tap was running hot again a couple of hours after that. Then he put his bag down and sat on the arm of her sofa.
- **AND WHAT HE SAID IS THAT WHAT HE HAD BEEN TRYING TO WORK OUT SINCE ABOUT THE SEPTEMBER WAS NOT WHAT SHE HAD DONE BUT WHAT HE WAS**, and that there is nothing on him, and that the only paper about him anywhere is a sign on the side of a van he paid for, and that if there were anything on him a person has to be put on something first, and there was nothing to put him on.
- **AND SHE ASKED HIM FOR NOTHING AND HE ASKED HER FOR NOTHING AND THE FIGURE DID NOT MOVE AND HE TOLD HER THE OFFICE SETS IT TWICE.** A person who is not counted is not a person who is helped, a price that moves is not a plot, a man who is called is not a man who has been made a standing, and a man who is useful is not on anything. He wrote nothing down, there was no receipt book out, she did not ask him for one, and a bill reached her later from that office across the water, carrying a number and carrying nothing else.

## 7. A wheelbarrow in a yard nobody recognises

- **THE MAJOR TURN: IT IS THE SAME OBJECT AND NOBODY RECOGNISES IT, INCLUDING THE MAN WHO PUT IT THERE, AND IT IS PUT DOWN SOMEWHERE ELSE, AND THE SOMEWHERE ELSE IS A ROOM NOBODY IS GOING TO LOOK IN.** A builder's barrow, one wheel, galvanised, flat tyre, a dent in the front left corner of the tray, and a stamp in the underside of the handle nobody could read, standing against a wall by a shed in the yard at the back of a shop that shuts early.
- **A WOMAN HAD LIVED IN THE FLAT OVER THAT SHOP AND WENT IN NOVEMBER, AND A MAN arrived in the first week of the month with very little and a bicycle, AND HE ASKED ABOUT THE BARROW IN NOVEMBER AND WAS TOLD IT WAS NOT HIS.** The man in his thirties came in with a length of batten over his shoulder at twenty past nine, went over the barrow, and said out loud that it would be a Landis, and stopped, because he had never in his life had a Landis.
- **THE THREE OF THEM SPENT NINE HUNDRED WORDS AND SIX MINUTES ON IT AND ESTABLISHED NOTHING, AND HE WENT IN THROUGH THE KITCHEN DOOR AND SHUT IT BEHIND HIM.** A find is not a discovery, no person is discovered, nobody is a villain, nobody is a hero, and the thing that came back is not a handbag, not the buff file, not the sheet of eight towns, not the folded sheet and not the book at the end of the corridor.
- **IT WENT ON ITS SIDE IN THE BACK ROOM OF THAT SHOP ON THE SATURDAY AFTER, AGAINST A WALL FOUR FOOT OFF THE FLOOR WHERE THE CEILING SLOPES, WITH A CRATE OF BULBS IN FRONT OF IT.**

## 8. A third sheet, and a sentence that learned the wrong thing

- **THE MAJOR TURN: THE THIRD SHEET IS HANDLED BY A PERSON WHO HAS LEARNED SOMETHING FROM THE FIRST TWO AND WHO LEARNS IT WRONG, AND THE THIRD COST ALSO GOES NOWHERE, AND SOMEBODY CARRIES SOMETHING OUT AND PUTS IT SOMEWHERE NOBODY AGREED ON, AND IT IS STILL NOT ARRANGED.** A heating engineer came in unasked because a man rang him in the afternoon about the figure that went on a piece of paper in that address in November for taking a boiler out, and put a sheet on the table with a hundred and fifty-five pounds on it for a service and a record, and a line saying a service could not be booked until an account was opened.
- **THE HALL HAS NO BOILER, BECAUSE IT WENT DOWN A BACK LANE ON A TROLLEY IN NOVEMBER. WHAT IS LEFT IS A SET OF STAIRS, TWO BATTENS WITH ONE TUBE OUT, A RUN OF PIPE UNDER THE FLOOR THAT BELONGS TO A SHOP THAT HAS STOOD EMPTY SINCE THE SUMMER, AND A METER IN A DIFFERENT COMPANY'S NAME.** The engineer said the difference from the last sheet is that the last one wanted a room to prove something and this one wants him to sign, and that there is no boiler here to have a hundred and fifty-five pound's worth of heating off.
- **THE WOMAN WITH THE KEY SAID HER SENTENCE AGAIN, IN THE SAME WORDS, IN THE SAME SEQUENCE, AT THE SAME SPEED, AND IT DID NOT WORK, BECAUSE SHE ALSO SAID THAT THE SHOP NEXT DOOR WAS NOT HAVING IT EITHER.** The man in his forties said the shop next door is not hers to be speaking for, and that her two halves went either side of one thing both times they worked, and that there are three things on that table now and they go either side of nothing, and that she has learned the sentence and not the room. Nobody said which of the two she meant.
- **AND THE MAN IN HIS SIXTIES CARRIED A 2013 SERVICE CARD OUT OF THAT HALL AND STOOD IT AGAINST THE OUTSIDE WALL OF THE PORCH WITH ITS FACE TURNED INWARDS.** The man who did it is dead and his name is no use to anybody including him. Nobody opened an account, nobody rang the mobile on the letting agent's card that has been on that table since before Christmas, and the sheet went on the table face up next to the meter and was on it at midnight. The boiler in the Methodist hall on Carrow Lane, which anybody could have had for nothing since about February, is still there and still free and is not a thirteenth thing.

## 9. A lad in five places who is asked one thing

- **THE MAJOR TURN: HE IS ASKED ONE THING BY SOMEONE WHO DOES NOT KNOW THAT ASKING HIM ANYTHING IS A THING, AND HE ANSWERS IT, AND NOBODY MAKES ANYTHING OF HIM, AND HE GOES HOME, AND THE ONLY CONSEQUENCE IS THAT SOMEBODY ELSE NOW KNOWS HE EXISTS.** The woman of about forty-two with the key to that hall asked him whether he was in there on Tuesdays. He said he did not know. She said right, and went and found her keys.
- **AND LATER SHE TOLD the man in his forties, with her chin towards the rest of it, THAT THAT WAS THE LAD WHO DID THE DISHES AT THE PARADE, AND HE SAID AYE, AND SHE SAID SHE HAD seen him out the front of that shop in the middle of the morning, AND he said aye and went back to what was under the floor.** He went round that table four times with a tray. Nobody and no one at that table put anything to him about his own life, and neither of the two words people use for somebody his age was used at that table that night.
- **HE HAS NO TITLE, GRADE, DEPARTMENT, CHAIR, SEAT, MEMBERSHIP, FORM OR ROW ON A ROTA. BEING ASKED IS NOT A STANDING, BEING USEFUL IS NOT A JOB AND BEING IN A ROOM IS NOT BEING A MEMBER, AND THE THING HE ASKED IN THAT ROOM IN JUNE WAS NOT PUT TO ANYBODY IN IT AGAIN AND WAS NOT ANSWERED BY ANYBODY IN IT.** The pair of fingerless gloves are still in the left pocket of that grey cardigan and he never put them on again. **No chapter of this batch contains a thanks of any kind and the word *thank* is at zero in all ten.**
