# VOLUME 05 OPEN THREADS — after Continuation 0016, Chapter 354, Sunday 24 September 2017

**Read with the "VOLUME 05, CONTINUATION 0016 — CHAPTERS 345–354" block at the end of `state/continuity.md`, which carries the canon for these ten chapters and governs wherever the two differ, and with the "VOLUME 05, CONTINUATION 0015 — CHAPTERS 335–344" block above it, which still governs everything those ten chapters did. **VOLUME 05 IS NOT CLOSED AND IS NOT DECLARED CLOSED. THE SERIES IS AT 354 OF 720. NOTHING IN CONTINUATION 0016 RESOLVED ANYTHING AND NOTHING IN IT MAY BE UNDONE, IMPROVED ON, RESTATED OR ANSWERED. EVERY DAY-COUNT BELOW IS CALCULATED FROM ITS ANCHOR ON THE DAY IN QUESTION AND NOT CARRIED FORWARD FROM A SUMMARY: at Sunday 24 September 2017 the blank line under the nineteenth is one thousand and thirty-three days, the card in the slot is nine hundred and forty-seven, and the letter in the tray is nine hundred and forty-nine.**

## 1. A smell in a corridor, and a figure nobody was told

- **MAJOR TURN: THE BUILDING DOES A SEVENTH THING, SHE IS STILL IN THAT ROOM ON THE SAME TERMS, SOMEBODY ELSE COUNTS SOMETHING AND GETS A NUMBER THAT IS A NUMBER, AND NEITHER FACT TOUCHES THE OTHER.** The seventh thing is a smell and it is neither water nor heat: it comes into that first-floor corridor and into the room at the end of it in the dark, since about the tenth of the month, and it is gone before the light, and gone by daylight and not there when the wind is off the land, and it is worse at the bottom of the outside stair than at the top of it.
- **WHAT SHE DID, AND NOBODY WAS TOLD ANY OF IT AND NOBODY ASKED HER ANY OF IT:** she left the window open because it was open anyway, checked the one thing in that flat that makes gas and found nothing, and ruled out the pipe somebody matted in the front room years ago by herself, because that one smells in the wrong wind. **ON THE SIXTEENTH SHE COULD NOT SETTLE, AND SHE PUT THE PLASTIC CHAIR SHE KEEPS FOR THE WINDOW OUT ON TO THE LANDING AT ABOUT TWENTY TO FIVE AND SLEPT ON IT, AND SHE WAS UP AND HAD IT BACK UNDER THE WINDOW BY HALF PAST SIX, AND SHE DID IT TWICE.** She is not at anybody's door because anybody arranged it.
- The woman in the room next door along came out once because her own window is on the wrong aspect and she has had it shut since the mornings turned. **She said it was the gas, and that it was not coming out of the room next door because the woman was sat in the corridor, and was told that that was where it was coming from, said right, and put her own door back where she keeps it.** No second exchange and no offer, and no note on any door in that block, and nobody in that block has a telephone, because that block stopped being anybody's job in June.
- **THE MAN IN HIS FORTIES IS THE ONLY REASON THERE ARE TWO ACCOUNTS OF THAT SMELL IN THIS BOROUGH.** He was on that landing for about an hour on somebody else's work and gave her a cause that is real and ordinary — the river coming up under there when the wind is off the water, worse on the stairs than on the landing, a gully at the bottom he has had it off for as long as he can remember — and named a standpipe on that stair nobody has looked at since the year before last and a vent on the back of that block coming out under the second landing, and said the vent was the last thing he would be looking at. She told him the woman next door along had said it was the gas, and he stopped, because he heard a woman in that building get there before he did, and he knew it while he was saying so. **HE HAS NOT BEEN UP THAT STAIR AGAIN, AND BOTH OF THE THINGS THAT WERE SAID ARE TRUE, AND NOBODY IN THAT BUILDING WILL EVER BE TOLD WHICH OF THE TWO WOMEN WAS NEARER IT.**
- **THE COUNT IS A MILE AND A HALF AWAY AND TOUCHES NONE OF IT.** At about half past four that afternoon the woman who works in a shop brought the day's takings up the outside stair at the back of three shops, which she does four times a week, and counted them on her own kitchen table in the only order anybody who has done that for a while would use, and wrote the figure on the back of her own hand and put the money in a safe under her own counter and took the key into her own pocket. It came out about where the other three Thursdays of that month came out. **NOBODY IN THAT SHOP KNOWS WHAT IT CAME TO, NOBODY COULD TELL YOU WHAT THE SHOP TAKES IN A WEEK, SHE HAS NEVER OFFERED IT, AND THERE IS NOBODY IN THIS BOROUGH SHE WOULD TELL.** Neither of those two women has any idea the other one is on the page.
- **THE WOMAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-FIVE IS NOT HOUSED BY ANYBODY IN THAT CHAPTER. NOBODY PUT HER IN THAT ROOM, NOBODY ARRANGED ONE WORD OF HOW SHE LIVES IN IT, NOBODY WAS TOLD WHO PUT THE HASPIED SIDE ON, WHO CAPPED AN OUTLET, WHO PUT THE STOP TAP BACK ON ACROSS, OR WHO WAS ON THAT ROOF, AND NOBODY WAS TOLD ABOUT THE CHAIR OR THE BOWL OR THE COUNT, BECAUSE NOBODY KNOWS ANY OF IT.**

## 2. A ladder, a bench and a back room, and two men who are each certain

- **MAJOR TURN: THE THING IS PUT DOWN, TAKEN UP, PUT DOWN SOMEWHERE ELSE AND TAKEN UP AGAIN, TWO PEOPLE ARE SURE THEY WERE THE LAST TO HAVE IT, NEITHER IS SURE, AND NEITHER WILL ASK THE OTHER.** A four-foot painted wooden step ladder with somebody's spanner on the top tread. **A THING THAT IS MOVED IS NOT A THING THAT HAS BEEN LOOKED AFTER, NOBODY WAS TOLD WHERE IT CAME FROM, NOBODY WAS ASKED, A PERSON WHO PICKS A THING UP IS NOT A PERSON WHO HAS ADOPTED IT, AND THERE IS NO PERSON IN THIS BOROUGH WHO COULD HAVE GRANTED THE USE OF THAT YARD TO ANYBODY AT ALL.**
- Sat 5 Aug, late afternoon: the man in his forties left it in a yard off the Cleeve road with its feet up on a bench, because he did not want to explain to a man in his own workshop why he had taken his own ladder out of his van.
- Sun 6 Aug, morning: the man in his thirties found it, used it for half a morning on somebody's upstairs, put it back where it was, and did not shut a gate he had opened. That afternoon he asked one question about it at a counter in a shop and did not say where it had been. **She said one word and has never asked him a second thing about it.**
- Wed 16 Aug, early afternoon: the man in his forties went into that shop's back room for something else and found the ladder against the far wall with a fortnight of dust round its feet. **He was not the man it had been left with and nobody was in a position to tell him that.** He took the spanner off the top tread into his pocket without deciding to, carried it out past a counter where she was on the telephone, said good afternoon, and put it back on the bench in that yard. He has told nobody he took a thing out of a shop.
- Sun 20 Sep, ten to ten: he went into that shop after a coil of wire, went through to the back room while she was at the rack, and it was under a blanket at the back of his van before a minute had gone. **She saw him go through and come out and charged him for the wire and said the price was dear and he said it was, and neither of them said one word about the ladder.** He has it under a blanket in his van.
- **BOTH ACCOUNTS ARE STRAIGHT AND EACH HAS A HOLE IN IT.** Each man is certain the other never had a hand on it, and the reason each is certain is a fact about his own week and not about the other's. **ASKING IS ONE QUESTION AND THE REPLY TO IT IS THE OTHER QUESTION, AND THERE IS NOT ONE ANSWER BETWEEN THEM THAT WOULD SURVIVE BEING GIVEN.** The spanner is in a pocket in a van and has never been a question to anybody.

## 3. A true sentence, a wrong lane, and a longer walk home

- **MAJOR TURN: THE SENTENCE GETS ONE PLACE FURTHER AND THE ROOM THAT HEARS IT TAKES IT AS A FACT, AND SOMEBODY IN THAT ROOM IS WRONG ABOUT SOMETHING IN IT, AND NOBODY ASKS ANYBODY ANYTHING.** In the hall on a meter the man in his sixties put forward that a house stands empty at the top of a lane, and he gave the address in more detail than anything has been given in that room in months, and **the only person who heard it was a shopkeeper.**
- She gave it to the man who works nights at a counter as a fact rather than as something she had been told, and it came back with two questions, one about which house and one about which road, and she could not answer either. **THE ROAD SHE ATTACHED IT TO WAS NOT THE ROAD IT IS ON.** His lane has a kerb on one side, seven houses in it, a light over the last door and no board on any window in it. The other one is off a different road, a quarter of a mile the other way, and there is a board outside the house in that one.
- She does not know that she was wrong. He did not find out and is not going to, because the only route to finding out runs through a question about a road he cannot name, and a man who asks a woman which road a lane comes off has told her he could not say which road that lane hangs off, and he had somewhere else to be on the Friday of that week whatever she said.
- **WHAT IT HAS COST IS ABOUT TWO HUNDRED YARD OF PAVEMENT AND ABOUT FOUR MINUTES, EVERY NIGHT, FOR FIVE WEEKS.** He has never told anybody he used that lane. There is nothing wrong with the lane and there is a woman in the last house of it with a car on the drive, and the board outside the other house is a different house, and no one here will ever walk up either lane and establish it. The man in his sixties has no way of finding out that he was wrong and would not go and look for himself if he could.
- **A FAMILIAR WRONG ANSWER IS NOT A CONFIRMED ONE AND NOT A WEAKENED ONE AND NOT A SECOND ONE OF THE SAME. THE THIRD WRONG ANSWER WAS NOT CORRECTED AND NOT IMPROVED ON AND NOT ADDED TO, THE FOURTH WAS NOT CALLED A FIFTH, AND NOBODY WAS TOLD WHICH DAY ANY COLLECTION COMES ON.**

## 4. A shutter at half past ten and a man who lost a working day

- **MAJOR TURN: TWO SMALL THINGS HAPPEN, ONE IS ORDINARY AND ONE COSTS SOMEBODY A DAY, ONE PERSON COULD PUT THEM TOGETHER, THE CHAPTER DOES NOT, AND THE ONE PERSON WHO COULD IS NOT IN EITHER PLACE.**
- **THE ORDINARY ONE IS A SHOP OPENING HOUR.** A shopter on that parade went out for her lunch and the man behind the counter put the bar across and hauled the shutter down with about nine people inside and a queue at the card machine, and the rope stuck and then did not, and the shop went dark from the pavement with the light still on inside and the machine visible through the slot. She came back at about one and carried on serving and has never mentioned it to anybody. About thirty people went past in the middle of the day, nine of them looked, and not one mentioned it to the next person. **THE ONLY PERSON TOLD ANYTHING WAS A MAN ON HIS WAY TO A BUS, AND HE TOLD THE WOMAN WHO WORKS IN A SHOP FOUR DAYS LATER IN THAT SHOP, AND SHE AGREED WITH HIM AND SAID THE OBVIOUS THING ABOUT A LUNCH, AND THAT WAS THE WHOLE OF IT.**
- **THE ONE THAT COSTS A DAY IS A TRADESMAN'S MORNING.** He turned up at a house a few minutes before ten for half an hour's work. The woman who lives there told him at the door that she was out until about two, that the buses were hourly, and that it would be as well to come first, and she was sorry about it. He said it was no trouble and did not come at about two. **HE WAITED A LITTLE AND THEN WENT AND SAT IN AN EMPTY CAR PARK FOR THE REST OF THE DAY, BECAUSE THERE WAS WORK IN HIS OWN SHOP PROMISED FOR THE MONDAY AND IT WAS NOT THAT KIND OF WORK AND HE WAS NOT GOING TO STAND IN THAT SHOP ON A FRIDAY AFTERNOON WITH HIS HANDS EMPTY.** He read a paper he had brought with him, which takes about an hour and a half, drank the water he had brought for that, nodded at a man doing a stocktake on a van, watched a woman and a dog at the far kerb, did the job at ten past two in about twenty minutes, and got home at about half past five. About six hours of that day are nobody's, and he has not said one word about that day to anybody.
- **THE ONE PERSON WHO HAS BOTH IS A THIRD OF A MILE FROM BOTH.** She heard the shutter on the Thursday and the day on the Friday, at her own step, with the other man's bag in her hand. **SHE HAS NEVER SPOKEN TO THE MAN WHO TOLD HER ABOUT THE SHUTTER AND COULD NOT TELL YOU HIS NAME, AND THE MAN WHO LOST THE DAY DOES NOT KNOW THAT SHE WAS EVER TOLD ABOUT THE SHUTTER AT ALL.** There is nothing in this borough that puts those two in one breath, and she did not try, and it was not a thing she thought about afterwards. Two things in a week is not a pattern and a coincidence is not a connection.

## 5. A fifth time, and somebody else's hands on a ladder

- **MAJOR TURN: HE SAYS IT AGAIN AND DOES NOT DO IT, SOMEBODY ELSE HEARD IT FROM TWO MEN AND NOT FROM HIM, ALL THREE OF THEM ARE BEING STRAIGHT, AND THE CONSEQUENCE OF THE SENTENCE IS SOMEBODY ELSE'S HANDS AND NOT A WORD.**
- **THE THING IS A BIRD BOX THE SIZE OF A SHOEBOX** on the gable end of a house at the bottom of a street off the Cleeve road, painted the colour of the render, with a chip out of the front lip, and nobody on that street knows who fixed it there. **THERE IS OTHER WORK ON THAT SAME GABLE WHICH IS NOT THE BIRD BOX:** four foot of soft mortar joints, priced in June, chased twice, and refused in July because three other people were being asked about it. The box has been on that wall the whole time and neither man in this story has ever referred to it.
- **HE HAS SAID HE WILL HAVE A BOX MADE AND SCREWED UP THERE BEFORE THE END OF SEPTEMBER FIVE TIMES, TO FOUR PEOPLE, AND THE FIFTH WAS THIS MORNING to a man who wanted nothing from him.** The other four went to a woman at her own gate in July, to the man in his forties in a yard over a length of batten, to a man in a fleece on a parade, and to the woman who works in a shop at her counter — **and on that last occasion his work notes were out of the bag and in his hand the band round it off, and she watched him slip it back into the bag with nothing written on it, and she told him he was not going to write that down, and he said no, and said he has a line in there for three letters in another sign that he has not opened since the summer before last and is not starting now.**
- **WHAT HAS GONE ROUND THAT STREET IS A DIFFERENT SENTENCE, AND IT CAME FROM TWO MEN WHO HAD NOT HAD IT FROM HIM.** What has gone round is a claim that somebody is going to have that wall seen to. Two men in fleeces are the source of it and neither of the two of them had it from him: one picked it up at a stall in a market four miles off, the other got it from that one a good way above that, and no name went with it in either direction. **THE MAN IN HIS FORTIES HAD HIS OWN QUOTATION ON THAT WALL FROM JUNE AND HAD NOT BEEN GIVEN THE WORK, AND ON TUESDAY AFTERNOON HE PUT THOSE TWO FACTS TOGETHER AND WENT UP THERE WITH A LADDER AND A FLAT BAR.**
- **HE TOOK THE BOX OFF ITS TWO SCREWS AND PUT IT ON THE PATH FACE DOWN AND HE IS NOT GOING TO PUT IT BACK.** The screws came out with two foot of render still on the heads of them. He came back on the Wednesday to do the pointing he had not been given, found the box still on the path, stood and looked at it and left it where it was, **because a man here who restores a fitting to a surface somebody has told him is booked in is a man who has taken the job on.** He did the four foot in about two hours with nobody watching and has not charged anybody and has not mentioned it. The woman who lives there stepped over it on the Tuesday night and again on the Wednesday morning.
- **THE MAN WHO MADE THE PROMISE FOUND OUT BY LOOKING AT THE PATH AND SAID NOTHING ELSE AT ALL.** He has not done it and September is out in a month and he has not started it. At about half past four that afternoon the woman who works in a shop had the whole of it at her counter in about six minutes, in that order, and he agreed with every part of it. **A LIST IS NOT A DOCUMENT, A LIST IS NOT A FORM, THERE IS NO FORM IN THIS BOROUGH, A THING SAID OUT LOAD IS NOT A THING ANYBODY KEEPS, AND NOBODY WAS GIVEN A TITLE, A GRADE, A DEPARTMENT, A CHAIR, A SEAT, A MEMBERSHIP OR A ROW. THE THING IS NOT A STEP, A SLATE, A LENGTH OF CLOSE-BOARD, A GUTTER, A DOWNPIPE, A FENCE POST OR THREE LETTERS.**

## 6. Two doorsteps, one refusal and one leaving, and nobody told about either

- **MAJOR TURN: ONE THING IS HELD OUT AND TURNED DOWN WITHOUT EXPLANATION AND WITHOUT A QUESTION, AND A SECOND THING IS CARRIED TO A DIFFERENT DOOR AND LEFT AGAINST IT, AND NEITHER PERSON IS TOLD THAT THE OTHER HAPPENED. IT IS NOT A CARPET, IT IS NOT A CHEST, IT IS NOT A VACUUM CLEANER, IT IS NOT A SAUCEPAN, IT IS NOT A FOLDING TABLE, AND NOTHING IN IT CAME OUT OF A SKIP OR A YARD.**
- **THE FIRST, THREE WEEKS AGO, AT THE TOP OF AN OUTSIDE STAIR.** A man who clears houses got up nine treads in two carries with a complete green sewing machine on a wooden stand, and put it down on the step outside a door and knocked. He did not open with the name of it; he stood aside so she could see all of it and then named it, and said where it had come from, and told her that should she not want it he would undo his own errand and let it lie. **SHE SAID NO. HE DID NOT ASK HER WHY, NOT ONE SYLLABLE CAME BACK, AND NOTHING AT ALL CAME OUT OF EITHER OF THEM IN THE TIME IT TOOK HIS HANDS TO FIND THE HEAD OF THAT MACHINE AGAIN.** He took it down, left the street door on the latch and drove off, and has not been up that stair since. **THE NOISE OF HIM ON THAT STAIR IS THE ONLY EVIDENCE ANYBODY IN THAT BLOCK HAS THAT ANYTHING HAPPENED.** She is still in that room, she has told nobody, she has told the woman next door along a single word of it, and that block holds nobody with anybody to hear it.
- **THE SECOND, TWO DAYS AGO, IN A STREET OFF THE CLEEVE ROAD.** Out of the same house went a wooden chair, one of four, with a ring worn into the seat. **HE CARRIED IT UP BECAUSE HE WAS TWO DOORS ALONG FROM THERE THAT WEEK AND HIS VAN WAS FULL AND THE CHAIR WAS IN THE WAY.** He put it on the front step of number fourteen against the door. It was not raining. He did not knock, he left no note and he did not put it anywhere sheltered, and then he went on down the street to the job he was there for and did not come back to that door.
- **THE WOMAN AT THAT HOUSE IS ABOUT THIRTY-FIVE, HER HUSBAND IS AWAY AT SEA, AND THERE HAS BEEN AN EMPTY PLACE AT ONE END OF HER SETTEE SINCE THE FIRST WEEK OF JUNE.** The chair is in that gap. It does not match, it is a foot too wide, and one spindle is a different colour from the rest. She has not asked anybody where it came from and has not mentioned it. **THE MAN IN HIS FORTIES WORKED AT THE HOUSE NEXT DOOR FOR THE WHOLE OF THAT DAY AND DID NOT KNOW THERE WAS A CHAIR ON A STEP, AND A MAN IN A FLEECE WENT PAST, LOOKED, AND KEPT GOING, AND THOSE TWO HAVE NEVER EXCHANGED A WORD.**
- **ON THE MONDAY HE WAS AT A COUNTER FOR ABOUT FIVE MINUTES AND TOLD THE WOMAN WHO WORKS IN A SHOP ABOUT THE MACHINE, ABOUT HOW MANY TIMES HE HAS BEEN UP THAT STAIR, AND ABOUT NINE FOOT OF WALL IN A BEDROOM HE COULD MAKE IF ANYBODY WANTED IT, AND THAT HE WAS NOT GOING BACK UNTIL SOMEBODY IN THAT BLOCK ASKED HIM, AND NOBODY IN THAT BLOCK HAS A TELEPHONE. HE SAID NOTHING ABOUT THE CHAIR, AND SHE KNOWS NOTHING ABOUT THE CHAIR.** A gift turned down is not a falling-out, a gift taken is not a purchase, a person who refuses owes nobody a reason and is owed nobody a question, and a thing left on a step is not a gift either.

## 7. A fitting nobody would name, and a torch on a wall

- **MAJOR TURN: HE HAS THE THING ALL DAY, THE ONLY PERSON IN THAT ROOM WHO KNEW WHY THE LIGHT WAS OUT SAYS NOTHING, HE LEAVES THE THING SOMEWHERE HIMSELF, HE TELLS ONE PERSON, AND THAT PERSON DOES NOTHING WITH WHAT HE SAYS.**
- **THE CHAPTER IS ONE ROOM AND ONE MORNING AND A CORRIDOR AND A WALL BY A STOP. IT IS NOT SEVEN ROOMS, IT IS NOT A DAY, AND THE ONE THING HE SAYS IS ANSWERED WITH A QUESTION HE CANNOT ANSWER, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT FAILURE FROM THE SIX THAT CAME BEFORE IT.**
- **THE FITTING IN THAT KITCHEN TAKES A CAP THAT HAS NOT BEEN MADE NEW FOR A GENERATION, AND EVERY SHOP IN THIS BOROUGH THAT SELLS A BULB SELLS THE OTHER ONE.** The man who cooks in that kitchen worked that out in July, or was told it, and has bought the wrong thing about six times since, on Saturdays, four miles out of his way, and put the wrong thing in each time because the light was out, and has sat with a lamp on a table ever since. **HE HAS NEVER USED THE WORD FOR HIS OWN FITTING IN THAT ROOM AND NOBODY HAS.**
- **THE LAD KNOWS WHY IT IS NOT WORKING AND HAS KNOWN FOR A WEEK, AND HE WORKED IT OUT IN JUNE.** He bought a hand torch off a man with a trestle of old stock at a market four miles off, for two pounds, and it needed a cap of the kind his own kitchen takes, and he had one and put it in the torch, and it is the last of them he has. **IF HE HAD SAID THE WORD IN THAT KITCHEN IN JUNE, THE MAN WHO COOKS IN IT WOULD HAVE HAD WHAT HE NEEDED AND THE TORCH WOULD HAVE GONE ON THAT MAN'S SHELF FOR GOOD.** So he has said nothing for seven weeks, including on four Mondays on which he thought about it.
- **THE BULB WENT AT ABOUT HALF PAST TEN WITH ABOUT NINE PEOPLE IN THAT ROOM AND A CONVERSATION OF ABOUT A MINUTE.** Three of them accounted for it out loud. **THE LAD HAD A CLOTH AT THE SINK IN HIS HAND AND WIPED SOMETHING THAT WAS ALREADY DRY.** The man who cooks in that kitchen then took one of his spares out of a cupboard, put it in to see, could not get it past the ring, said the word for what that is, said he had a look at the back of it, and said it was one of the old ones. **HE DID NOT ASK THE LAD AND THE LAD DID NOT TELL HIM.** The spares are still in that cupboard and the lamp is still on that table.
- **IN THE AFTERNOON HE WENT UP THE HILL WITH HIS BAG, TOOK THE TORCH OUT, CLOSED HIS HAND ON IT, AND LEFT IT IN THE BAG.** The woman of about fifty-five stopped him in that corridor and asked him one question about where it was going, and he told her he did not know, and she accepted that and carried on down with what she was carrying and used nothing he had said. He has not been asked why he comes up on a day that is not his and has not said.
- **AT ABOUT HALF PAST FOUR HE PUT THE TORCH ON A WALL BY A BUS STOP AT THE TOP OF A ROAD AND LEFT IT.** No note, no word to anybody, two men at the stop who did not look at it. **THE WOMAN WHO HOLDS THE KEY TO A HALL OFF THAT PARADE GOT A BUS FROM THAT STOP AT ABOUT TEN PAST FIVE AND WAS STOOD AT THE END OF THAT WALL AND LOOKED AT IT AND DID NOT PICK IT UP,** and there is no way of carrying a torch off a pavement for no reason that ends well for anybody, and she is four times a week at that stop, and has passed it every time since and never once stopped. **HE DOES NOT KNOW THAT SHE WAS STOOD THERE.** He was told, that evening, from a second hand, and said that if that was the kind of thing it was then the fitting could have had it back in July, and nobody took him up on it, and he never asked after the whereabouts of it. The three key-holding women were not put in one sentence in that chapter. **NO THANKS OF ANY KIND APPEARS IN THAT CHAPTER AND NONE APPEARS ANYWHERE IN THIS BATCH.**

## 8. A window painted shut by somebody who did not live there, and a time on a list

- **MAJOR TURN: THE BUILDING DOES AN ORDINARY THING TO NOBODY, SOMEBODY PUTS UP A LIST OF NOTHING AND FINDS ONE THING ON IT, THE ONE THING IS NOT WHAT THE LIST IS FOR, AND NEITHER FACT CHANGES ANYTHING.**
- **A SASH WINDOW AT THE END OF THAT CORRIDOR HAS NOT BEEN OPENABLE FOR A LONG TIME AND THERE IS NO WAY OF TELLING HOW LONG.** It was shut and painted shut by somebody, on purpose, and the paint in the corner of it is several layers thick and none of them has ever cracked, which means it has not been argued with. **A WEDGE OF OFFCUT WENT UNDER IT IN THE LAST HOT WEEK, PUT IN BY SOMEBODY IN THAT BUILDING WITH A KNIFE, AND THE SASH HAS NOT SHIFTED SINCE.** A cat lives in the room behind it and there is a chair by it and a radio, and the woman in there has not opened it and did not try in the heat, and that wedge has not had anything shift in it for the best part of a year.
- **THE MAN IN HIS FORTIES FOUND THAT OUT BY ACCIDENT, IN THE MIDDLE OF DOING SOMETHING ELSE, WITH HIS HAND ON THE FRAME.** He was steadying himself while he set a bit into plaster and the frame did not move at all, so he came back to it later with a knife and lifted the corner, and the paint came away in three flakes, each about as long as a finger, **and the coat on top of that window is the same colour as the four doors of that landing and is the only unbroken coat on it, and underneath it is a thin drab green that has run across the joint between the two sashes, which can only happen if it went on after they were last moved.**
- **THE DOORS WERE DONE ABOUT TWELVE YEARS AGO, ALL FOUR OFF ONE TIN, WHICH PUTS THE WINDOW SHUT BEFORE THE DOORS AND PUTS THE MAN WHO SHUT IT SOMEWHERE IN THAT BUILDING IN A DECADE NOBODY CAN NAME.** The block stopped being anybody's responsibility before the summer and there is no paper about that window in this borough, and a stranger with a ladder and an afternoon could have shut one like that in any decade of the last fifty, and nobody in that street is going to add anything to that. He put the wedge back, did the shelf he came for, did not tell the man who let him in, and **did not knock on the door of the flat behind the window.**
- **A MILE OFF, THE WOMAN WHO WORKS IN A SHOP WRITES DOWN WHAT HER SHOP WANTS FOR THE WEEK, EACH SUNDAY NIGHT, ON THE REVERSE OF A PAD LEAF.** About nine lines, no columns, no boxes, no heading, and nobody in this borough will ever see it. Two weeks running there is a time of day written four lines below the fruit on both of those sheets, in the same pencil in the same hand. **IT IS NOT A PRICE, IT IS NEITHER A DELIVERY NOR AN HOUR OF OPENING, BECAUSE THAT SHOP OPENS AT EIGHT AND HAS NEVER OPENED AT THAT TIME ON ANY DAY OF ITS LIFE.** She wrote it twice, three days of shopping apart, on two sheets of the same size out of the same pad, and she cannot account for it, and there is nothing in this borough that would let her account for it, **because a page like that holds no day beside any line on it.** She has not thrown the first one out.
- **THE TWO THINGS NEVER CAME WITHIN ABOUT A MILE AND A HALF OF EACH OTHER, AND THE ONE TIME THE TWO OF THEM WERE IN A ROOM TOGETHER ONE OF THEM WAS BUYING A LENGTH OF BOARD AND THE OTHER HAD THE PAD IN HER HAND, AND NEITHER KNEW THE OTHER WAS THINKING ABOUT ANYTHING.** A LIST OF NOTHING IS NOT A FORM, A LIST OF NOTHING IS NOT A DOCUMENT, AND NOBODY WAS ADDED TO IT AND NOBODY WAS TAKEN OFF IT.

## 9. One sentence, two hearers, and a room they were both in

- **MAJOR TURN: THE SAME SENTENCE GOES OUT TWICE AND COMES BACK TWICE AS TWO DIFFERENT THINGS, THE PERSON WHO SAID IT CANNOT TELL WHICH SHE MEANT, AND THE TWO PEOPLE WHO HEARD IT ARE IN A ROOM TOGETHER BEFORE EITHER OF THEM SAYS ANYTHING.**
- **SHE GOES TO THAT HALL BECAUSE THE ROOM IS WARM AND THAT WALK IS THE ONLY WALKING SHE DOES NOW.** On the Sunday she sat at the back for the whole of a meeting, said nothing in it, and afterwards put her coat over the back of a chair while the room emptied and the man who does that hall went through to the kitchen with the tap running. **He was at that table's far end with a cloth.** There was nobody else in the room. **SHE SAID THE NAME OF THE BUILDING AND THEN SHE SAID THAT NOBODY HAS EVER MADE A LIST OF IT, AND HE SAID NOTHING FOR ABOUT FOUR SECONDS AND SAID NO AND CARRIED ON WITH THE CLOTH.** He did not ask her and she did not tell him, and that stair has never been on his round and never will be, and the pad was in the bag at his feet and stayed where it was.
- **ON THE TUESDAY SHE SAID THE SAME EIGHT WORDS TO A MAN IN A FLEECE AT A BUS STOP WHILE HE WAS WAITING FOR A BUS HE TAKES EVERY MORNING.** Three other people were at that stop and heard none of it. He asked what she meant by it, and she told him the building, and he told her that nothing in that building is on any list of anything and that nobody has ever been asked for anything in it and that he has walked past its foot a hundred times and has never seen a man go up that stair with anything in his hand. He got on the bus. **HE DID NOT ASK HER A SECOND QUESTION, BECAUSE A WOMAN OF FIFTY-FIVE STANDING AT A BUS STOP SAYING SOMETHING HE DOES NOT UNDERSTAND IS NOT A THING A MAN IN THIS BOROUGH CAN FOLLOW UP ON, AND HE TOOK FROM IT THAT THERE IS NOBODY COUNTING ANYTHING THERE, WHICH IS WHAT HE BELIEVED ABOUT THAT STREET ALREADY.** **What she meant by it she does not know. BOTH SAYINGS WERE THE SAME SENTENCE IN HER MOUTH, FOUR DAYS APART, TO A MAN WITH A BAG OF WORK NOTES IN IT AND AGAIN TO A MAN CARRYING A FOLDED PAPER, AND SHE HAS NOT THOUGHT ABOUT IT SINCE THE MIDDLE OF THAT TUESDAY AND NOBODY IS GOING TO ASK HER.**
- **ON THE WEDNESDAY EVENING THE PAIR OF THEM STOOD IN THAT SAME ROOM WITHIN FOUR FEET OF EACH OTHER ON THE SAME SIDE OF IT FOR TWENTY MINUTES.** The hall was open and eight of them were in it, and they had both had a cup, and neither of them said anything about anything until one of them said the tea had gone cold. **Each of them was without the other's half of it and neither was going to say. THE ONLY SENTENCE EITHER OF THEM ADDRESSED TO THE OTHER THAT EVENING WAS ABOUT THE TEMPERATURE OF A CUP OF TEA.** A man at the end of a street put something about his own afternoon to the table and nobody picked it up. **A THING SAID TWICE BY ONE PERSON IS NOT A POLICY AND NOT A MESSAGE AND NOT A STANDING, AND NOBODY WAS TOLD WHAT SHE MEANT AND NOBODY IS GOING TO BE.**

- **THE MAN IN HIS FORTIES LET HIMSELF INTO THE BUILDING BY THE WATER WITH HIS OWN KEY AT ABOUT HALF PAST FIVE, WENT UP THE OUTSIDE STAIR AND ALONG THAT CORRIDOR, STOOD A COUPLE OF MINUTES NINE FOOT OFF THAT END WALL WITH HIS HANDS IN HIS POCKETS, AND CAME BACK DOWN AND WENT HOME. THE LAST OF THEM IS A YARD LAMP, ENTERED AS GONE ABOUT TWO YEARS BACK AGAINST A HEADING KEPT BACK FOR THAT CLASS OF ENTRY, THE COLUMN UNDER THAT HEADING HAS BEEN EMPTY SINCE THE LAMP WENT IN, AND THE SHEET GOES ON A COUPLE OF FINGERS PAST IT AND THEN GIVES OUT WELL SHORT OF THE BOTTOM OF THAT VOLUME, AND NOBODY EVER CLOSED THE GAP. THE LINE UNDER THAT LAST ENTRY IS THE ONE FIXED THING IN THAT BUILDING, IT IS BLANK, IT WAS BLANK AT THE START OF THIS MONTH, AND TODAY IT WAS NOT TOUCHED AT ALL.**
- **AND AT ABOUT HALF PAST NINE THAT EVENING, ON THE SECOND STAIR OF THAT OUTSIDE STAIR, WITH HER BACK AGAINST THE WALL, SHE DID IT AGAIN ON HER FINGERS.** She has not been near that bay since long before the hot weather and is not going, and she does not know what the other eighteen entries say and has never tried. **She worked it out in her own kitchen off a calendar in April, counted it again in July, said the figure out loud in that hall in July, was told nobody was going to check it, and said that she was not asking anybody to. TONIGHT IT IS A THOUSAND AND THIRTY-THREE DAYS, AND NO OTHER ROAD RUNS TO THAT, AND THE PAGE OFFERS IT NOTHING TO STAND AGAINST, AND SHE WROTE NOTHING AND TOLD NOBODY.** Then she got up, and went down for her water with two of them and one hooked through the other, and pulled the street door to behind her at the bottom, the way she has since June.

# VOLUME 05 OPEN THREADS — after Continuation 0018, Chapter 374

**Read with the "VOLUME 05, CONTINUATION 0018 — CHAPTERS 365–374" block at the end of `state/continuity.md`, which carries the canon for these ten chapters and governs wherever the two differ, and with the "VOLUME 05, CONTINUATION 0017 — CHAPTERS 355–364" block above it, which still governs everything those ten chapters did. **VOLUME 05 IS NOT CLOSED AND IS NOT DECLARED CLOSED. THE SERIES IS AT 374 OF 720. NOTHING IN CONTINUATION 0018 RESOLVED ANYTHING AND NOTHING IN IT MAY BE UNDONE, IMPROVED ON, RESTATED OR ANSWERED. EVERY DAY-COUNT BELOW IS CALCULATED FROM ITS ANCHOR ON THE DAY IN QUESTION AND NOT CARRIED FORWARD FROM A SUMMARY: at Thursday 7 December 2017 the blank line under the nineteenth is one thousand one hundred and seven days, the card in the slot is one thousand and twenty-one, and the letter in the tray is one thousand and twenty-three.****

## 1. A household that lost its warm room for four days

- **MAJOR TURN: HE QUOTED A DAY AND A HALF AND SPENT FOUR, HE FINISHED AND WENT HOME, HE WAS LATE FOR A MAN WITH A FLOOR OF HIS OWN, AND THE DAY AFTER HE LEFT A MAN THE HOUSEHOLD FOUND FOR ITSELF HAD THE WHOLE OF IT DONE IN ONE. NEITHER PARTY HAS SAID A WORD ABOUT ANY OF IT TO ANYBODY.**
- **WHY FOUR DAYS:** the room is not what he was told it was, the joists are at eighteen inch and not sixteen, and there is an obstruction under the plaster on the wall side that nobody thought to mention. He took his own new work out, scribed to what was there, made a filler out of a cutting and went back up three nights running.
- **WHAT IT COST:** the only warm room in that house in the month of November, and a man half a mile off who stood waiting there until the middle of the morning on the Tuesday, before he began, and finished the last of it by himself on the Thursday, and has not mentioned the wait since.
- **THE MOMENT:** he came back a fortnight later for a canvas bag of fixings he had left in a front room and the work was visible from the gate. He did not look at it. He asked whether there was a socket in the front room. She was in the doorway of the back room the whole time and neither of them said anything, then or since.
- **WHAT IS LEFT:** nine sacks under a tarpaulin along a brick wall, because there was no hurry set and nobody has chased them, and a tool he left on that wall on the Thursday and collected on the Thursday.

## 2. A thing for a fire, in a room with no fire

- **MAJOR TURN: SOMEONE ELSE'S JOB THREW OUT A SET OF FIRE IMPLEMENTS, A MAN WITH A BARROW COULD FIND NOWHERE TO PUT IT, HE USED SOMEBODY ELSE'S ROOM AT TEN AT NIGHT WITHOUT ARRANGING ANYTHING, AND THREE PEOPLE ON THAT LANDING HAVE SEEN IT AND NONE OF THEM WILL RAISE IT. THE MAN WHO BROUGHT IT DOES NOT KNOW THAT THE OTHER TWO LOOKED.**
- **THE THING:** about eighteen inch high on a stand of its own, shovel, brush and tongs, the rail rubbed bright, a clean half-moon on the floor under one foot, and a dark patch on the handle where a hand goes. It is not dusty. **NOTHING FOR A FIRE EXISTS IN THAT ROOM, AND WHATEVER OPENING THERE ONCE WAS SITS IN THE WALL OF THE ROOM NEXT ALONGSIDE, WHICH IS NOT HERS.**
- **THE THREE, AND WHY NONE ASKS:** the woman whose floor it is on will not move it, because moving it is an admission, and she has hung a jug on the rail of it for want of anywhere else in a small room to hang one; the neighbour next door, whose door never shuts over three inches and who saw it from her own doorway; and the man himself, who has been in that room once and has not been near it since.
- **A THING PUT INTO A ROOM BY A MAN WHO GAINS NOTHING AND EXPECTS NOTHING IS NOT A GIFT, NOT A DELIVERY, NOT A PRESENT, NOT A BEQUEST AND NOT AN ARRANGEMENT, AND NOBODY IN THAT BUILDING OWES ANYBODY AN ACCOUNT OF WHAT IS ON THE FLOOR. THE ONLY MAN WHO COULD ANSWER THE QUESTION IS THE MAN WHO DID IT, AND HE IS NOT GOING TO BE ASKED.**

## 3. Nine words, two men, one gap

- **MAJOR TURN: A SENTENCE OF NINE WORDS WENT ACROSS A TABLE OF FOUR PEOPLE ONCE AND CLOSED A SUBJECT, AND TWO OF THEM HEARD SOMETHING ELSE IN IT, AND THE SPEAKER WILL NEVER BE TOLD WHICH.**
- **THE SENTENCE:** nine words, said to nobody in particular, closing a subject: a man who used to come into that shop on that day, stopped coming in the summer, and is in none of this now. **WHAT SHE SAID WAS A CLOSURE AND NOT A FINDING AND SHE HAS NOT BEEN ASKED FOR IT TWICE.**
- **THE FIRST HEARING, which is the true one:** the man who does that hall took it as that man being done with, and had a half-formed addition ready and did not make it, and has not raised it since.
- **THE SECOND HEARING:** the man in his sixties took the identical words as being about himself. **HE HAS BEEN ON NOTHING FOR SIX YEARS AND HAS NEVER BEEN THE SUBJECT OF ANYTHING SAID ALOUD IN THAT ROOM, AND HE NOW KNOWS WHAT THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THOSE TWO THINGS FEELS LIKE FROM THE INSIDE.** Nothing had been going on round him and nothing is shut. He will not ask, because the only route to asking runs through saying he thinks she was talking about him.
- **THE GAP NOBODY SAW:** he had come in that afternoon with a question of his own — about how many people go into that hall on a Wednesday — a question he has wanted to ask since the middle of the summer and had twice got as far as the back room door and turned round because the room was full. He went home not knowing that anything at all had been said in that room before he arrived in it from the front.
- **A SENTENCE SAID ONCE IS NOT A POLICY, NOT A MESSAGE AND NOT A STANDING. A REPORT IS NOT A FORM. NOBODY IS ENTERED ON ANYTHING AND BEING TALKED ABOUT IS NOT BEING ASKED ANYTHING.**

## 4. Twelve Saturdays, one block, six accounts

- **MAJOR TURN: A HARD SURFACE WENT DOWN ONE SIDE OF A BLOCK OF FLATS BETWEEN AUGUST AND NOVEMBER, IN THREE PASSES, OUT OF ONE MAN'S OWN WAGES, IN HIS OWN TIME, AND NOBODY STOPPED HIM AND NOBODY ASKED HIM, AND NOW THAT IT IS FINISHED NOT ONE PERSON IN THAT BUILDING CAN SAY WHAT IT WAS SUPPOSED TO BE.**
- **THE WORK:** hardcore a barrow-load at a time, sand and cement mixed by hand, rolled while soft, edges packed with a spade, Saturdays only, about a hundred and ninety pounds and never asked for and never offered.
- **THE TWO COMPLAINTS, AND NEITHER WENT ANYWHERE:** water arriving under a ground-floor back step twice a week, wiped by hand and never stood in the yard about; and a planted bed that had been there since the building was done, moved once on request to the other corner and looked at from a window every morning since.
- **THE NAME HE COULD HAVE GIVEN:** the woman told the man who does floors, in her front room, with tea, on a Wednesday. He had been in that yard the Monday before, for an hour and a half, with a trowel in his hand when he came out of it. **HE COULD HAVE SAID A NAME AT ABOUT THE FOURTH MINUTE AND DID NOT AND IS NEVER GOING TO, AND WHAT STOPPED HIM WAS NOT LOYALTY TO THE MAN: A NAME CARRIED BACK TO A WOMAN WITH A WET STEP MAKES THAT MAN SOMETHING HE HAS NEVER BEEN, AND HE IS ON NOTHING AT ALL AND COULD NOT BE PUT ON A LIST OF ANYBODY'S, AND A MAN WHO PUTS PEOPLE LIKE THAT HAS DONE IT BEFORE.**
- **THE SIX ACCOUNTS:** a path; for the bin men; for the bikes; a waste of good stone laid in October; the mud coming in off the lane; and the fact that nobody can say whether that last one is true, because it depends on what the man was thinking and he has not said. **NO TWO OF THE SIX ARE THE SAME AND NONE OF THEM IS A REASON.**
- **A CHANGE TO A BUILDING IS NOT A PERMISSION AND NOT A CLAIM AND NOT A RESCUE. A PERSON WHO CAN DO A THING IS NOT A PERSON WHO HAS BEEN GIVEN A STANDING TO DO IT.**

## 5. A chest at the back of a shop, and one Friday

- **MAJOR TURN: A WEEKLY ERRAND OF FIVE MONTHS DID NOT HAPPEN ON ONE MORNING, THE MAN WHO WAS DOING IT FOUND OUT AT TEN PAST SIX WITH TWO OTHER PEOPLE ALREADY AT THE COUNTER, A MAN WHO WORKS NIGHTS ASKED FOR ONE AND WAS TOLD NO AND WILL NOT ASK AGAIN, AND NOBODY PUT ANYTHING TO ANYBODY.**
- **WHY IT DID NOT HAPPEN:** a loaded lorry across a yard door, a driver who went off to eat, two hours with the engine off, and no detour for a sack bought elsewhere, because that is not how that errand goes: the sack is somebody else's purchase and what is inside it is not his to pick.
- **THE ONE QUESTION:** asked at about half past four by a man who has bought his ice at that shop for years, in front of the shopkeeper, when the chest was down. He has not put it to her since and buys half a mile further on, where the shop shuts sooner.
- **THE MOMENT:** at ten past six, in the back way, with a bag of plugs, and about ten seconds in which one of the other two could have said something. **NEITHER DID. HE PAID AND WENT OUT INTO THE PARADE.**
- **AFTERWARDS:** she shut the lid and put a cloth on the outside of it and told nobody, and told nobody on the Saturday either. He brought two sacks on the Saturday because a load had come in, and she took one, and the other is in a passage at the back of that shop.
- **A THING NOT BROUGHT IS NOT A REFUSAL AND NOT A DEBT AND NOT A FALLING-OUT. AN ABSENCE THAT IS NOTICED IS NOT AN ACCUSATION AND NOT A QUESTION. NOBODY IS GIVEN A TITLE, A GRADE OR A WAY OF BEING THANKED.**

## 6. A barrow, two men, one question in a gap

- **MAJOR TURN: A BARROW STOOD AT THE BACK OF A SHOP FOR TWELVE DAYS WITH A PRICE ON A CARD, TWO MEN WANTED IT, ONE BOUGHT IT IN FRONT OF THE OTHER ON A PAVEMENT ON THE WEDNESDAY OF THE TWENTY-SECOND OF NOVEMBER, AND FOURTEEN DAYS LATER THE OTHER WAS ASKED A QUESTION IN A GAP AND SAID NO AND HAS SAID NOTHING SINCE.**
- **THE THING:** a builder's barrow, front end squared, tyre new in the summer, a long scratch along one handle, left against what was owed on an account and priced by the shopkeeper below what it was worth. **THE SHOP DOES NOT WANT IT AND HAS NEVER HAD ONE.**
- **THE FIRST MAN:** the Monday of the thirteenth, the Thursday of the sixteenth, the Monday of the twentieth and the Wednesday of the twenty-second, stopping properly at it on the sixteenth and the twentieth, and on the twentieth lifting an edge with his thumb. **HE SAID NOTHING TO ANYBODY AT ANY TIME, BEFORE OR AFTER, AND ON TWO OTHER MORNINGS IN THAT FORTNIGHT HE WENT ROUND THE BACK OF THAT PARADE RATHER THAN GO IN, AND NOBODY IN THAT BOROUGH KNOWS THAT BUT HIM.**
- **THE SECOND MAN:** asked the price, tipped it forward to get at the underneath, said the front end was squared, which is better than a rounded one. Four minutes, and then ten more on the pavement tying it on with the first man walking the length of that parade and not turning round and not being looked at.
- **THE QUESTION IN THE GAP:** a remark about the barrow having gone on the Wednesday, followed by a hope that he had not wanted it, said at a rack fourteen days later because he had paused there for a second. **HE GAVE HER THE ONE-LETTER ANSWER, PAID FOR WHAT HE HAD COME IN FOR, AND WENT OUT. SHE HAS NOT KNOWN SINCE THAT HE STOPPED THERE AT ALL, AND SHE IS NOT GOING TO PUT IT TO HIM, BECAUSE PUTTING IT TO HIM WOULD SAY OUT LOUD THAT SHE HAD BEEN LOOKING.** At a job in the middle of December he has told one man that the shop had had one going and nothing more.
- **WANTING IS NOT CLAIMING AND NOT AN ARRANGEMENT AND NOT A QUEUE AND NOT A RIGHT. NOBODY IS GIVEN A PLACE, A ROW, A SEAT OR A TURN, AND THE ONE WHO WENT WITHOUT IS NOT CROSS AND THE ONE WHO GOT IT IS NOT PROUD.**

## 7. Nine years of a wrong figure

- **MAJOR TURN: A MAN HAS STATED THE WEIGHT OF A SACK OF SAND WRONGLY FOR NINE YEARS AND IT HAS COST NOBODY ANYTHING, THE ONLY CONSEQUENCE IN THAT CHAPTER IS A SPLIT BAG AND IS UNRELATED, AND THE ONE PERSON WHO WORKED IT OUT SAID NOTHING AND IS NOT GOING TO.**
- **WHY IT COSTS NOTHING:** he has never picked one up, and the material is weighed where it is loaded and priced there, so what a sack weighs is not on anybody's bill. Nobody has been cheated, because there is nobody to cheat.
- **THE SPLIT BAG:** a nail standing up out of the bed of the lorry, a bag opened along its length where the nail caught it, and a small part of a sack across the concrete of a yard in November, and it set where it fell. It went back on the stack with a shovel inside five minutes, and the concrete under it is a shade darker than the rest of that apron and has stayed that way. **THE MAN WHO PUT IT THERE SAID IT WAS NOT MUCH AND HE WAS RIGHT, AND THAT IS THE ONLY THING THE CHAPTER SAYS ABOUT IT.**
- **HOW SHE FOUND OUT, BY ACCIDENT:** she goes through that gate four mornings a week because it saves six minutes. She stopped about ten foot inside it with two jugs hooked through each other while a man stood on a stack, and he made a remark to somebody at the foot of the stack about the weight. **SHE BOUGHT THE SAME MATERIAL HERSELF IN THE SUMMER, NINE OF IT, FOR A BAY OF HER OWN FRONT, AND WATCHED IT GO IN FROM HER OWN FRONT WINDOW WITHOUT BEING ABLE TO SEE HOW FAR DOWN IT WENT, AND WORKED OUT INSIDE A FEW SECONDS AT THAT GATE THAT NINE OF THEM COULD NOT HAVE MADE WHAT HE SAYS THEY MAKE.**
- **WHAT SHE DID WITH IT:** nothing. There is no version of telling him that improves anything — he would tell her there is no difference between one of those and another, and carry on shovelling, and she would have walked up that lane for that.
- **A WRONG FIGURE IS NOT A FRAUD AND NOT A DISCOVERY AND NOT A VILLAIN. A NUMBER TWO PEOPLE DISAGREE ABOUT IS NOT A WRONG ANSWER UNTIL SOMEBODY SAYS WHICH IS RIGHT.**

## 8. A stone and no address

- **MAJOR TURN: A PIECE OF AN OLD HEARTH WAS CARRIED UP A STAIR BY TWO MEN WHO COULD NOT TURN IT ON A HALF-LANDING, THEY PUT THE FAR END INTO THE HANDS OF A THIRD MAN WHO WAS IN HIS OWN DOORWAY, THEY PUT IT DOWN OUTSIDE A FLAT WHOSE TENANT IS NOT IN, THEY SAID THEY WOULD COME BACK FOR IT AND DID NOT, AND IT IS AGAINST THE WALL OF THAT HALF-LANDING OPPOSITE HIS OWN DOOR AND HE CANNOT GIVE IT BACK.**
- **WHAT WAS SAID:** four words, to a man with his bag in his hand, and then a statement that the tenant was not in, and then a statement that meant put it off the stair, because a thing left in that passage blocks it both ways.
- **WHY HE CANNOT RETURN IT:** nothing on the stone and nothing on either man, and the only address he has is the flat at the top of that block, with a door that is not being answered and a woman behind it who does not know him. **RETURNING IT WOULD MEAN STANDING ON A LANDING HOLDING SOMETHING HE CANNOT ACCOUNT FOR, AND A MAN WHO GIVES A THING BACK HAS ADMITTED IT WAS NEVER HIS.**
- **WHAT IT DOES TO THAT LANDING:** a foot and a half square against a wall on a landing four foot three across, undressed at the edge, leaving about two foot nine to get past, in the way of his own front door, and the woman who lives across that landing from him has gone past it sideways every evening since the thirtieth of November. **HE COULD HAVE TAKEN IT THROUGH HIS OWN FRONT DOOR AND CLOSED THAT DOOR AND DID NOT.**
- **AND NEITHER OF THEM HAS RAISED IT.** A thing handed over is not a gift, is not the handing on of a claim and is not a rescue, nobody is relieved of anything by it, and a person who has something they did not ask for has not accepted anything.

## 9. Three people, three reasons of their own

- **MAJOR TURN: ONE MAN WAS SEEN ON AN ORDINARY MONDAY BY THREE PEOPLE WHO DID NOT KNOW ABOUT EACH OTHER AND NONE OF WHOM WAS WATCHING HIM, AND NOTHING AT ALL HAPPENED TO HIM AND HE HAS NO IDEA.**
- **HIS DAY:** four hours in him and two of them done, because a house was shut and he waited in the cold at the bottom of a street and then went and did something else. Then work paid in cash, lunch standing up, a small purchase at a counter, an afternoon in a yard, home at about half past seven.
- **THE FIRST:** a shopkeeper, counting her week, noticed a purchase made at that counter for years and not made that Monday, and thought about her order. She has not mentioned it and has not thought about it since.
- **THE SECOND:** a man in his thirties standing on a pavement with nothing to do saw a man he does not know take a short flight of steps in two halves and stop at the bottom. **HE WAS NOT WATCHING HIM, WOULD NOT TELL ANYBODY, AND WOULD NOT GO ROUND SAYING THAT A STRANGER TOOK SOME STEPS IN TWO HALVES.**
- **THE THIRD:** a man in his sixties on a low wall in the sun with a cup, who read nothing into a man stopping in a road and looking upward, and went home and could not describe the man to anybody.
- **BEING SEEN IS NOT A STANDING, IS NOT A DECISION ABOUT ANYBODY AND PUTS NOTHING ON A FORM. NOBODY IS ENTERED ON ANYTHING AND A PERSON WHO IS SEEN DOES NOT KNOW IT AND NEVER WILL.**

## 10. A fortnight, a smell, and a recess at the end of a stair

- **THE BOROUGH IS ORDINARY AND THE FORTNIGHT IS A FORTNIGHT AND IS NOT A TURN OF ANYTHING, AND CARD 0374 IS NOT A CLOSE AND IS NOT CALLED ONE.** shutters up in an order nobody has altered, with the slowest one left to the end of the morning · a shopkeeper on the parade with a pad · a coil of wire and a bag of plugs, and both men in and out twice · a man off nights in that parade · a man in his sixties on a wall for an hour with a cup · a hall on a meter open on the Sunday, ten till four, with about fourteen people through it, a man behind the counter nobody asked anything, more sugar in that urn than a parade would smell of at half past seven, and nothing of the smell itself in that building at all, because it was gone by ten and that door opens at ten · nine people through the fortnight with nothing on them, every one of them holding what the other eight were not, and no afternoon on which one of them said a word to another.
- **THE ONE THING THAT IS DIFFERENT:** a sweet smell that comes into that parade in the mornings, strongest low down, gone by ten, and no more in the afternoon, and no date on it that anybody can stand behind. **TWO PEOPLE CAN DATE IT CLOSELY BECAUSE THEY BEGAN NOTICING IT LATER THAN IT ARRIVED, AND THE ONE MAN WHO HAS WALKED THAT STREET SEVERAL TIMES A DAY FOR MONTHS CANNOT DATE IT AT ALL, AND HAS STOOD IN THE MIDDLE OF IT TWICE ON PURPOSE SINCE THE START OF THE MONTH TRYING TO WORK OUT WHETHER IT WAS THERE A MONTH EARLIER, AND CANNOT, BECAUSE HE WAS THERE EVERY MORNING BEFORE IT AND EVERY MORNING AFTER IT AND THERE IS NOTHING TO SORT THEM BY.**
- **THREE EXPLANATIONS, NONE OF WHICH FITS:** a flat above that shop; a pipe on that side; and the weather, which it is not. Nobody has gone to that door and the woman who runs the shop has not said who lives there.
- **THE FINDING, AND IT IS SMALL:** it does not matter and it is there, and nobody has turned anything round over it.
- **THE FOUR ANSWERS, GIVEN AT ONE COUNTER IN ABOUT TEN MINUTES BY THREE PEOPLE WHO EACH HAD A POINT:** a line in a book, because a book does not argue; a thing two men can both stand in front of and see, which needs nothing written about it; nothing at all, ever, because whatever gets proved in this town will turn out to be a small thing, and by then every person alive who could have said otherwise will have gone; and the first one proved being a thing somebody was told about before anybody laid eyes on it, arriving in about four mouths. **THE FOUR CANNOT BE SET AGAINST ONE ANOTHER, BECAUSE NONE OF THEM IS ABOUT THE SAME SORT OF THING AS THE OTHER THREE. THE QUESTION IS STILL A QUESTION AND NOBODY ANSWERED IT ANYWHERE IN THAT FORTNIGHT.**
- **AND ONE MAN STOPPED IN A CORRIDOR:** he went up the outside concrete steps of that building for about an hour's work and, coming back down, stopped at the end of a corridor where the cold off the yard was coming in. Off that end there is an alcove with a door in it that has never latched and it stands open, and a book on a shelf inside it with the covers turned to the inside of that door, at nineteen entries, the last of them concerning a lamp outside a yard, entered a couple of Novembers back as lost against a heading somebody held open for that sort of loss, with nothing under it, and the paper on that page giving out a long way short of the foot of the volume. **A LINE UNDER THAT LAST ENTRY HAS BEEN BLANK FOR ONE THOUSAND ONE HUNDRED AND SEVEN DAYS. HE DID NOT GO IN AND IS NOT GOING TO AND NOBODY COUNTED ANYTHING ON THAT STAIR, AND THE FIGURE IS A FACT ABOUT A LINE IN A BOOK AND NOT A COUNT BY ANY PERSON.**

## 11. Still open, and still forbidden to Continuation 0019

Nothing in Volume 04 has been resolved, undone, improved on, restated or answered, and nothing in Batches 0001 to 0005 or in Continuations 0006 to 0018 may be. Nobody renews the order, nobody expires it, nobody renames the blank term, nobody puts a name in the line on page two, nobody fills the empty square, Roy Albery does not walk again, nobody dies, nobody is rescued by chance, nobody walks again, the eleven refusals are not twelve, the counter in the vestibule answers nothing and was not entered and was in no scene, the rota is not rebuilt, the second line under Bram Osei's Thursday is not looked at, the register does not move, the letter, the card, the page, the printed sheets, the column, the shop-window card, the crate with a lid and the four bottles all stand, the drawer under the counter in the vestibule is not opened, is not counted, is not asked about and is not mentioned, **AND THE WORD *DRAWER* IS AT ZERO IN ALL TEN CHAPTERS OF 0018 AND NO CHAPTER NEEDED A DRAWER**, and the compartment under the trade counter is in no chapter of that batch and holds two sheets and neither has been out since the nineteenth of July. **THE QUIET CUT, THE CIVIC ERASURE, THE ORIGIN OF THE COMMUNITY-WATCH TERM, THE THREE-LINE BRASS TOKENS, THE FIRST CHARTER, THE PROXY, THE ROOT CHAMBER, THE LOWGLASS FLOOR, THE BORROWED CITY AND THE NINE HINGES ARE NOT SPENT. FRANCES TOLLEY IS NOT NAMED AND THE READING RULE IS NOT USED. PRUE CALLOWAY'S FINDING IS NOT OPENED AGAIN AND THE CLAIM TO OPEN A DOOR IS SPENT. ## 1. A worktop edge nobody asked for

- **MAJOR TURN: A MAN CAME TO A KITCHEN FOR A WEEPING JOINT AND FOUND THE FRONT EDGE OF THE WORKTOP GONE SOFT, AND HE TOOK IT OFF AND CUT A NEW PIECE AND PUT IT BACK, AND SHE WAS ON A SHIFT WHEN HE CAME AND HE WAS GONE AGAIN BEFORE SHE GOT IN, AND THE ONLY WORD SAID IN THAT KITCHEN THAT MORNING WAS ONE WORD FROM THE MAN WHO LIVES IN IT, AND HE WENT OFF TO HIS OWN WORK ON IT, AND NEITHER OF THEM HAS MENTIONED IT SINCE.**
- **WHO IS CARRYING WHAT:** the tradesman is carrying the knowledge that he put in a piece of work nobody ordered, and he has not told anybody, and no man who works alongside him knows. The man of that house is carrying a piece of wood he never asked to be given him and did not notice until he got in that evening, and the one question he asked that afternoon was about the tiles behind it and had nothing to do with the wood. The woman of that house is carrying nothing at all, has not been told, and has not asked.
- **WHY NOBODY WILL RAISE IT:** nobody in that house would ring a tradesman to say he had cut something extra for them, and the tradesman would have to open the subject himself, and he gains nothing by it.

## 2. A chest with a lid, in a man's front room

- **MAJOR TURN: A MAN WALKING PAST A MAN WITH BOTH HANDS FULL PUT A TEA CHEST INTO THE CROOK OF HIS ARM AND CARRIED ON AT THE SAME PACE AND SAID NOTHING, AND THE MAN WITH THE CHEST COULD NOT HAVE STOPPED HIM AND DID NOT, AND HE STILL HAS IT AND IS NOT GOING TO ASK.**
- **WHY HE WILL NOT ASK:** to ask he would have to stand in a street and say that somebody handed him something he never asked for, and a stranger handing a man something and walking on leaves that man holding a debt he never agreed to. **IT IS NOT A MYSTERY HE IS TRYING TO SOLVE AND HE IS NOT TRYING.**
- **THE OTHER SIDE:** the man who set it down was clearing a house for a woman who is not named in this account, and he put it in the space there was because the man's arm was full, and has not wondered about it once since. The chest went into a garage in a terrace two streets off, and the man who carried it out does not know whose it is, and it is not going anywhere.
- **WHAT IS ON IT:** about half of a stencilled word and part of a fifth letter, worn over once. He has not tried to make out what it said.

## 3. One hour of the morning that two men want

- **MAJOR TURN: TWO MEN WANT TO KNOW WHAT TIME THAT SHOP OPENS ITS DOOR IN THE MORNING, AND ONE OF THEM COULD GET IT FROM HER AND ONE COULD GET IT FROM THE OTHER, AND NEITHER ASKS EITHER, AND SHE ANSWERED IT TWICE IN THAT ROOM IN FRONT OF BOTH OF THEM AND NEITHER OF THE TWO HEARD IT AS AN ANSWER.**
- **HOW EACH HEARD IT:** one of them took a person being in early and let the door go past him, and the other took a woman in a bad mood on her feet and did not follow it, and the hour itself went past both of them. **THE FACT IS STILL IN THE ROOM AND STILL AVAILABLE TO BOTH OF THEM.**
- **THE TWO ROUTES, AND NEITHER TAKEN:** the man in his forties to her, on a Wednesday, in a room with three men sitting in it. The man who works nights to the man in his forties, who would give an answer to a question put as a statement, which neither of them has ever managed to do on a weekday. **WANTING TO KNOW IS NOT ASKING AND BEING ASKED NOTHING IS NOT A THING ANYBODY MAY COMPLAIN ABOUT.**

## 4. A landing that went dark at four o'clock

- **MAJOR TURN: A LIGHT ON A LANDING IN A BLOCK OF SEVEN CAME ON AN HOUR AND A HALF EARLIER THAN IT HAD BEEN COMING ON, AND THREE PEOPLE IN THAT BLOCK WORKED OUT THREE DIFFERENT REASONS FOR IT INSIDE A WEEK AND TOLD NOBODY, AND THE MAN WHO HAD THE KEYS WALKED UP THAT STAIR FOUR DAYS LATER WITH HIS OWN HAND ON THE WALL AND LOOKED UP AT THE FITTING AND WENT ON.**
- **THE THREE, AND WHY EACH IS SILENT:** the woman in the first flat has gone at the clock twice and is not going to say so out loud, because the second she says it she has admitted she has not put her hand on it. The man in his thirties has decided for himself that the bulb in that fitting is at the end of its life, and has kept that to himself, because it is not his stair and it is not his bulb and he is not going to be the man who says a thing like that about somebody else's. The man in his sixties decided what he was looking at before he had finished looking at it, and a man of his age does not take that back in front of a cup of tea.
- **THE CONSEQUENCE:** it goes on being different. Four evenings of that stair in the dark and one of them said one word out loud on the bottom step, to nobody. **A FAULT IS NOT A FINDING UNTIL SOMEBODY SAYS WHICH OF TWO THINGS IT IS, AND NOBODY HAS SAID, AND NOBODY WAS ASKED ANYTHING.**

## 5. One no, at the kerb, and no second attempt

- **MAJOR TURN: A MAN IN HIS THIRTIES OFFERED A CHEST FREEZER ONCE, ON A MORNING IN LATE DECEMBER, TO A MAN IN HIS FORTIES, AND THE ANSWER WAS ONE WORD WITH NOTHING BEHIND IT, AND THE FREEZER WENT BACK IN THE PICKUP AND THE TAILGATE WENT UP.**
- **WHAT WAS NOT SAID:** no reason from either of them, then or since. The man in his thirties did not go and put it to a second person, and the reason is not a decision he took at the time. The reason is not a decision he took at the time. One refusal from that man is enough for a man like him, and going to somebody else afterwards is the part of it that costs.
- **WHO WAS NEAR ENOUGH TO HEAR:** nobody. Behind that counter, on the morning of that refusal, she had her back to her own window with a local radio going on the shelf above the till, and there were two people in the shop and then there was one, and she waited until the pickup had gone up the street before she looked out, and by then there was nothing there to see. **SHE HAS NEVER PUT IT TO EITHER OF THEM AND IS NOT GOING TO, AND SHE COULD NOT PUT IT TO EITHER OF THEM WITHOUT ITS BEING ABOUT SOMEBODY SHE KNOWS NOTHING AT ALL, AND SHE IS NOT GOING TO STAND IN A STREET ASKING A MAN WHY HE IS CARRYING SOMETHING.**
- **WHERE IT IS:** behind a low wall in his own yard, where it is, and it stops him getting at the other side of his own yard, and no arrangement exists and nobody is owed anything and nobody has been asked anything.

## 6. A cold morning and a machine, an hour and a bit apart

- **MAJOR TURN: TWO SMALL THINGS FAILED ON ONE MAN ON ONE DAY. HE STRAIGHTENED BOTH OF THEM HIMSELF INSIDE ABOUT A MINUTE EACH AND TOLD NEITHER. A MAN IN HIS THIRTIES STOOD THROUGH THE FIRST IN THE STREET AND THEN STOOD AT THE END OF THE COUNTER THROUGH THE SECOND AND SPOKE TO NEITHER OF THEM.**
- **THE FIRST, AT TEN PAST NINE:** his van would not start and he turned it over five times and the fifth time it did. Nothing is wrong with a van for that. The man in his thirties was thirty foot off with a bin he had just put out, and he watched the whole business of that van being turned over five times, and he stayed on that kerb until it went, and he did not go into that shop and say one word about it to anybody, and he did not put his face away either.
- **THE SECOND, AT A QUARTER PAST TEN:** the machine on the counter would not take his card and did the two buzzes three times, and he paid in money, and it took as long as the van had taken.
- **AND NEITHER WAS TOLD, ANYWHERE:** the man in his thirties has told the man with the van nothing and the woman at the till nothing and has not put the two failures near each other in his own head, and if it were said to him he would say that things break. **TWO THINGS THAT HAPPEN TO A MAN ARE NOT A PATTERN AND A BODY IS NOT A SET OF FACTS.**

## 7. Six days on a landing, and two people on the same morning

- **MAJOR TURN: TWO MEN PUT A CHEST OUT ONTO A LANDING TO GET A FLOOR UP IN A ROOM, AND LEFT IT THERE OVER THE SUNDAY, THE MONDAY, THE TUESDAY, THE WEDNESDAY, THE THURSDAY AND THE FRIDAY, AND ON THAT FRIDAY IT WENT OUT IN A PICKUP WITH NOBODY ASKED, AND ON THE SATURDAY MORNING AFTERWARDS THE WOMAN WHO LIVES ON THAT LANDING AND THE MAN WHO WORKS NIGHTS STOOD AT THE SAME END OF IT LOOKING AT THE MARK IT LEFT AND NEITHER SAID ANYTHING.**
- **WHY NOBODY ASKED IN SIX DAYS:** the men who put it down were there to lift a floor and were paid for that, and the four people who lived on that landing had no reason in the world to be interested in a box somebody had shifted out of a flat, and not one of the four of them opened a door.
- **WHY THE TWO DID NOT SPEAK:** she was at her own end with her back to him and did not turn round. He was at the other end for a paper and did not look at her. They were looking at the same two foot of paper from eleven foot apart on the same morning and neither of them knows the other was there.
- **WHERE IT WENT:** a short drive to a yard he keeps at the top of the town, under a sheet of roofing felt. It does not belong to him and he never found out whose it was, and he was in that building for ten minutes and knocked on none of the four doors. **TAKING A THING IS NOT THEFT AND IS NOT A FAVOUR AND A THING GONE IS NOT A DISAPPEARANCE AND A DISAPPEARANCE IS NOT A MYSTERY TO BE SOLVED.**

## 8. Five words on a stair, and a man who thought he was understood

- **MAJOR TURN: A MAN IN HIS SIXTIES SAID FIVE WORDS IN A PASSAGE WHILE A MAN IN HIS THIRTIES WENT PAST HIM, AND MEANT A MAN FOUR STREETS AWAY, AND THE MAN IN HIS THIRTIES TOOK THEM AS BEING ABOUT A MAN ON THE FLOOR ABOVE HIM AND WAS RIGHT, AND THE MAN WHO SAID THEM WENT HOME THAT DAY BELIEVING THE OTHER ONE HAD UNDERSTOOD, AND HE WAS NEVER TOLD OTHERWISE.**
- **WHY HE SAID IT:** he had it going round in his own head since he got up that morning, and it came out of him on his own, not to anybody, at the moment when somebody was going past.
- **WHY THE OTHER MAN HEARD IT CORRECTLY:** a man on that landing had told him in December that there would be no more work coming his way, and nothing else in that block had been the subject of a word in a fortnight.
- **THE MISREADING, WHICH WAS THE SPEAKER'S:** somebody answering with nothing is somebody who has understood, and that is how a man of his age has read every reply he has ever had. **HE HAS NEVER ASKED WHETHER IT WENT IN AND HE IS NOT GOING TO, AND NEITHER OF THEM WILL EVER MENTION IT AGAIN AND NEITHER WILL EVER KNOW.**

## 9. A wall that is better than the yard has always said

- **MAJOR TURN: A MAN WHO HAS TRADED OUT OF THAT YARD FOR LONGER THAN THE OTHER MAN HAS BEEN IN IT SAYS THAT A CLASS OF WALL WILL NOT TAKE A SCREW AND PUTS THOSE IN FOR EVERY FIXING, AND THE OTHER MAN FOUND THAT ONE OF HIS OWN WOULD NOT COME OUT AND FOUND OUT WHY, AND TOLD NOBODY.**
- **WHAT HE FOUND:** a resin plug that had gone right round the screw and set hard, on a wall that is the hardest thing in that yard, with a furring batten on it that is what he was fixing into in the first place and not the wall at all.
- **WHY HE SAID NOTHING:** there is no case to put, because the older man is right about a great many walls, and the only way to settle it is both of them standing over the same piece of work, and there is nothing standing at the moment, and nobody in that yard could be asked where he got it.
- **WHAT IT COST:** nothing. Every plate, bracket, shelf, cupboard and sign he has put into a wall of that kind since the summer is where a fitter would want it, and none of them is going to move, and no job in this borough is coming back in a year over a plug. **HE WILL CARRY THE GUN UP THE LADDER NEXT MONTH AND WILL SAY THE SAME THING HE HAS ALWAYS SAID, AND EVERYTHING HE HAS BUILT ON IT IS FINE.**

## 10. A fortnight, and a line nobody can explain

- **MAJOR TURN: NOTHING IN THAT FORTNIGHT WAS DIFFERENT FROM THE FORTNIGHT BEFORE IT, THE FOUR ANSWERS GIVEN AT THAT COUNTER IN DECEMBER ARE STILL GOING ROUND AND CANNOT BE PUT BESIDE ONE ANOTHER, NOBODY ANSWERED ANYTHING, AND THE ONE THING IN THAT BOROUGH THAT NOBODY COULD EXPLAIN IF THEY WERE ASKED IS THE SAME ONE IT WAS A FORTNIGHT AGO.**
- **THE ROUND, UNCHANGED:** shutters in an unaltered order with the last one at the top left to the end of the morning · a counter from ten to nine with the order on for the Friday · a man off nights up that parade before the shops are open, which is what he has done instead of lying there since the beginning of December, and into it again in the afternoon · a man in his sixties on a low wall for about an hour with a cup · a hall on a meter on the Saturday morning with the urn on, about sixteen people through it, and a man behind the counter that nobody put anything to · a man who did an hour's work on a Thursday and came back down a warm stair and stopped in a corridor · a sweet smell under that awning in the mornings and gone by ten, which nobody on that parade has ever raised with anybody else and which nobody can put a date to.
- **THE FOUR ANSWERS:** still four, still given by people who each had a point, still not about the same sort of thing as one another. On a Wednesday in that fortnight one of those men said in a shop that it was still not settled and the other said no, and neither said which of the four he held, and the woman at the till said nothing.
- **AND THE LINE, WHICH IS THE FINDING AND WHICH IS SMALL:** the book on that shelf stands at nineteen entries and nobody has added a twentieth, and the nineteenth is a report of a lamp outside a yard, written a couple of Novembers ago by somebody who was told, and put under a heading that was left open for the next thing of that sort, and nothing has gone under it since, and there is paper left for a good many more lines before the volume would end. **NOBODY HAS PUT A FIGURE AGAINST IT IN THE DAYS SINCE, AND THE ONE MAN IN THAT BOROUGH WHO COULD HAVE PUT ONE THERE BY COUNTING DID NOT COUNT, AND THE ALCOVE DOOR IS STILL OPEN AND NOTHING ON THAT SHELF HAS BEEN TOUCHED BY ANYBODY. NOBODY IN THAT BOROUGH COULD TELL YOU WHAT THE RULE UNDER THAT LAST LINE IS FOR.**

## 1. A tin of grease that is not on a bench

- **MAJOR TURN: A MAN WENT BACK TO A YARD FOR A TIN OF GREASE LEFT BEHIND ON A CONCRETE BENCH AND IT WAS NOT THERE AND HE SAID NOTHING TO THE MAN WHO SWEEPS THAT YARD ABOUT IT, AND HE TOOK A CRATE OF APPLES THAT WAS ON THAT BENCH INSTEAD WITHOUT ASKING ANYBODY ANYTHING, AND CARRIED IT OUT OF THE GATE IN FRONT OF THE MAN WHO WAS WATCHING HIM, AND HAS SAID NOTHING SINCE.**
- **WHO IS CARRYING WHAT:** the man in his forties is carrying a fortnight of not having said anything, and he cannot put a reason on it that would survive being said out loud. The man who keeps that yard is carrying nothing at all — he was thirty foot away with a broom, he watched a stranger walk out with a crate, and he has not wondered about it since.
- **WHY NEITHER WILL RAISE IT:** a tin of grease is worth about two pounds ten and asking after it is a question about a person he does not know. A man who is asked would say he had not seen it and that would be the end of it and the other man would be exactly where he was. Neither man has anything to gain and both would lose the thing they are not saying.
- **WHERE THE CRATE WENT:** a kerb on his own street, gone by two o'clock on the fifth of February, and he does not know who has it.

## 2. A question that was answered once and went nowhere

- **MAJOR TURN: THE WOMAN WHO RUNS A SHOP OFF THAT PARADE ASKED A MAN IN HIS FORTIES, ONCE, WHETHER THERE IS ANYBODY IN THIS TOWN WHO CAN LOOK AT A BELL IN HER OWN SHOPFRAME, AND HE ANSWERED IN ONE SENTENCE THAT HE HAS NEVER HAD ONE DONE, AND WHAT HE SAID WAS TRUE.**
- **WHAT SHE DID WITH IT:** nothing. She did not ask him a second time, including on a Saturday when he was at the counter and the number was in her apron pocket. She has not rung anybody else, including the man the card she tore up was for. She has told nobody that she asked.
- **WHO ELSE HEARD IT:** a man in his thirties, at the far end of that counter, with his back half turned. He has put it to neither of them. He has not made it a thing the two of them share and he is not going to.
- **WHAT HE DOES NOT KNOW:** that a second person was near enough to take any of it in. He was facing a counter with a woman in it and a bell over his head and he did not turn round.

## 3. A churn on a ledge and two reasons that do not meet

- **MAJOR TURN: A MAN IN HIS THIRTIES COULD NOT GET A BICYCLE PAST A CHURN ON A LEDGE IN A SHARED BACK PASSAGE AND A MAN IN HIS SIXTIES CAME OUT THROUGH A GATE ABOUT TEN FOOT OFF AT THE SAME MOMENT, AND NEITHER OF THEM SAID A WORD, AND IT IS STILL ON THAT LEDGE.**
- **THE TWO REASONS, WHICH ARE NOT THE SAME:** the man in his thirties wants it off that ledge because it is in the way of a thing he has to move and he loses a quarter of an hour going round. The man in his sixties wants it gone because it belongs to him and it is sitting on masonry that does not, and he will not be the one who bends in the wet in a shared passage for something that can be carried in four seconds.
- **WHAT NEITHER HAS DONE:** neither has mentioned it to anybody, and the man in his thirties has been down that passage about six times since and has gone round it every time.
- **WHERE IT ENDS:** on that ledge, in that passage, in the rain, with nobody in this borough who could say why neither of them moved it.

## 4. A floor laid in a room that is not a flat

- **MAJOR TURN: A MAN IN HIS FORTIES LAID JUST UNDER THIRTY SQUARE FOOT OF CHIPBOARD AND SHEET VINYL OVER THE FLOOR OF AN UNLET ROOM AT THE HEAD OF A STAIR IN A BUILDING HE HAS NO CONNECTION WITH, AND A WOMAN WHO HAS THE FLAT BELOW SAW HIM DOING IT AND SAID NOTHING TO HIM AND TO NOBODY ELSE, AND HE IS NOT TOLD THAT ANYBODY KNOWS.**
- **WHY THE ROOM:** a woman who lets that block asked him in a corridor in November to keep it shut. He has a bench in it. He cannot have it at his own place. There is no money in it and nothing in writing.
- **WHY SHE SAID NOTHING:** any sentence she could use would come out as a complaint, and the day she uses one is the day that room is in front of somebody with a say over it. She has been in that block nine years and she wants the man out of her part of it, which he has been.
- **WHERE THE FLOOR IS:** thirty square foot of hardboard and vinyl in a room nine foot by seven, and the man in his forties was back in that block on the Thursday after for half a day's work in one of the flats and was not spoken to differently by anybody.

## 5. Two rails in one outbuilding, thirteen inches apart

- **MAJOR TURN: TWO MEN PUT UP A RAIL INSIDE THE SAME BUILDING IN THE SAME WINTER, ONE AT ABOUT FIVE FOOT AND ONE AT ABOUT SIX FOOT TWO, THREE WEEKS OR LESS APART, AND NEITHER KNOWS ABOUT THE OTHER, AND A WOMAN WENT IN THERE AND SAW ONE OF THEM.**
- **WHY EACH IS RIGHT:** the lower rail is at the height a man of a certain age can get his own things down off, and it is on brackets that hook over the brick so that nothing goes into the wall at all. The upper rail is above a bench two foot deep that has not been built yet, and it is on brackets that do go into the brick.
- **WHY NEITHER WOULD CALL THE OTHER A MISTAKE:** they are at different heights for different reasons and neither is in the way of the other, and two men using a building neither of them owns is what happens.
- **WHAT THE WOMAN SAW:** a rail, two brackets, three hooks, a bag on one hook and a coil of cable on another. The lower one. The sheets are leaning in front of the upper one and it is not a thing anybody sees from the front of that building.

## 6. A chair that does not wobble and nobody who knows

- **MAJOR TURN: A MAN IN HIS FORTIES CARRIED A CHAIR OUT OF A MAN'S FRONT ROOM TO GET AT THE BOARDS BEHIND IT, PUT IT BACK INSIDE THE HOUR, FOUND A LOOSE LEG AND A SHORT LEG, PUT A PIECE OF THE RUG'S BACKING UNDER THAT LEG, KNOCKED THE JOINT DOWN TWICE, AND TOLD NOBODY.**
- **THE FLOOR:** there was nothing the matter with it. It had lifted where a joist had shrunk, and a strip of the rug's stiff packing under the board brought it down again in about eight minutes, and the boards were true all the way when he put his eye on them.
- **WHAT THE MAN IN HIS SIXTIES DID:** came in at about ten past one, sat down in it, and noticed nothing at all. He would tell anybody who asked him that there had never been anything the matter with that chair, and he would not be lying, because from where he has always sat there never was.
- **WHAT THE MAN IN HIS FORTIES DID WITH IT:** put it back, and was particular about the mark in the dust on the brick and moved the leg about half an inch to get it right, and then said nothing to the woman behind the counter at the bottom of that street, before or after.
- **WHAT THE WOMAN AT THE SHOP DID WITH IT:** put the two of those facts together inside about four seconds and then carried on with what she was doing. She has said none of it to the man in his sixties and does not mean to, and she has not put a question to the man in his forties about that morning either.

## 7. A minute and a half at a counter, and two true facts that do not meet

- **MAJOR TURN: TWO MEN ARGUED ABOUT A PATCH OF PLASTER THAT CAME DOWN OUT OF A CEILING, EACH GAVE ONE THING THAT WAS TRUE, NEITHER GAVE THE OTHER ANYTHING, NEITHER CONCEDED, AND IT WAS LEFT AS IT IS.**
- **THE FIRST TRUE FACT:** the boards behind that corner were damp with a dark line along the bottom of them before the man in his forties ever took the old plaster off.
- **THE SECOND TRUE FACT:** the plaster was soft under the new lath at the corner, a fortnight before the lath had been in a month, and the man in his thirties put his thumb in it and said so.
- **WHY NEITHER GAVE THE OTHER:** the first would have had to say his own work had held four months; the second would have had to say he saw the damp in December and said nothing then because he had a tap to do. Neither of those is available in a shop on a Wednesday afternoon.
- **WHERE IT IS LEFT:** about two foot of open lath in a corner ceiling, a plastic sheet hooked over a rail, and two men who stood about two foot apart at that counter twice in the week after and said nothing.

## 8. A tin handed over in a street, and a question that got an answer to a different question

- **MAJOR TURN: A MAN IN HIS SIXTIES PUT A TIN INTO A MAN IN HIS FORTIES' HAND IN THE MIDDLE OF A SENTENCE ABOUT SOMETHING ELSE, AND THE MAN IN HIS FORTIES CARRIED IT ABOUT FOR FOUR DAYS AND PUT IT BACK ON THAT LEDGE WHEN THE OTHER MAN WAS NOT THERE, AND NEITHER OF THEM HAS MENTIONED IT.**
- **WHERE IT CAME FROM:** the top of a wardrobe in the giver's front bedroom, with about nine other things on it, since about 2014, out of a house he did a day's work in. He picked it up off that wardrobe instead of the cap he had gone into that room for, and did not register what he was holding until the other man's hand came under it.
- **THE ONE QUESTION AND THE REPLY:** he asked where it came from and was told it was up in the house, which answers where and not why, and he did not ask why.
- **WHAT HE DID WITH IT:** nothing. He did not open it. It was on a shelf in his van and on the seat and in the footwell.
- **WHAT THE OTHER MAN DID WITH IT:** took it off the ledge on the Wednesday, put it in his pocket, and put it back on the wardrobe. He had not known the tin was in his hand at all until the other man's fingers were closing on it.

## 9. A box put down on a table and not asked about by anybody

- **MAJOR TURN: A MAN IN HIS FORTIES PUT A BOX ON A TABLE IN A ROOM AT THE BACK OF A SHOP, SAID NOTHING TO THE THREE PEOPLE IN IT, WENT AT ABOUT FIVE O'CLOCK, AND HAS NOT BEEN BACK INTO THAT ROOM.**
- **WHY HE CARRIED IT FOR A FORTNIGHT:** there was not one moment in fourteen days when he was standing at the back of that van with his hands free and somewhere to put it. It came out of a house on the Cleeve road on the fifteenth of January and has not worked since.
- **WHAT EACH OF THE THREE DID:** the man who works nights moved his bag of ice about six inches under the table. The woman who works in a shop put her elbow nearer it and later put her cup on it because that was the flat place. The man in his sixties did not look at it once.
- **WHY NONE OF THEM WILL ASK:** anything any of them said would be about him rather than about the box, and all three worked that out in about four seconds when it went down.
- **WHERE IT IS:** on that table, where the four of them can reach it, and the man who put it there comes along that counter and out of the front and does not use the hatch.

## 10. A fortnight in which one man was fifty-five minutes late for nothing

- **MAJOR TURN: THE BOROUGH WAS ORDINARY ON THE THIRD OF MARCH AND A GATE OFF A SIDE TURNING KEPT A MAN WAITING FOR ABOUT TEN MINUTES BECAUSE HE HAD TURNED UP FIFTY-FIVE MINUTES AFTER THE HOUR HE HAD IN HIS OWN HEAD FOR SOMETHING NOBODY HAD ASKED HIM TO COME FOR, AND NEITHER MAN SAID ANYTHING ABOUT IT.**
- **THE TWO THINGS THAT ARE WRONG AND STAY WRONG:** a shutter at the top of that parade that has been sitting about a foot above the pavement since the twelfth of February, which the man who puts shutters up lifts twice every morning; and a paving slab in the middle of that parade that has lifted an inch and a half across the whole footway. Both have been reported to nobody.
- **THE ROUND, UNCHANGED:** shutters in an unaltered order · a counter from ten with the order in for the Friday and shut at half past three on the Saturday · a man off nights up that parade at about seven and into it again in the afternoon · a man in his sixties on a low wall for about an hour with a cup · a hall on a meter on the Saturday morning with the urn on and about twenty people through it and a man behind a table that nobody put anything to · about nine people on that parade and not one of them carrying anything for anybody else.
- **AND THE LINE, WHICH IS STILL THE SAME:** a book in a block by the water with nineteen entries in it, and a space under the last of them, empty now across one thousand one hundred and ninety-three days, and nobody counted it that day or this month, and nobody has stood in that room, and there is nobody in that borough who could say what that heading is there to record.
