# VOLUME 05 OPEN THREADS — after Continuation 0021, Chapter 404

**Read with the "VOLUME 05, CONTINUATION 0021 — CHAPTERS 395–404" block at the end of `state/continuity.md`, which carries the canon for these ten chapters and governs wherever the two differ, and with the Continuation 0020 block above it, which still governs everything those ten chapters did. **VOLUME 05 IS NOT CLOSED AND IS NOT DECLARED CLOSED. THE SERIES IS AT 404 OF 720. NOTHING IN CONTINUATION 0021 RESOLVED ANYTHING AND NOTHING IN IT MAY BE UNDONE, IMPROVED ON, RESTATED OR ANSWERED. EVERY DAY-COUNT BELOW IS CALCULATED FROM ITS OWN ANCHOR ON THE DAY IN QUESTION AND NOT CARRIED FORWARD FROM A SUMMARY: at Wednesday 18 April 2018 the blank line under the nineteenth is one thousand two hundred and thirty-nine days, the card in the slot is one thousand one hundred and fifty-three, and the letter in the tray is one thousand one hundred and fifty-five.**

## 1. A door that two men packed, and the paper still in the hinge

- **MAJOR TURN: THE MAN IN HIS THIRTIES TOOK THE TOP HINGE OFF THAT DOOR ON THE FOURTH OF MARCH AND FOUND A TORN STRIP OF BROWN PAPER PACKED IN THE KNUCKLE AND TOUCH-UP PAINT ON THE FRAME THAT WAS NOT THE PAINT AROUND IT, AND HE PUT THE PAPER BACK AND DID HIS OWN REPAIR AND SAID NOTHING.**
- **WHAT HE WORKED OUT, IN ABOUT FORTY SECONDS:** that whoever had been there had packed two hinges and not one, had not touched the wrong side, had used the paint that was standing on that landing because there was nothing else on that landing, and had been in and out in half an hour. That nobody had told the woman who has the letting that a man had been up that stair.
- **WHAT EACH OF THEM DID NEXT:** he shifted both hinges about three-eighths of an inch instead, which is the other way of doing the same job, and put two inch screws in. The paper is still in that bottom hinge.
- **WHY NEITHER WILL RAISE IT:** the man in his forties has not been in that building since February and is not going back. The man in his thirties went down that stair with his bag and said nothing and has not mentioned that door to anybody.

## 2. Crosses on a wall, and four more by the end of the month

- **MAJOR TURN: HE FOUND ABOUT THIRTY PENCIL CROSSES ON THE PLASTER BEHIND A BATTEN HE HAD TAKEN OFF A WALL IN A CELLAR, AND HE WENT BACK TWICE AFTER THE JOB WAS FINISHED AND DID NOTHING AT ALL ON EITHER OF THOSE TWO VISITS, AND HE STILL CANNOT SAY WHAT THEY ARE.**
- **WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE:** a column, four inch apart, half an inch across, one arm of each blunt because the pencil was sharpened with a knife. Six under a coat of pink distemper and showing through it. Eighteen faded to the colour of the plaster. Four on the top coat and about four days old when he first saw them. A pencil stub about two inch long is stuck in a joint of the brick at the height of the sixth one up.
- **WHAT HE HAS DONE ABOUT IT:** nothing, and he has not even done that on paper. There was four more at the top of that column when he looked on the last Thursday of March and five more when he looked on the second of April, and he has not written the number down, and he has not got it in words, and if he were asked about it the whole of the answer would be that he was chasing a stack and that the key came to him from the woman who works in a shop.
- **WHO HE HAS NOT ASKED:** the man in his sixties, who goes down into that cellar most days and has never been in it with anybody, and who has not asked him why there is a batten off that wall. **AND THE FLAG FOR 0022: THIS IS A COLUMN OF MARKS AND NOT A CODE, AND 0022 MAY NOT TURN IT INTO ONE, MAY NOT COUNT IT AGAIN AND MAY NOT GIVE ANYBODY THE SATISFACTION OF A SOLUTION.**

## 3. Nine foot of new brickwork, and the man who read it from twenty foot

- **MAJOR TURN: TWO MEN WORKED OPPOSITE SIDES OF THE SAME BUILDING IN THE SAME MORNING AND WERE ABOUT TWENTY FEET APART FOR NINETY SECONDS WITHOUT EITHER LOOKING UP, AND THE ONE WHO CAME BACK AT HALF PAST THREE READ A NINE FOOT LINE OF CHAMFERED ARRISES AND KNEW WHOSE THEY WERE IN ABOUT TWO SECONDS.**
- **WHAT EACH HAD DONE:** the man in his thirties put a new hardwood shop door and frame in on the front, made by him, with four raised squares in it. The man in his forties took the top course off a boundary wall in the yard behind and built it again and re-did the coping, which the woman who works in a shop asked him about in February.
- **WHY HE KNEW:** he has watched the man in his forties cut brick four times in two years and has heard him say once, unprompted, that a sharp edge on a cut brick takes the suction off it. Nobody else he has built alongside knocks the arris off a cut.
- **WHAT NEITHER WILL DO:** he told nobody. The man in his forties knows the front was done because the shop has a new door on it and everybody on that parade knows it.

## 4. Four rods, asked for and given up

- **MAJOR TURN: A WOMAN WITH THE KEYS TO A HOUSE THAT IS BEING EMPTIED ASKED THE MAN IN HIS FORTIES FOR FOUR BRASS STAIR RODS HE HAD HAD IN A BAG ON A LEDGE SINCE MAY 2015 AND HE PUT THEM INTO HER HAND INSIDE ABOUT TEN SECONDS.**
- **WHERE THEY CAME FROM:** out of the hall of a house off that parade in 2015, off the stair, in a bag with about nine other things, because the treads had to come up. He said nothing to the woman of that house and she said nothing to him. She is in a home and has not been told.
- **WHAT SHE SAID:** two sentences, one of them a question about a house she did not name, and one of them after. She wrote nothing down and took them out in a carrier bag.
- **WHAT EACH HAS DONE WITH IT:** nothing. He has not said a word to anybody and the bag is still on that ledge and lighter by about two pounds. The man in his thirties was at the door with his bag for about nine minutes of it, did not turn round, and has not been asked what he saw.

## 5. A wall pointed on a Saturday and raked out on a Wednesday

- **MAJOR TURN: A MAN IN HIS FORTIES REPOINTED NINE FOOT OF A NORTH-FACING GARDEN WALL FOR NOTHING AND TOLD NOBODY, AND A MAN IN HIS THIRTIES RAKED THE WHOLE OF IT BACK OUT THREE WEEKS LATER AND SAID NOTHING, AND THE FIRST MAN FOUND OUT FIFTEEN DAYS AFTER THAT AND SAID NOTHING EITHER.**
- **WHY THE FIRST ONE DID IT:** the water off a gutter on the parapet above was going down that face and the face was frost-blasted and flaking, and there is a woman and a girl in that last house. He was on a pair of steps above it for four hours before he started.
- **WHY THE SECOND ONE TOOK IT OUT:** the man in his sixties told him on the eighth of March that the wall is coming down in June for a garage. He went into that yard on the Tuesday for a length of downpipe, saw nine foot of new pointing, thought nothing of it, came back on the Wednesday at about half past ten, and raked the whole of it out in about six hours and packed the rubble back in loose.
- **THE ONE THING HE CANNOT UNDO:** the point of a bolster went through the face of a brick a foot in from the gate pier and took off about a thumbnail of it, and there is a raw pale place there now. The rest of the face is loose rubble standing a bit proud.
- **WHERE BOTH MEN ARE:** the man in his forties went back once, on the Thursday of the fifth of April, for something to do with a door at the last house in that row, and stood at that wall for half a minute, and has not been back. The man in his thirties has not asked him why it was done and does not know he looked.

## 6. Four chisels on a wheel that was not his

- **MAJOR TURN: THE MAN IN HIS FORTIES TOOK HIS OWN CHISEL ROLL INTO AN EMPTY LOCK-UP HE WAS NOT ASKED TO BE IN AND GROUND FOUR OF HIS OWN TOOLS ON A WHEEL THAT BELONGS TO A MAN WHO IS AWAY, AND A WOMAN WATCHED HIM FOR ABOUT A MINUTE FROM THE MOUTH OF THE DOOR.**
- **WHY HE WENT:** his own garage at the top of the town is full of a job that runs to Wednesday, and he had wanted to do those four for about a week and had not been able to stand the chisels.
- **WHAT HE DID NOT DO:** he did not use any of the man's materials, he did not touch his bench, he did not leave it worse, and he put the cover and the brick back and sponged the spill under the wheel up. He told nobody he had gone up there for it.
- **WHAT SHE DID:** she stopped with a paper bag in each hand, watched about a minute, walked four doors to her own car and drove out of that turning. She has not been in that garage since and has not told the man in his sixties, who came back on the Saturday, looked at a wiped bench and a covered wheel, and said nothing.
- **WHAT HE DOES NOT KNOW:** that she was there. He was on one knee on a board with a wheel running six foot from his head and did not hear a car door four doors away.

## 7. Two bands of slates and a length of corrugated iron

- **MAJOR TURN: THE MAN IN HIS THIRTIES CARRIED TWO BUNDLES OF TWELVE SLATES HALF A MILE DOWN A LANE FOR THE MAN IN HIS FORTIES, FOUND THAT GATE STANDING OPEN ON ITS OWN DROPPED HINGE WITH THE BAR LEANING AGAINST THE BRICK BESIDE IT AND NOBODY IN THAT YARD, WAITED ABOUT TWENTY MINUTES, AND PUT THEM UNDER A SHEET OF IRON.**
- **WHAT HE CONSIDERED AND DID NOT DO:** he could have taken them back to the van, rung again, gone looking for another key, or put them by the gate where somebody would walk over them. He did none of them and he did not take long deciding.
- **WHO SAW HIM:** a man who works nights and who has walked that lane four or five mornings a week for two years because it is quicker than the parade at that hour came round the corner at about half past six, was level with the gate at about fifteen foot, saw a man in that yard with a length of iron in his hands, and went on down the lane at the pace he goes down it and has not mentioned it to anybody since.
- **WHAT THE OTHER MAN DID:** he came on the Wednesday of the fourth, saw the iron leaning the other way with a lump of mortar on it, lifted it, and did not ask anybody where they had been. He put them on the pallet himself and carried them the half mile in two loads and was on his own roof on the Friday.

## 8. A bundle two inches forward, and two men both wrong the same way

- **MAJOR TURN: TWO MEN WENT INTO THE SAME LOCKED STORE IN THE SAME WEEK, EACH SAW THE SAME BUNDLE OF LATHS OUT OF SQUARE WITH ITS BAND TURNED THE WRONG WAY, AND EACH CONCLUDED THAT THE OTHER HAD BEEN IN THERE. NEITHER WAS RIGHT. THE WOMAN WHO WORKS AT THAT COUNTER HAD MOVED IT HERSELF, TWICE.**
- **WHAT EACH MAN'S ARITHMETIC WAS:** a woman who works at that counter does not move laths, because there is a barrow and a man comes in with it on Wednesdays and Fridays. The man in his forties has a key and the man in his thirties has not got one and has not been offered one. So it is one of those two, and the man in his thirties put it on the man who has a key.
- **WHAT SHE ACTUALLY DID:** she took the top bundle off that stack to get at a box of hinges behind it, and put it down about two inches forward and two inches to the right because you cannot get a foot behind a bundle once it is in, and she has done that about once a month for two years. On the Wednesday she did it while the man in his forties was in the same room and neither of them was in the other's way for more than a minute and a half.
- **WHY NEITHER WILL BE THE ONE:** to raise it is to admit to standing at a rack with nothing in your hands and no reason to be.

## 9. A comb and a coil, in the same hour, on the same landing

- **MAJOR TURN: HE PUT A COMB BACK IN THE RING OF DUST IT WAS STANDING IN INSIDE THE MINUTE AND TOOK THIRTY FOOT OF CABLE OFF A NAIL BEHIND A DOOR, AND TOLD NOBODY ABOUT EITHER.**
- **THE COMB:** a tortoiseshell one about three inch long with two teeth gone out of it, and it is the man in his thirties', and he left it on that sill in the last week of February beside a saucer and forgot it, and he has not been back in that flat since.
- **THE CABLE:** about thirty foot of two-core and earth, rubber, with a plug on the end, and it is the man in his sixties', and he coiled it onto a nail behind that door in June of the year before last and has never been in that room since. The nail is still there and is bright only where the coil was.
- **WHY ONE WENT BACK AND ONE DID NOT:** a thing on a bench in his own garage is a thing he can have, and a thing on a nail behind a door in somebody's flat is not, and he has done it in his own place before and not this one in this one, and the reason is a pair of steps and a lamp and nowhere else to put the lamp for a minute and a half.
- **WHO KNOWS:** the man in his thirties was in the passage thirty foot away and will never know about the comb. The man in his sixties has not opened that door and is not going to before the summer.

## 10. A wind off the river, and an awning tied up again

- **MAJOR TURN: THE WIND TOOK THE FRONT OFF A CANVAS AWNING OVER A SHOP ABOUT TWO THIRDS OF THE WAY UP THAT PARADE AT TWENTY PAST ONE ON THE EIGHTEENTH OF APRIL, AND THE MAN WHO PUTS SHUTTERS UP CAME DOWN OFF THE TOP OF THE PARADE, PUT A PAIR OF STEPS ON THE KERB, PUT THE CHAIN BACK OVER ITS CLEAT AND TIED THE FRONT BAR TO THE FRAME WITH A PIECE OF CORD OUT OF HIS POCKET, AND WAS GONE BY TWO.**
- **WHAT SHE DID:** she heard it, put her head out of that door, stood there about half a minute, did not go out into it, came out afterwards and stood at the foot of his steps and looked up at what he had done for about ten seconds while he was already getting his things into his van. Neither of them said one word.
- **THE TWO THINGS THAT ARE STILL WRONG:** the shutter at the top of that parade, which has not shut fully since the twelfth of February and which he lifts under the bottom rail twice every morning, and a slab in the middle of that footway standing an inch and a half proud across its whole width. Neither has been reported to anybody. On the way out at half past three the woman put a hand on a door frame she did not need to put a hand on.
- **THE ROUND, UNCHANGED:** shutters in an unaltered order with the last one at the top left to the end of the morning · a counter from ten · a man off nights up that parade at about seven and into it again at about half past four · a man in his sixties on a low wall for about an hour and a bit with a cup · a hall on a meter that was shut, with the key in and the clock switching the light off at four · about nine people on that parade and not one of them holding anything for any of the other eight · and the four answers still going round with no two of them able to be set beside one another.
- **AND THE LINE, WHICH IS STILL THE SAME:** a book in a block by the water with nineteen entries in it, and a space under the last of them, empty now across one thousand two hundred and thirty-nine days, and nobody counted it that day or this month, and nobody has stood in that room, and there is nobody in that borough who could say what that heading is there to record.

# VOLUME 05 OPEN THREADS — after Continuation 0022, Chapter 414

**Read with the "VOLUME 05, CONTINUATION 0022 — CHAPTERS 405–414" block at the end of `state/continuity.md`, which carries the canon for these ten chapters and governs wherever the two differ, and with the Continuation 0021 block above it, which still governs everything those ten chapters did. **VOLUME 05 IS NOT CLOSED AND IS NOT DECLARED CLOSED. THE SERIES IS AT 414 OF 720. NOTHING IN CONTINUATION 0022 RESOLVED ANYTHING AND NOTHING IN IT MAY BE UNDONE, IMPROVED ON, RESTATED OR ANSWERED. EVERY DAY-COUNT BELOW IS CALCULATED FROM ITS OWN ANCHOR ON THE DAY IN QUESTION AND NOT CARRIED FORWARD FROM A SUMMARY: at Monday 28 May 2018 the blank line under the nineteenth is one thousand two hundred and seventy-nine days, the card in the slot is one thousand one hundred and ninety-three, and the letter in the tray is one thousand one hundred and ninety-five.**

## 1. A shovel in a room over a room, and two men twenty-five minutes apart

- **MAJOR TURN: THE MAN IN HIS THIRTIES PUT A CEMENT SHOVEL BACK AGAINST AN END WALL, AND TWENTY-FIVE MINUTES LATER THE MAN IN HIS FORTIES TOOK IT OFF THAT WALL AGAIN AND LAID IT ON A STACK OF PLASTERBOARD BECAUSE HE HAD BOTH HANDS FULL, AND NEITHER OF THEM KNEW THE OTHER HAD BEEN IN THAT ROOM. **THE INTERVAL IS TWENTY-FIVE MINUTES AND NOT TWENTY, AND IT IS TWENTY-FIVE BECAUSE ONE WENT DOWN THAT STAIR AT ABOUT A QUARTER TO TEN AND THE OTHER WENT UP IT AT ABOUT TEN PAST TEN.**
- **WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED:** the shovel had stood against that end wall since a load came out of the cellar under that room on the last Thursday of November, and by April the boards had tipped it forward into the middle of the floor and a stack of plasterboard was holding it up. The man in his thirties took it in one hand and stood it back. The man in his forties came up an outside stair twenty-five minutes later with a sheet of plasterboard under his arm, found it in the door reveal, and put it down on that stack about ten foot away. **SO IT IS ABOUT TEN FOOT FROM WHERE THE FIRST OF THEM PUT IT AND NOT A FOOT FROM WHERE THE SECOND ONE DID. ANY FILE THAT GIVES A DISTANCE FROM WHERE EITHER OF THEM PUT IT IS WRONG, BECAUSE THE SECOND OF THEM IS THE ONE WHO PUT IT WHERE IT IS.**
- **WHAT EACH OF THEM DID NEXT:** the man in his thirties cleared out at a quarter to ten and has not been back up that stair. The man in his forties cleared his tools out at about ten to twelve and has not been in that building since. Neither of them has said one word to anybody.
- **WHY NEITHER WILL RAISE IT:** the shovel is nobody's, it was moved twice by men doing their own work, and to raise it would be to stand in a room and admit to having been in it for nothing. It is on that stack and it is going to be on that stack.

## 2. A tank under a store, and a sentence said in a shop

- **MAJOR TURN: A MAN BEHIND A COUNTER ON THAT PARADE SAID IN ABOUT FIFTEEN SECONDS THAT NOBODY HAD HAD A TANK LID OFF SINCE BEFORE CHRISTMAS, THE MAN IN HIS FORTIES ACTED ON IT THE SAME MORNING, AND THE SENTENCE WAS TRUE, AND HE HAS NEVER ASKED WHERE IT CAME FROM.**
- **WHAT WAS ACTUALLY UNDER THE LID:** a sectional tank with the water five inches down, four inches of sludge settled across the bottom and gone into the joints of all four sides, a float valve stuck wide open at one position since Christmas, an overflow running, and two clean lines on the side it had been standing against where the level had come down twice.
- **WHERE THE SENTENCE CAME FROM AND HOW FAR IT TRAVELLED:** from a man in a fleece to the counter on a Friday afternoon in the last week of March, from a man who used to keep keys to those yards to the man in a fleece, from a man who had a look at that tank at Christmas to the man who used to keep the keys. Not one of the three has a key, owns a house, or has been inside that store.
- **WHAT WAS DONE ABOUT IT:** he cleaned it out on the second and third of May, changed the valve, and took a cheque for one hundred and ten pounds from the man at the end of that terrace. That man gave him about four seconds of sentence, said that this yard of eight houses had never once thrown him in all the time he had been at the end of it and that this had, and nothing else passed between the two of them about it. **THE CHAPTER DOES NOT SAY THAT MAN HAD WONDERED ABOUT IT AND THAT IT HAD BEEN GOING ON FOR YEARS, AND NO FILE MAY SAY IT FOR HIM.** The bills in that terrace have been about the same since before 1974 and nobody ever asked why.

## 3. Four posts, and a man who said four seconds in a shop

- **MAJOR TURN: THE MAN IN HIS FORTIES SAID AT ABOUT TEN PAST FOUR ON THE MONDAY THAT THERE WAS A MAN DOWN THE END OF THAT STREET WITH FOUR POSTS UP IN A YARD, AND ON THE FRIDAY THE WOMAN WHO WORKS IN A SHOP PUT THAT BACK TO THE MAN IN HIS THIRTIES AT HER COUNTER AND HE SAID NEITHER YES NOR NO.**
- **HOW HE KNEW, WHICH IS THE WHOLE OF IT:** he was stopped at the parade end of that street at half past two with a hand trolley, looking up a hundred yard, and there was a man in a yard with a bar, a shovel, a barrow and a string line, and about four foot of galvanised post standing out of the ground. He did not go up the street. He did not see the man's face. He does not know who it is and could not pick one of nine out.
- **WHAT THE MAN IN HIS THIRTIES DID:** nothing. He said "Did he", he said "He did", he took his bag off that counter, and he drove back down that street and put a proper galvanised line on four posts that are dead straight over twenty foot. Nobody has asked him about it and he is not going to raise it.
- **WHAT ALSO HAPPENED IN THAT YARD:** he knocked the third post out at about twenty to twelve and dug it all out again with a bar and a shovel, because that post is over a raft and a wet mix leans on made ground, and he set it again at about twenty past one. A woman who lives in that house came out at about ten past ten and asked whether the line would take a wet sheet, and got a straight answer, and put no name to him.

## 4. A mark in the bottom of a bag, and two men who looked at it

- **MAJOR TURN: THE MAN IN HIS SIXTIES OPENED A BAG THAT HAD BEEN ON THE TOP OF THAT CUPBOARD SINCE ABOUT 2014, SAW A HARD DARK PLACE IN THE BOTTOM OF IT, DECIDED IN ABOUT FOUR SECONDS THAT IT WAS NOTHING, AND PUT IT BACK WITH THAT PLACE AGAINST THE WALL.**
- **WHAT A MAN THE CHAPTER GIVES NO AGE DID AT NINE IN THE MORNING OF THE SAME DAY:** moved the bag off the lino roll to get at the roll, put his thumb into that place without meaning to, found it soft at one edge, and left a grey tip on his thumb, and said nothing to the man in his sixties who was about four foot off with a cup. **HE IS IN THAT FLAT FROM ABOUT HALF PAST EIGHT TO ABOUT HALF PAST TEN ON THAT MORNING AND THE CHAPTER DOES NOT GIVE HIM AN AGE AND NO FILE MAY GIVE HIM ONE.**
- **WHAT THE MAN IN HIS SIXTIES DECIDED, AND WHY HE IS WRONG:** that it is old grease and an old wet rag and a wood stove thirty inches away, and thirty years of that makes a dark place in the bottom of a bag. **HE DID NOT TOUCH IT. That is the part of it that still stands, and the man in his thirties did touch it, and the two of them will never mention a bag to each other.**
- **WHAT IT ACTUALLY IS:** not found out by anybody in this borough. The crease in the canvas runs about five inch, which is longer than the place is wide, and the hide has come up through from underneath and dried there.

## 5. A level off a shelf, and a pale rectangle on a wall

- **MAJOR TURN: THE MAN IN HIS FORTIES WENT INTO THE BACK ROOM OF THE MAN IN HIS SIXTIES AT ABOUT TWENTY PAST NINE ON THE SEVENTH OF MAY TO FIND A STOP TAP AND CAME OUT WITH A THIRTEEN-INCH DOVETAIL LEVEL OFF THE SHELF BY THE WINDOW, AND AT HALF PAST FOUR THAT AFTERNOON THE MAN IN HIS SIXTIES STOOD IN THAT DOORWAY TWICE AND SAID NOTHING.**
- **WHY HE TOOK IT:** he had a stair carriage to fit on the Tuesday morning that is out of true by a quarter of an inch, and his own level was in a van in a yard in a town eight miles off until the Wednesday. It is a small boxwood level gone the colour of an old cricket ball, with brass plates let into both of its faces and gone green where the two of them meet, the vial cover gone, the vial still there, and a thumbwheel on the side of it that moves it.
- **WHAT HE SAW THE SECOND TIME:** a pale rectangle on the plaster behind where that shelf is, about thirteen inch by three and a quarter, the cleanest thing on that wall, clean because about twenty-five years of a level standing against it kept the dust off and nothing else ever stood there. He looked at it for about ten seconds and went downstairs and made his tea.
- **WHY HE WILL NOT ASK:** he has never had a list for any of those rooms and is not going to begin one, and asking is what would make it a thing that happened between two men. He has been in that room four times since and has not stood in that doorway a third time.

## 6. Seventy foot of pipe and a square of wired glass

- **MAJOR TURN: TWO MEN STRIPPED THAT RUN OUT FROM OPPOSITE ENDS, MET AT A CAST-IRON COLUMN ON THE SECOND MORNING, ARGUED IT OUT IN ABOUT SIX MINUTES, AND THE MAN IN HIS THIRTIES TOOK HIS OWN LENGTH OUT AGAIN THAT AFTERNOON AND DID IT THE OTHER WAY, AND A WOMAN BEHIND A SQUARE OF GLASS IN A DOOR SAW ALL OF IT AND SAID NOTHING TO EITHER OF THEM.**
- **WHAT EACH MAN WAS RIGHT ABOUT:** the pipe will go over the top of that column and stay up for a fortnight, and the man in his thirties has fitted one over a column in a school in the March of the year before last and it was perfectly all right. It will not stay there, because that is the high side of an inch-and-a-half flow off a tank on that wall and the joint at that column is the one nobody will be able to get a spanner on in about nine years. The man in his forties had measured the day before.
- **WHAT SHE SAW:** both of them stop inside about two minutes of each other at ten past nine, one of them go up on the steps and put an eye along the pipe, six minutes of talking, one of them come back with a piece of paper, an hour and a quarter of one of them undoing his own work with the other one about five foot off him, and a hammer about four foot off her door that she did not get up and open once.
- **WHAT THE JOB WAS:** about ninety minutes' worth of talking and about an hour and a quarter of undoing, and the run is in, lagged and clipped, and they shook hands on that yard at five past five and got into their vans. Nobody has asked either of them how it went and she is not going to find out.

## 7. A birdcage, ten days in a van, and a gate that does not shut

- **MAJOR TURN: THE WOMAN WHO WORKS IN A SHOP PUT A WIRE BIRD CAGE INTO THE MAN'S HANDS AT ABOUT HALF PAST TEN BECAUSE SHE HAD NO MORE ROOM AND NO MORE BAGS, AND HE CARRIED IT IN HIS OWN VAN FOR TEN DAYS AND SET IT DOWN UNDER THE HOOD OF A GATE AT THE BOTTOM OF A LANE HE WAS IN ONCE IN FEBRUARY.**
- **WHAT IT IS:** a dome on a base, about eighteen inch high, green over white and chalky on the dome, a door that lifts out about half an inch and will not stay, a hinge whose pin is not in it, a dish clipped in, a perch, a door in the top with a ring and no hasp, so that nothing can be shut in it and nothing ever was, and a ring-mark in the paint about a year old and about the size of a shilling.
- **WHAT CAME OF IT:** four pounds on the floor behind the passenger seat on its side, moved about four times a day, out entirely for one job on the twenty-fifth, a coat of plaster off one corner of the base on the first day which he brushed off with his thumb. He did not take it home and there is no room in that. He stood outside an ironmonger's window in a town eight miles off on the Thursday of the sixteenth for about a minute before he went back to his own van, and he saw a man in a fleece put a kettle on a trestle in the middle of a road on the Monday of the twenty-first and thought about it for a second and then thought about something else.
- **WHO KNOWS:** the man in his thirties was ten foot off at that counter and asked one question about the door and got one answer. The woman has not been down that lane since March and does not know there is one. The man that yard belongs to has not been down it since the middle of May, was not there when it was put down, and does not know it is there. None of the three will raise it.
- **THE TWO FIGURES THAT HAVE TO STAY TOGETHER: IT WENT INTO THAT VAN ON THE TUESDAY OF THE FIFTEENTH AND CAME OUT OF IT ON THE FRIDAY OF THE TWENTY-FIFTH, WHICH IS TEN DAYS, AND IT WAS NOT IN THAT VAN ON THE TWENTY-EIGHTH.** A state file that says thirteen days, or that says it is still in that van, or that says the owner of that yard has walked past it twice, is wrong on all three counts and the chapter is right on all three.

## 8. Four foot of marble, and two reasons that do not meet

- **MAJOR TURN: TWO MEN WALKED PAST A MARBLE CHIMNEY PIECE IN A STORE TWICE EACH ON ONE AFTERNOON AND NEITHER TOUCHED IT, ONE OF THEM KEEPS A RULE HE HAS NEVER PUT INTO WORDS FOR ANYBODY, AND WHAT THE RULE IS ABOUT IS A LOCKED ROOM AND HIS OWN VAN, WITH A HOUSE UNDERNEATH THAT, AND HE WOULD HAVE TO SAY ALL OF IT IN A STREET TO GET THE HELP HE NEEDS AND HE HAS NOBODY TO SAY IT TO. THE OTHER ONE'S REASON IS ABOUT HAVING NOBODY TO HOLD A BOARD AND NOT BEING THE ONE WHO GOES LOOKING FOR ONE. NEITHER WILL EVER KNOW THE OTHER ONE'S REASON.**
- **WHAT THE OBJECT IS:** a plain white marble surround, about four foot wide and three foot ten high and five inch deep, a grey veining running up from the bottom left and out through the top, a roundel in the frieze, two small square panels, a three foot two opening, and a slate base about four foot wide. It came out of a house in Terrace Street in about 1990, in a crate with straw and two battens, and it weighs about three hundred and twenty pounds. **THE FIGURE IT COMES IN AT IS ABOUT THREE HUNDRED AND TWENTY POUNDS AND A LATER FILE THAT PRINTED FOUR HUNDRED WAS WRONG; IT COMES IN AT THREE HUNDRED AND TWENTY AND NOT AT FOUR HUNDRED, AND NOBODY IN THIS BOROUGH IS ASKING.**
- **THE MAN IN HIS FORTIES' REASON:** he has had a key to that store for about six years and goes about four times a month and has never gone in for nothing. He made a rule a long time ago that he does not take a thing out of a locked room to put in his own van, and he has never said that rule out loud to anybody. It came out of a house. He has nobody to say the sentence to and is not going about looking for one.
- **THE MAN IN HIS THIRTIES' REASON:** it would take two men to get it down and a third on the boards, and he has not got a second man, and there is nobody in this borough he could ask, and he does not intend to be the one to ask, and that is the whole of it and it is not going to change.
- **WHAT THEY SAID TO EACH OTHER, TWICE:** at about twenty to twelve one of them said something about where the other one's load could stand, which is the ordinary thing to say to a man carrying that, and got two words back. At about half past three one of them wanted a second pair of hands on the bottom of that door, which is heavy and stands on a ledge, and the other one came back up the yard and gave him it. **THE LINES THEMSELVES ARE IN 0412 AND ARE NOT PRINTED HERE. A STATE FILE THAT COPIES A CHAPTER'S DIALOGUE HAS COPIED A CHAPTER, AND A FILE THAT INVENTS A LINE HAS SAID SOMETHING NOBODY SAID; BOTH ARE WORSE THAN SAYING THAT SOMETHING PASSED BETWEEN TWO MEN, AND AN EARLIER TALLY OF THIS BLOCK PRINTED A LINE THAT IS NOT IN THAT CHAPTER AT ALL AND HAS BEEN STRUCK.**

## 9. A hot cupboard, and a man on a step in the dark

- **MAJOR TURN: THE MAN IN HIS FORTIES WENT INTO A HOT CUPBOARD OFF A DARK HALF-LANDING TWICE WITH HIS HEAD AND HIS SHOULDER IN IT, AND ON THE SECOND TIME HE CAME OUT AT ABOUT TEN TO TWO AND SAT DOWN ON THE BOTTOM STEP OF THE UPPER FLIGHT FOR ABOUT SIX MINUTES AND THEN FINISHED THAT BATHROOM AND RANG NOBODY.**
- **WHAT THE CUPBOARD IS:** two foot four by two foot by a foot and a half, holding a cylinder four foot long, lagged to within four inch of the floor and not lagged at all over the top eight inch of the head, on a plank door whose bottom hinge screw has come out of the head of the hinge and gone about two inches into the timber, so the door hangs about two inch proud. About seventy-eight in there on the twenty-second of May.
- **WHAT HAPPENED TO HIM:** the first time, at about half past ten, he came out backwards on his knees, stood up with a hand on the wall, and was wrong for about a minute. He went back and finished that valve. The second time he went into that cupboard at about twenty past one and was out of it again at about ten to two, got four steps down and sat down and put his hand across his eyes for about six minutes, and for about four seconds he was not sure whether he was all right and then he was, and then he said out loud to himself, once, that he would not go in there again that afternoon. He did not go in again that afternoon. He finished the basin, the tap, the trap, the pedestal and the paint on the tile, and left that flat at half past four.
- **WHO NOTICED:** the man in his thirties went up that stair at about ten to two, saw him on that step, carried on up, said nothing, came back down the same flight at about twenty to three, and has not mentioned it and is not going to. The woman who works in a shop was on a counter at about twenty to six and saw him put his hand flat on the counter for about two seconds while she gave him his change. **THE ONLY MAN WHO COULD HAVE SEEN HIM IS THE ONE WHO CAME UP THAT STAIR AT TEN TO TWO AND NOT AT TWENTY PAST ONE, BECAUSE AT TWENTY PAST ONE HE WAS STILL IN THAT CUPBOARD, AND ANY FILE THAT PUTS THE SIGHTING AT TWENTY PAST ONE IS WRONG.**

## 10. A table that stopped rocking, and a Monday

- **MAJOR TURN: A MAN PUT A THREE-FOOT LENGTH OF BATTEN UNDER THE SHORT LEG OF A TABLE IN A ROOM AT THE BACK OF A SHOP AT ABOUT A QUARTER TO NINE ON THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF MAY AND TOLD NOBODY, AND THE WOMAN WHO WORKS IN A SHOP FOUND IT AT ABOUT TEN AND DID NOT GO AND GET HIM.**
- **WHY IT WAS WRONG:** the table is about four foot by two foot on a painted steel frame with tubular legs, one frame repaired once with a length of angle and a pop rivet, and the heater was moved against that wall in about January. It has rocked on the end nearest the heater since before Christmas and it is the table everything in that shop is done on. **HE WAS ASKED FOR THE TAP AND NOT ASKED FOR THE TABLE, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE DIFFERENCE.** She put it to him across a counter that morning while he was buying washers, he agreed on the spot because the pipe happened to be out already, and he stood at that tap for three quarters of an hour with that table at the edge of his sight the whole way through and gave it not a thought at all until he had his bag in his hand. **NO FILE MAY PUT THE TABLE INSIDE THAT ASK.**
- **WHAT SHE DID:** she came in for a sheet of paper, put her hand flat on the top of it, found the batten cut off square and standing a quarter inch proud, and worked out in about two seconds who put it there, and did not go four doors up the street, and has not, and is not going to.
- **THE ROUND, UNCHANGED AND DESCRIBED DIFFERENTLY:** the man who puts shutters up down that parade at a quarter past eight with four up by twenty to nine and the rest still to do at half past ten · a man off nights up it at a quarter to one and out again with a bag of compost · a woman down it at half past nine with a folded ladder who did not come back up · a van outside the shop that shuts early at ten past nine with its hazards on for about four minutes · a hall on a meter shut all Monday with the key in it and a clock switching the light off at four and nobody in the building to see it happen · about nine people out and most of them under ten minutes and not one of them carrying anything for any of the other eight.
- **AND THE LINE, WHICH IS STILL THE SAME:** a room in a block by the water with a door that has never caught, and a shelf, and a book with nineteen entries in it, and under the last of them a space that has stood empty for one thousand two hundred and seventy-nine days, and nobody went near that room that day or the day before or the day after, and one woman has ever had that book in her hands and did not go down that corridor.

## 1. A limb, a refusal, a roof, a pane, a window, two facts, a gate, a door, a wall, a bicycle

- **A LIMB DOWN ACROSS A FENCE IN JUNE, AND TWO MEN WHO EACH REFUSED, IN THE SAME WEEK, TO HAVE IT CUT, AND NEITHER KNOWS THAT THE OTHER REFUSED.** The man in his thirties said one word to two people and gave his reasons to neither; his reasons were the month, a boundary he has never established, and his own leaving. The man in his forties saw it in a garden he was not invited into and walked out with his tape in his bag; his reasons were that a thing is either his or it is not, what he has seen happen to every tree that comes out of a house he has worked in, and the fact that he had no saw. **NEITHER WILL EVER ASK THE OTHER, AND A CLOSE-BOARD IS STILL OFF THE FENCE AND A NAIL IS STILL BENT DOUBLE.**
- **A BORROWING REFUSED IN ABOUT FOUR SECONDS BY A MAN WHO HAS THE THING, AND WHO WILL NOT GIVE IT AWAY TO ANYBODY.** The reason is a shop in town in 2016 and a price list on a wall he could not read and a pair that cannot be had again quickly, and the reason is not the man who asked. **IT IS IN A VAN, IT WILL BE THERE ON ANY MONDAY, AND NOBODY HAS ASKED FOR IT SINCE.**
- **A ROOF HEAD DONE PROPERLY IN SEVENTY MINUTES BY A MAN WHO WAS ONLY IN THAT YARD TO PARK, WHO ALSO TOOK THREE MORE SHEETS OFF, AND WHO TOOK THE RUBBISH HOME IN HIS OWN VAN.** One person worked out who it was within seconds and did not fetch him. The far end of the same roof is still failing and she knows it and he does not, and she put her own hand on that wall in April and said out loud that there was a wet mark on it. **NOBODY HAS JOINED THE TWO HALVES.**
- **A CRACKED PANE ON A LANDING, LEFT BY TWO MEN FOR UNRELATED REASONS AND THEN DONE BY A THIRD PERSON WHO WAS NEVER ASKED.** Her reasons were that a landlord's is a landlord's, and that a man in his thirties cannot be the one who did that window; his were that it is not his and that the woman either knows and has decided to leave it or does not know. Hers were that nobody in that building is going to do it and that if she leaves it, it will not get done for the best part of five years. **SHE PAID FOR IT HERSELF, DID IT IN THREE GOES, TOLD NOBODY, AND HAS NEVER ASKED FOR ANYTHING AND HAS NEVER BEEN ASKED FOR ANYTHING.**
- **A WINDOW CARRIED FURTHER THAN IT NEEDED TO GO, AND PUT DOWN WHERE THE MAN WAS GOING TO BE ANYWAY.** What he was going there for was a question about the ground, and about a lorry that is coming on the Thursday. The man in his thirties was thirty yard behind him, offered a hand, was refused, and does not know what he saw. **THERE IS A CHALK MARK ON A GATE POST AND NOTHING ON THE WINDOW.**
- **TWO TRUE THINGS LEARNED IN ONE HOUR BY TWO PEOPLE WHO WERE NEITHER OF THE OTHER MAN, AND NEITHER MAN ACTED.** One was a man who has never hired anything buying a set of tools; the other was a yard past the junction, three men in it, his own name on every job that leaves it. **A WRITER WHO WANTS A NINTH DIVERGENCE DEVICE MAY BUILD ONE AND SHOULD SAY SO FIRST.**
- **A GATE PUT RIGHT BY A MAN WHO WALKED IN THROUGH A GAP WHERE A GATE DOES NOT SHUT, IN ABOUT THREE QUARTERS OF AN HOUR, AND WHO WILL NOT SAY WHY.** The man who lives there is seventy-one, has a bad hip, has asked nobody and will not. The man in his thirties was in the house all day, noticed afterwards, and told him it was all right, and was told that the man he meant was not in the house. **THE REASON IS A HOUSE CLEARED IN JANUARY, A FRIDGE THAT WENT THROUGH THE GATE BACKWARDS, FOUR MINUTES, AND A MAN WHO DIED IN THAT HOUSE, AND NOBODY IN THIS BOROUGH KNOWS BUT THE MAN WHO IS GONE.**
- **A SHOP DOOR THAT CATCHES PEOPLE, TWICE IN FOUR HOURS ON THE SAME AFTERNOON, ON A MAN AND THEN ON A WOMAN.** She stood against the front of her own building for about two minutes and nobody on that parade stopped, which is how this borough behaves, and she is one of them. He stopped it with his hand and walked off. The third person saw both and is the only person in this borough who has, and has said nothing to anybody then or since. **IN A FORTNIGHT NEITHER OF THE TWO HAS RAISED IT.**
- **A WALL BEGUN BY A MAN IN HIS SIXTIES AND FINISHED BY A MAN IN HIS THIRTIES IN THREE EVENINGS, WITH HIS OWN BUCKET AND HIS OWN BOARDS CARRIED OUT EVERY NIGHT AND NOTHING OF THE ROOM'S USED.** A man with a key to that passage door came through in the middle of the second evening, saw a man working, and left. **THE MAN WHO BEGAN IT FOUND IT FINISHED, SAID NOTHING, DID NOT ASK, DID NOT PUT HIS HAND ON IT, AND DID NOT LOOK AT THE ONE CORNER HE COULD NOT DO. THE TROWEL IS STILL ON THE LEDGE AND THE BAG OF PLASTER HAS NOT BEEN OPENED.**
- **A BICYCLE MOVED FOUR FOOT FURTHER IN AGAINST A WALL BY A MAN CARRYING HIS OWN STEPS, AT HALF PAST SEVEN IN THE MORNING, AND TOLD TO NOBODY.** The man who left it there did not notice and would not have known what to mention. The woman who works in a shop was in a room with a bench in it and no table and did not see any of it. **ABOUT NINE PEOPLE WERE ON THAT PARADE THAT DAY AND NONE OF THEM WAS DOING ANYTHING FOR ANY OF THE OTHERS, AND THE HALL AT THE BOTTOM WAS SHUT ON A METER AND PUT ITS OWN LIGHTS OUT AT FOUR WITH NOBODY IN IT.**

**AND THE SEVEN DEVICES OF DIVERGENCE STAND WHERE THEY STOOD, AND 0023 ADDED AN EIGHTH OF ITS OWN AND FLAGGED IT. THE THREE TIMES A SENTENCE HAS BEEN SAID TWICE AND HEARD AS TWO THINGS ARE 0323, 0333 AND 0353, AND 0367 IS NOT A FOURTH, AND 0019 THROUGH 0023 ADDED NO FIFTH. 0382 IS A FIFTH CASE AND IS NOT THAT DEVICE AND IS NOT A FOURTH RUN OF IT. **0391 IS A SIXTH CASE AND IS A DIVERGENCE OF INFORMATION AND NOT OF MEANING. **0402 IS A SEVENTH CASE OF THAT LAST THING, WHICH IS A DIVERGENCE OF INFORMATION IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS FROM EACH OTHER. **0406 AND 0412 ARE NOT ANY OF THESE SEVEN AND ARE NOT AN EIGHTH. 0406 IS A DIVERGENCE OF KNOWLEDGE AND 0412 IS A CONVERGENCE OF SILENCE. **AND 0420 IS AN EIGHTH AND IS FLAGGED RATHER THAN PASSED OFF AS A NINTH CLASS: TWO MEN EACH LEARNED ONE TRUE THING ABOUT THE OTHER IN THE SAME HOUR, FROM TWO PEOPLE WHO WERE NEITHER OF THE OTHER MAN, AND BOTH FACTS WERE TRUE AND NEITHER MAN ACTED. THAT IS A DIVERGENCE OF INFORMATION OF A KIND THAT IS HARDER TO HIDE THAN EITHER 0391 OR 0402, BECAUSE A FALSE FACT CAN BE CORRECTED BY ONE MAN AND A TRUE FACT CAN ONLY BE DEALT WITH BY BOTH, AND NEITHER OF THEM DID ANYTHING AT ALL. A WRITER WHO WANTS A NINTH MAY BUILD ONE AND SHOULD NOT BUILD IT WITHOUT SAYING SO FIRST.****

# VOLUME 05 OPEN THREADS — after Continuation 0024, Chapter 434

## 1. A true thing said at a counter, and a true thing said at a van, and a passing at a blind end

- **A WOMAN ASKED HIM, LIGHTLY, WHETHER HE HAD EATEN PROPERLY IN THIS TOWN SINCE CHRISTMAS, AND HE SAID NO.** She has not raised it since and does not know she said it. He told nobody, checked nothing, and went on eating at half past one in his own van for six weeks, and there was no second question to ask because there was nothing in it for anybody. **HIS OWN REASON FOR LEAVING IT ALONE WAS THAT A SECOND QUESTION WOULD TURN HIM INTO SOMEBODY WHO ASKS SECOND QUESTIONS, AND HE HAS DECIDED HE IS NOT GOING TO BE THAT PERSON.**
- **SIX WEEKS AFTER THAT A MAN IN HIS SIXTIES PUT IT TO HIM, BESIDE AN OPEN VAN, OVER THE OTHER ONE HAVING HAD NO TELEPHONE SINCE THE NOVEMBER BEFORE LAST AND GOING TO THE CALL BOX AT THE END OF THAT STREET TO RING.** The man in his forties put it against six years of a number he has never used, looked the number up on the Friday night, and put the telephone back in his coat. **A FACT LEARNED LATE IS NOT THE SAME AS A FACT LEARNED IN AN HOUR, AND A PERSON WHO HAS TOLD YOU SOMETHING TRUE ABOUT SOMEBODY HAS NOT ASKED YOU FOR ANYTHING, AND TWO MEN WHO EACH KNOW ONE TRUE THING ABOUT THE OTHER ARE NOT TWO MEN WHO HAVE MET.**
- **THEY WENT PAST EACH OTHER AT A BLIND END SIX WEEKS AND ONE DAY AFTER SHE ASKED HIM, AND ONE SAID GOOD MORNING AND THE OTHER LIFTED A HAND FOUR INCHES AND SAID NOTHING.** He was a foot away and did not see it. **NEITHER OF THEM BROKE STEP AND NEITHER OF THEM LOOKED BACK, AND NEITHER HAS PUT A SINGLE QUESTION TO THE OTHER ABOUT ANYTHING, AND NEITHER KNOWS THAT THE OTHER HAS ANYTHING AT ALL.**

## 2. Iron against a gable end, and a promise made to avoid being asked twice

- **A MAN CALLED BRIGGS TOOK A ROOF OFF A HOUSE IN THE SUMMER OF 2017, PUT THE OLD RAINWATER GOODS OUT AT THE KERB, AND ASKED A MAN IN HIS FORTIES WHETHER HE WANTED ANY OF IT.** The answer was no, and then a promise to come back next week, and he had known when he said the second sentence that he was not going to. **THE IRON HAS BEEN AGAINST THAT GABLE END SINCE AND IS STILL AGAINST IT, AND IT IS NOT A GIFT THAT WAS REFUSED AND NOT A THING THAT WAS OWED.**
- **HE PUT HIS HAND ON IT FOR ABOUT TEN MINUTES ON THE TENTH OF JULY AND LEFT IT EXACTLY WHERE IT WAS, AND HE WORKED OUT THREE THINGS WHILE HE STOOD THERE AND WAS RIGHT ABOUT ALL THREE.** Being right was worth nothing, and there is nobody in this borough who is going to be told and nobody who is going to be impressed. **HE CAME BACK ON THE THURSDAY HE HAD SAID HE WOULD COME BACK AND ON THE SUNDAY MORNING HE HAD SAID NOTHING ABOUT, AND HE HAS DECIDED NOTHING.**

## 3. Three boards, one building, and the man at the bottom of it

- **A MAN IN HIS FORTIES WENT UP ON THAT ROOF ABOUT WHAT HE WAS NOT SURE WAS STILL SOUND AND FOUND THAT IT WAS, AND CAME BACK DOWN AND LEFT THE BOARDS WHERE THEY WERE.** A man in his thirties had the top flat of the same building to himself for two hours that morning on a job of his own, and the pair of them never knew. **A MAN IN HIS SIXTIES AT THE BOTTOM OF THAT BUILDING SAW ALL THREE THINGS, WHICH WERE A VAN, A MAN OVER A PARAPET AND A SCREWDRIVER ON THE FLAGS, AND HE DRANK HIS TEA AND DID NOT GO OUT.**
- **THE SCREWDRIVER IS STILL ON THOSE FLAGS AND THE OWNER OF IT HAS NOT BEEN TOLD IT IS THERE, AND NOBODY HAS PUT A CLAIM ON IT, AND IT WILL NOT BE IN ANY COUNT.** The woman who owns the top flat came home, said the room looked bigger, and has never opened the two rooms over the shop and does not know they were opened.

## 4. Five sentences about a building he had been inside

- **HE SAID HE HAD NEVER BEEN INSIDE THAT BUILDING AND HE HAD BEEN IN ITS YARD, ALONE, IN APRIL, AND HE SAID IT BECAUSE TWO MEN FROM A TOWN EIGHT MILES OFF HAD ALREADY ASKED HIM ONCE EACH AND HE WANTED THE ANSWER ON THE RECORD IN HIS OWN MOUTH BEFORE A THIRD ASK.** He was not protecting anybody and the owner of the freehold has not spoken to him since 2014 and does not know he was ever there.
- **HE SAID IT FOUR MORE TIMES, ONCE TO A MAN IN HIS SIXTIES IN A PASSAGE AND ONCE AT THAT COUNTER TO NOBODY AT ALL, AND NOT ONE OF THE FIVE SOUNDS DIFFERENT FROM ANY OTHER.** She believes him and has no reason not to. **A MAN IN HIS SIXTIES ASKED THAT QUESTION OF FOUR PEOPLE ACROSS THREE WEEKS AND HEARD THE SAME ANSWER FROM THREE OF THEM, AND PUT THEM DOWN AS THREE, WHICH IS WHAT ANYBODY WOULD PUT THEM DOWN AS.**

## 5. A saucer, a door pocket, and a folding rule

- **SHE PUT IT INTO THE HAND THAT WAS FREE AND SAID ONE WORD AND WENT BACK ROUND THE COUNTER, AND HE ASKED NOTHING AND SHE SAID NOTHING ELSE.** It had been on a sill behind that counter since June because nobody wanted a saucer with a chip through the rim, and she wanted about nine people to have it.
- **HE PUT IT IN THE OFFSIDE DOOR POCKET OF HIS OWN VAN AT ABOUT HALF PAST FOUR THAT AFTERNOON, FACE DOWN, ON TOP OF A FOLDING RULE, AND AT THE END OF THAT WEEK IT WAS STILL THERE.** He opened that pocket four times and moved it four inches once to get at the rule. **IT IS NOT A GIFT AND NOT AN INSTRUCTION AND NOT A DEBT, AND NOBODY HAS GIVEN HIM ANYTHING TO DO, AND IT IS NOT GOING INTO A HOUSE AND HE IS NOT GOING TO ASK HER WHY.**

## 6. Thirty foot of flex, a bare hook, and a decision taken in a coat

- **HE TOOK IT AT TEN TO TEN WALKING PAST IT, USED IT FOR SEVEN HOURS, AND HUNG IT BACK ON THAT HOOK AT FIVE, AND KNOCKED NEITHER TIME.** The man who was working over by the outbuilding that afternoon saw the whole of it and shut his mouth, and his reason for shutting it is his own and is not a good one: he has never in his life been the sort of man who raises it when he sees another man take a thing.
- **A WOMAN AT THE END OF THAT TERRACE ASKED WHOSE THE HOOK WAS AND WAS TOLD THE THING HAD BEEN PUT BACK, AND IT HAD NOT, AND SHE HAS NOT ASKED ANYBODY ABOUT IT SINCE.** The man in his sixties found the hook bare at half past three, put the kettle on instead of his coat on, and watched the reel go back up from his own front room. **HE HAS DECIDED THAT THIRTY FOOT OF FLEX IS NOT A THING HE IS GOING TO SPEND AN EVENING OF HIS LIFE ON, AND HE HAS NOT CHANGED HIS MIND AND NOBODY IS GOING TO ASK HIM.**

## 7. One sink, and a man who did not mind

- **A MERCHANT EIGHT MILES OFF TOLD ONE MAN AND A MAN WHO SELLS PIPE TOLD THE OTHER, THE SAME AFTERNOON, THIRD HAND, AND THE MERCHANT COULD NOT USE IT HIMSELF.** The second man did not go and look until he was walking back that way at ten to seven and the first man had it in his own van.
- **HE STOOD ON THE FAR KERB ABOUT A MINUTE AND SAID HE HAD JUST HAD A LOOK AND WENT ON DOWN THE STREET.** He wanted it and had wanted one for about two years without knowing it, and most of that went out of him while he was standing there. **NOT MINDING IS NOT A VIRTUE AND IS NOT A DEFEAT AND WAS AWARDED TO NOBODY, AND HE HAS NOT SAID THE WORD SINCE AND HE FOUND HE WAS WHISTLING AND DID NOT NOTICE DOING IT, AND NOBODY KNOWS THERE WERE TWO MEN AFTER IT.**

## 8. Eight months of a chimney, and ninety minutes of a picture

- **IT STARTED IN THE FIRST COLD WEEK OF DECEMBER, AFTER A FLUE THAT WAS SWEPT IN NOVEMBER AND WAS CLEAR, AND IT IS A GREY SMOKE THAT COMES DOWN ONE SIDE OF THE ROOM.** There is a bloom at the throat, a streak on the breast, grey across the top of the curtains, a cough since the second week of January, four days of washing dried in that room in February, and a settee six inch out of the smoke that has never been put back. **SHE TOLD HER SON HALF OF IT ON A SUNDAY IN APRIL AND HALF OF IT IS STILL UNUSED.**
- **A MAN WAS PAID TO HANG THREE PICTURES IN THAT ROOM IN AUGUST AND WAS IN IT NINETY MINUTES, AND PART WAY THROUGH HE SAW WHAT SHE HAD BEEN LIVING WITH AND GOT HIMSELF UP HIGH ENOUGH TO SEE ROUND THE HOOD, AND PUT TWO QUESTIONS TO HER, AND GOT ANSWERS, AND THEN WENT BACK TO WHAT HE HAD BEEN PAID TO DO AND TOOK HIS MONEY AND LEFT WITHOUT ANOTHER WORD.** He did not tell her to put that fire out and he did not say a man could come. **NOBODY WAS TELEPHONED AND THERE IS NOWHERE A REPORT OF IT WOULD GO AND SHE LIT IT AGAIN AT HALF PAST SEVEN THAT EVENING AND WILL GO ON LIGHTING IT, AND A HOUSE THAT HAS STOPPED TALKING TO ITSELF ABOUT WHAT IS GOING ON INSIDE IT HAS AGREED TO NOTHING.**

## 9. A frame off a shelf, and the way he got back in

- **HE WENT IN TO PRICE A RANGE AND PRICED IT AT ROUGHLY FOUR TIMES WHAT THE ROOM WAS WORTH, AND TOOK A PICTURE FRAME OFF A SHELF, AND SAID WHY TO NOBODY BECAUSE THERE WAS NOBODY THERE.** His reason is his own and is not about money: he has stood in two hundred rooms in this borough that were being cleared and has watched photographs of people go out with the plaster, and he does not want that to happen to that one. **HE IS NOT A RESCUER OF ANYTHING AND HAS RESCUED NOTHING AND HAS NOT ASKED HIMSELF ONCE WHAT HE IS GOING TO DO WITH IT.**
- **ON THE MONDAY HE CAME BACK FOR TWO DAYS' WORK ON A COUNTER AND THE SHOP WAS SHUT AND THE OTHER MAN WAS IN THERE, AND HE CAME ACROSS THE FLOOR AND OPENED THE FRONT AND STEPPED BACK AND PICKED HIS TAPE MEASURE UP AGAIN.** Nine sentences passed between them and every one was about the counter. On his way out he went upstairs, which is not a thing a man does on the way out of a shop, and left the frame standing on a shelf in the other room where the light is better. **THE OTHER MAN BELIEVES NOBODY HAS OPENED THOSE TWO ROOMS SINCE 2011 AND WILL NEVER BE TOLD OTHERWISE, AND THE RANGE IS STILL IN THERE AND THE SHOP STILL DOES NOT KNOW WHAT IT IS WORTH.**

## 10. A mat in a gutter, a lock-up with its shutter up, and a ruled space

- **A LOCK-UP AT THE TOP OF THAT PARADE HAS HAD ITS SHUTTER UP EVERY DAY SINCE MARCH WITH A MAN INSIDE IT FROM TEN UNTIL NINE REPAIRING THINGS THAT ARE NOT WORTH REPAIRING, AND NOBODY ON THAT PARADE HAS SPOKEN TO HIM IN ABOUT SEVEN MONTHS.** Nobody has ever knocked on that shutter and he is not sitting there waiting on anybody.
- **A COIR MAT WAS IN THE GUTTER SIX YARD UP THAT PARADE WITH A TYRE PRINT ACROSS THE RUBBER ON THE BACK OF IT, AND A WOMAN CARRIED IT BACK ON HER HIP, PUT IT ON HER OWN STEP, TOOK THE GRIT OFF THE FACE OF IT WITH HER HAND, WENT BACK IN AND FINISHED WITH THE CUSTOMER SHE HAD LEFT STANDING.** Nobody saw. **SOMEONE ELSE PUTS THAT MAT DOWN EARLY EVERY MONDAY MORNING AND CARRIES ON WITH EIGHT OTHER THINGS, AND HE HAS NO IDEA IT WAS EVER OFF, AND NOBODY IN THIS BOROUGH CAN BE TOLD, AND NOTHING IS EVER GOING TO BE PUT TO ANYBODY ABOUT IT.**
- **FOUR ANSWERS ARE STILL GOING ROUND AND THERE IS NO FIFTH, ONE OF THEM IS IN FAR MORE MOUTHS THAN THE OTHER THREE, THE OTHER THREE HAVE NOT BEEN SAID SINCE FEBRUARY, AND NONE OF THE FOUR CAN BE SET BESIDE ANY OF THE OTHERS.** In 0434 one man told another man outside a shutter that he knew what something was, and the other said he had no idea, and nobody has said out loud what any of them is an answer to. **THE SPACE UNDER THE NINETEENTH LINE OF THAT BOOK HAD BEEN OPEN FOR 1,364 DAYS WHEN THE TWENTY-FIRST OF AUGUST CAME, AND NOBODY WENT UP THAT CORRIDOR, AND THERE IS SOMETHING IN THIS BOROUGH THAT NOT ONE PERSON LIVING IN IT COULD DESCRIBE IF YOU STOPPED THEM IN THE STREET, AND IT IS THE SAME SOMETHING IT WAS AT THE END OF JULY.**

**AND ONE FINDING FROM THE REVIEW OF 0024 THAT 0025 MUST CARRY, AND IT IS A FINDING ABOUT A DATELINE AND NOT ABOUT A CHAPTER. THE MEASURING METHOD AT §12A OF THE 0024 BLOCK DROPS A DATELINE ONLY WHEN THE WHOLE OF A SPAN SITS INSIDE THE DATELINE PARAGRAPH, AND A SPAN THAT BEGINS INSIDE A DATELINE AND RUNS OUT OF IT INTO THE FIRST LINE OF THE CHAPTER IS NOT DROPPED AND IS REAL REUSE OF THE FRAME. 0024 HAD EXACTLY THAT TWICE ACROSS THE BATCH BOUNDARY, TWELVE TOKENS IN 0430 AGAINST 0419 AND NINE IN 0431 AGAINST 0419, AND THE RUN THREE WINDOW THAT CONTAINS THEM WAS REPORTED AS CLEAN BECAUSE OF IT. **SO: A DATELINE MAY NOT REUSE THE `from about X in the morning until about Y` CLOCK PAIR, WHICH IS IN 0398, 0419 AND OTHERS, AND MAY NOT END ON `off a side street, in Tideglass`, WHICH WAS IN ELEVEN CHAPTERS AND IS NOW OUT, AND A WRITER WHO WANTS A SPAN OF NINE OR MORE TOKENS SHOULD BUILD A DATELINE AROUND A DURATION, A SECOND DATE, OR A PLACE NOBODY ELSE HAS DATED ANYTHING IN. **AND A FIGURE PRINTED IN A FILE THAT DESCRIBES CHAPTERS IS NOT EVIDENCE, AND THE REVIEW OF 0024 FOUND FOUR OF THEM: A RUN THREE WINDOW UNDER-REPORTED, A SHOP-WOMAN CENSUS THAT SAID TEN CHAPTERS AND LISTED THREE ACTS THAT WERE NOT HERS, A DATELINE THAT SAID FOUR DAYS AND WAS FIVE, AND A CALENDAR THAT NAMED A FRIDAY AS A WEDNESDAY. ## 1. Two blankets, one woman at Brackness, and two people who never met

- **A MAN IN HIS SIXTIES COULD NOT CARRY ONE UPSTAIRS AND PUT IT IN A VAN INSTEAD, IN JUNE, AND HAS NOT ASKED FOR IT BACK AND IS NOT GOING TO.** He gave the address of a place and the week the woman went there and nothing else, standing on his own pavement with his gate shut. **THE MAN HE GAVE IT TO HAS BEEN TO THAT ROAD TWICE, HAS SAT IN THE CAR PARK BOTH TIMES, AND THE THING STOPPING HIM IS NOT THE PLACE AND NOT THE WOMAN AND IS WHICH OF THIRTY HOUSES SHE IS IN, AND HE IS NOT GOING TO GET THAT OUT OF ANYBODY WHO KEEPS A TILL.**
- **A WOMAN WHO WAS ASKED IN JULY BY SOMEBODY WHO ALSO COULD NOT CARRY IT UPSTAIRS HAS BEEN OUT AND BACK TWICE AND WILL BE BACK AGAIN.** She was not offered money for the bus and would not have taken any. She has twice bought the paper about what is happening in that hospital and twice thrown it away unread because there is a photograph of her own street in it. **WHAT SHE IS SHORT OF IS A WEEK, AND WHAT HE IS SHORT OF IS A HOUSE, AND NEITHER OF THEM CAN SUPPLY THE OTHER.**
- **THEY CROSSED ON THE TWENTY-SECOND OF AUGUST GOING OPPOSITE WAYS AND NEITHER OF THEM TURNED A HEAD.** He was reading signs. She was sorting him into a category she keeps nine other men in. **NOBODY HAS ASKED ANYBODY ANYTHING, AND THE WOMAN THOSE BLANKETS ARE FOR DOES NOT KNOW THAT ANY OF IT IS HAPPENING.**

## 2. A date on a string, and a rectangle in a table-top

- **HE READ IT WHILE THE CASE WAS SWINGING AND HE DID NOT READ IT AGAIN.** It was a printed label on a loop of string, and it carried a name, two place names and a date in October, and he turned it over afterwards with the case already back where it belonged.
- **HE PUT IT BACK WITHIN AN INCH OF WHERE IT HAD BEEN, WHICH MEANS HE LOOKED, AND HE DID NOT LOOK ON ANY OTHER DAY OF THAT WEEK.**
- **THREE DAYS LATER IT WAS GONE AND THE DUST KEPT IT.** He finished a length of beading, shut a door on a hinge and left. **HE TOLD NOBODY, HE HAS NOT BEEN BACK, HE HAS NOT LOOKED THE PLACE UP, AND THE PART OF THIS HE CANNOT PUT DOWN IS NOT THE NAME BUT THE CONDITION OF A MAN WHO HAS SPENT THREE DAYS IN A ROOM AND GONE OUT EVERY EVENING NOT KNOWING WHAT WAS IN IT.**

## 3. Two reasons for a stump, and neither of them said

- **HIS IS FROM JULY AND HE HAS NEVER TOLD IT.** She went down on the lip, was on the ground under a minute, got up and carried on up the parade, and he was the only person on that stretch of road.
- **HIS IS TWO YEARS OF A WOMAN STANDING IN THE SAME PLACE IN THE SAME WIND AND HE HAS NO NAME FOR HER.** She comes on weekday afternoons with something under her arm, does not go into anything, and goes up after about twenty minutes.
- **THEY AGREED AND SAID NOTHING, AND THE AGREEMENT WAS BETWEEN THEM AND NOT ABOUT THE STUMP.** Six sentences passed, all of them about roots and about who owned a machine. **THE TARMAC WENT BACK CROOKED, THE STUMP IS HALF AN INCH PROUDER, AND A BROKEN CORNER OF IT IS IN THE CHANNEL. NEITHER MAN HAS ANY IDEA THAT THE OTHER ONE HAS ANYTHING AT ALL.**

## 4. Four bulbs bought with a woman's own money

- **SHE PAID, AND SHE WAITED A WEEK AND A HALF WITH ONE OF THEM IN HER APRON BEFORE SHE USED IT, AND SHE HAS NEVER WORKED OUT WHY.** The woman of the ground floor gave her the same non-answer twice about a company for it.
- **HE PUT HIS HAND OUT INTO THE DARK AND COULD SEE IT, AND WENT UP, AND CAME BACK DOWN, AND STOOD THERE AGAIN.** That was his whole reaction and it took about two minutes.
- **SHE THEN DEALT WITH THREE THINGS IN THAT BUILDING THAT WERE NOT FOR HIM** — a bag that had been rained on, a door that had been catching for months, and a bulb that had been out longer than the landing had.
- **THEY SPOKE TWICE, ON TWO LANDINGS, IN FIVE WEEKS, AND SAID FOUR WORDS BETWEEN THEM.** **HE WILL NEVER FIND OUT, THE LANDING IS LIT FOUR MORNINGS AND DARK ON THE OTHER TWO, AND SHE IS THE ONLY PERSON IN THAT BUILDING WHO KNOWS ANY OF IT.**

## 5. A fence, a day, and the sentence he could not find

- **HE FOUND IT WITH HIS FOOT AT TEN PAST SIX IN THE MORNING IN JUNE AND IDENTIFIED IT IN ABOUT FOUR SECONDS.** He did not tell anybody at the time and he has not told anybody since.
- **HE SPENT THE SEVENTH OF SEPTEMBER ON IT ALONE, DIGGING INTO CLAY AND RAMMING BOTTOMS AND WASHING THE OLD LENGTHS AT A STANDPIPE, WHICH WAS THE LONGEST PART OF THE DAY.** He bent the heads off about fifty nails because the reason he was there was a nail in the dark.
- **HE PUT A WIRE ON THE TOP THAT THE FENCE DID NOT NEED, PUT THE TURF BACK THE RIGHT WAY UP, AND LEFT NOTHING ON ANY OF IT.** He charged nobody and he told nobody.
- **HE HAS BEEN WALKING PAST IT FOUR TIMES A DAY FOR A FORTNIGHT TRYING TO REDUCE THAT TO SOMETHING HE COULD SAY OUT LOUD.** **HE COULD NOT, AND BEING THE ONLY MAN WHO WAS GOING TO IS NOT A CLAIM ON ANYBODY, AND HE IS NOT GOING TO FIND A BETTER REASON AND GIVE IT TO ANYONE.**

## 6. Five people, one hour, one corner, four weeks

- **THEIR FIVE REASONS ARE UNLIKE EACH OTHER AND THE HOUR IS THE SAME, AND THE HOUR BELONGS TO A GABLE.** One of them has a plate and a preference for a lit table. One of them has a cigarette she will not light indoors. One of them has a cup and a reason not to put a hand on a wall in daylight. One of them has eaten alone too often in the middle of the day. One of them has been in a van since before seven.
- **ABOUT FORTY TIMES IN FOUR WEEKS AND NOT ONE COLLISION.** The only near miss was the man with the van finding the woman eight foot off and standing until she was finished, which he has thought about once and mentioned to nobody.
- **THERE IS NO LIST AND NOBODY KEEPS ONE.** **IT IS NOT A RULE AND NOT A ROTATION AND NOT A SCHEDULE, IT IS FIVE SEPARATE THINGS HAPPENING IN ONE PLACE, AND THAT GABLE WILL PUT ITS LIGHT ON THE SAME NINE FOOT OF BRICK TOMORROW AT THE SAME TEN MINUTES, AND A HANDFUL OF THEM WILL BE STANDING ON IT, AND NOT ONE OF THE FIVE WILL KNOW THAT ANY OF THE OTHER FOUR ARE.**

## 7. A true answer given flatly, and half of it taken

- **HE SAID WHAT HE HAD SEEN AND THEN SAID WHAT HE COULD NOT TELL HER, AND HE MEANT BOTH.** He had seen a stranger with two bags at a gate at half past eight and nothing else at all, and he had thought nothing at the time.
- **SHE REARRANGED A DELIVERY, A SHOP DAY, AN ERRAND, A QUESTION TO ANOTHER WOMAN AND A CONVERSATION WITH A MAN OF HER FATHER'S AGE, IN THAT ORDER, OVER SIX DAYS.** The sixth of those cost her, because the man decided inside a second that she had made it up, and she watched him do it.
- **SHE WENT OVER THE SIX DAYS AGAIN ON A SUNDAY NIGHT AND WORKED OUT HOW LITTLE SHE HAD ACTUALLY BEEN HANDED.** He found out nothing. On the twenty-fourth he came in at the usual time and she was exactly as she was. **NOT A SYLLABLE OF ANY OF IT HAS BEEN SAID BETWEEN THEM AND IT IS NOT GOING TO BE.**

## 8. A window, a bed, and six inch of carpet

- **HE TOOK THE BED OUT FOR ABOUT TEN MINUTES AND SAW THAT HE HAD DONE THE JOB.** The window went back a foot and a half with the bed clear of it. He said so. She said it was more than she had.
- **HE PUT THE BED BACK WITH THE PILLOW ON AND THE BLANKET FOLDED AND IT WENT BACK HALF AN INCH OUT OF LINE WITH TWO PALE RECTANGLES IN THE PILE.** Those rectangles have been there since April and they did not go with it.
- **HE DID THE ARITHMETIC IN A DOORWAY ON THE SATURDAY MORNING AND GAVE HIMSELF THREE REASONS FOR KEEPING IT TO HIMSELF, THE LAST OF WHICH IS THE ONE HE BELIEVES.** She has seen the marks and has not asked him about them and is not going to. **THE WINDOW IS FOUR INCH OPEN AND THE BED IS HERS, AND NEITHER OF THOSE TWO FACTS IS GOING TO CHANGE.**

## 9. One stool and two complete misreadings of it

- **IN THE MORNING HE READ IT AS SOMETHING PUT OUT BY SOMEBODY WHO WOULD COME BACK, HE CHECKED THE FRONT DOORS FOR A MAN AND FOUND NONE, AND HE LEFT AFTER A MINUTE AND CAME PAST TWICE MORE.**
- **AT NIGHT THE SECOND MAN READ IT AS A PLACE SOMEBODY HAS BEEN SITTING FOR A YEAR AND STOOD THERE ABOUT TWO MINUTES, AND HE COULD NOT HAVE TOLD YOU WHETHER THE OWNER HAD FORGOTTEN IT OR NEVER WANTED IT.**
- **BOTH OF THOSE THINGS WERE TRUE OF THE SAME STOOL ON THE SAME DAY.** It was gone by the Saturday and neither man asked anybody a single question about it. **They have spoken once since, in June, in a shop, about something else. There is no afternoon of the week on which one of them would raise it with the other, and neither is going to arrange one.**

## 10. Nine people on nothing, and a tray that came back up

- **NOT ONE OF THE NINE WAS THERE BECAUSE OF ANY OF THE OTHER EIGHT, AND NINE PEOPLE ON NOTHING IS THE NORMAL CONDITION OF THAT PARADE AND WAS NOT A FINDING.**
- **ABOUT A DOZEN ROLLS WENT INTO A CHANNEL OUTSIDE A SHOP BECAUSE A HEEL CAUGHT A FLAG, AND SIX OF THE NINE PICKED THEM UP, AND A CYCLIST TOOK ONE OFF THE PAVEMENT AND CARRIED ON, AND IT TOOK ABOUT FOUR MINUTES.** Nobody was told and nobody is going to be told, and the man who works nights was back up the road before the tray had reached the stack at the top.
- **ONE OF THE FOUR ANSWERS WENT OUT OF A MOUTH AT TEN PAST NINE AND CAME BACK AS ONE SYLLABLE.** There are four and there is no fifth, one of the four is carried a long way further than the other three together, the other three have not been out of a mouth since the February before last, and **NOBODY HERE HAS EVER SAID OUT LOUD WHICH QUESTION ANY ONE OF THE FOUR IS TRYING TO MEET.**
- **THE RULED SPACE UNDER THE LAST LINE IN THAT BOOK HAD BEEN OPEN FOR ONE THOUSAND FOUR HUNDRED AND SEVEN DAYS WHEN THE THIRD OF OCTOBER CAME, THAT ROOM WAS SHUT, AND NOBODY WENT ALONG THAT CORRIDOR.** There is one thing about this borough that no person living in it could put into words, it has not moved since the middle of August, and nobody is going to ask anybody about it.

## 1. A man in his forties, six years, and nobody knowing

- **NOBODY IN THAT BOROUGH KNOWS HE DOES IT, INCLUDING THE WOMAN WHO WATCHES HIM DO IT, AND HE HAS NEVER MENTIONED IT TO A PERSON AND IS NOT GOING TO.** It is not a service and it is not a favour and it is not on anything and it has no name.
- **HE STOPPED PART WAY UP ON ONE MORNING IN OCTOBER BECAUSE SOMETHING IN THE MIDDLE OF WHAT HE DOES WAS NOT AS HE HAD LEFT IT, AND HE COULD NOT MAKE IT FIT ANY OF THE FOUR THINGS HIS OWN HEAD OFFERED HIM.** He took all four on and dropped all four, and the fourth was about himself, and he went round it more than once before he left it.
- **HE PUT A HAND ON NOTHING, FINISHED WHAT WAS LEFT, SAID NOTHING TO THE WOMAN AT THE NEXT GATE, AND THE NEXT MORNING DID THE WHOLE OF IT FROM THE BOTTOM IN THE SEQUENCE HE ALWAYS USES AND DID NOT CHANGE PACE AT THAT PART.** HE WILL NOT GO BACK AND FIND OUT AND THE WOMAN AT THE GATE WILL NOT ASK AND NEITHER OF THEM HAS ANY IDEA WHAT IT WAS.
- **WHAT IS SITTING ON HIM IS NOT A NAME, BECAUSE THERE IS NO NAME IN IT. IT IS THE CONDITION OF A MAN WHO HAS DONE ONE THING EVERY DAY FOR SIX YEARS AND HAS BEEN SURPRISED BY IT ONCE.**

## 2. A woman who wants a room, and a man who worked it out

- **SHE HAS WANTED IT SINCE AUGUST AND HAS TOLD NOBODY, AND THE ONLY PERSON SHE HAS SPOKEN TO ABOUT IT IS THE WOMAN WHO HOLDS THE KEYS, AND SHE PUT ONE QUESTION AND WAS ANSWERED AND STOPPED DEAD ON PURPOSE.** A second question is what wanting turns into claiming and she knows it and did not ask it.
- **HER OWN TENANCY ENDS IN MARCH AND SHE HAS KNOWN THAT FOR TWO MONTHS AND HAS SAID NOTHING TO ANYBODY ABOUT EITHER THING.**
- **HE SAID ONE SENTENCE IN THAT ROOM AND IT WAS THAT IT IS A GOOD ROOM, AND HE ASKED HER NOTHING, AND HE LEFT. SHE PUT HERSELF IN HIS WAY ON THE STAIRS TO GET HIM IN THERE AND HE LET HER.**
- **HE UNDERSTOOD WHAT SHE WANTED WITHOUT BEING TOLD, ON THE ROOF, ON HIS OWN, AND HE TOLD NOBODY. HE COULD NOT HAVE KNOWN THAT AT HALF PAST FIVE SHE WAS STILL STANDING IN THERE, AND HE DID NOT GO UP AND LOOK.** SHE DOES NOT KNOW THAT HE UNDERSTOOD, BECAUSE A MAN WHO HAS UNDERSTOOD SOMETHING AND SAYS NOTHING IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A MAN WHO HAS NOT UNDERSTOOD ANYTHING.
- **THERE WAS A FORTNIGHT WHEN HE COULD HAVE SAID ONE WORD IN FOUR SECONDS AND SAID NOTHING, AND HE HAS GIVEN UP TRYING TO ACCOUNT FOR IT. THE ROOM IS STILL EMPTY AND THE TWO OF THEM HAVE NEVER DISCUSSED IT.**

## 3. A woman on her own in a yard, and a man behind a van

- **SHE DID NOT KNOW HOW TO TIE A LOAD FOR A SLOPE AND FOUND THAT OUT TWICE IN THE SAME WAY ON TWO CONSECUTIVE MORNINGS, AND SHE HAD NO REASON TO THINK IT WAS ANYTHING BUT SOMETHING SHE WAS BAD AT.**
- **HE WAS ABOUT TEN FOOT AWAY BEHIND HIS OWN VAN ON THE FIRST MORNING AND SAID NOTHING AND TOLD HIMSELF HE HAD NO REASON. ON THE SECOND HE HAD A FEW SECONDS IN WHICH ONE SENTENCE WOULD HAVE DONE IT AND HE SAID NOTHING IN THOSE TOO.**
- **HE SPENT THE BETTER PART OF A MINUTE BEING HONEST WITH HIMSELF ABOUT WHY, AND THE REASON IS A DECENT ONE: ANYTHING HE SAID WOULD HAVE HAD TO BE ADMITTED, AND BEING ADMITTED AT THAT MOMENT WOULD HAVE COST HER SOMETHING SHE DID NOT OWE HIM.**
- **ON THE THIRD MORNING SHE DID IT PROPERLY AND NOTHING SLIPPED. HE HAS NOT BEEN NEAR THAT END OF THE TOWN SINCE. SHE FINISHED THAT DAY'S WORK AND THOUGHT NOTHING MORE ABOUT EITHER MORNING AND WILL NEVER KNOW HE WAS THERE.**

## 4. Two years of the same dish, and eight words in a doorway

- **SHE HAS NOT CHANGED IT IN SEVEN MONTHS AND HAS CAUGHT HERSELF WANTING TO, AND TALKED HERSELF OUT OF IT, AND THE ARGUMENT SHE USED IS THAT A NEW DISH IS AN ATTEMPT AND AN ATTEMPT HAS AN OUTCOME AND SHE DOES NOT WANT THE OUTCOME.** Put it to her on a Wednesday and she would tell you that she is hungry and that there is a second person at that table.
- **HE STOPS EATING AFTER A COUPLE OF MOUTHFULS AND MAKES IT PLAIN THAT HE HAS FINISHED AND THEN TAKES A LITTLE MORE AFTER A WHILE, AND NOBODY IN THAT BUILDING CAN NAME WHAT IS WRONG WITH HIM.**
- **ON THE FIFTEENTH OF OCTOBER HE SAID, WITH TWO PLATES IN HER HANDS ON THE LANDING, THAT THERE WAS NO POINT IN IT. SHE TOLD HIM TO MIND HIS OWN. HE APOLOGISED FOR SOMEBODY WHO HAD NOT ASKED HIM TO AND SHUT THE DOOR BEHIND HIM PROPERLY.**
- **WHAT SHE CANNOT FORGIVE HERSELF FOR IS NOT THE RUDENESS. IT IS THAT HE WAS RIGHT, AND THAT A YEAR AGO SHE TOLD HIM PLAINLY SHE WAS NOT DOING IT ONE NIGHT AND HE SAID NOTHING AND WOULD HAVE EATEN SOME OF IT IF SHE HAD PUT IT DOWN, WHICH IS THE WHOLE OF WHAT HE WAS RIGHT ABOUT.** SHE HAS CARRIED A PLATE UP THOSE STAIRS TWICE A WEEK SINCE AND WILL NOT STOP.
- **ON THE SUNDAY AFTER THE FIFTEENTH SHE TOOK HIS PLATE AWAY BEFORE HE HAD FINISHED AND BINNED WHAT WAS LEFT OF IT AND WASHED IT AND CARRIED IT BACK, AND NEITHER OF THEM SAID ONE WORD.** HE HAS BEEN IN THAT FLAT TWICE SINCE ABOUT SOMETHING ELSE AND HAS NOT RAISED ANY OF IT.

## 5. A box, a wrong door, and two people who would not give way

- **HE HAS NOT OPENED IT AND HE IS EXPLICIT ABOUT WHY, BECAUSE IT IS THE FIRST THING ANYBODY WOULD THINK OF, AND HE HAS READ THE NAME ON THE SIDE OF IT ONLY FAR ENOUGH TO KNOW THAT THERE IS ONE.**
- **HE WOULD NOT PUT A STRANGER'S THINGS ON A STRANGER'S DOORSTEP, AND HE WOULD NOT CARRY THEM ROUND EITHER, AND THE SECOND OF THOSE IS NOT ABOUT THE MAN THEY BELONG TO. IT IS THAT HE CANNOT PRODUCE A REASON HE COULD SAY OUT LOUD.** AND SHE WOULD NOT TAKE IT BACK IN HER CAR AND CARRY IT ALONG THAT TERRACE ON HER OWN IN THE EVENING, AND HE COULD SEE THAT SHE WOULD NOT.
- **SHE CAME BACK THAT EVENING AND HE OFFERED AGAIN AND SHE DECLINED AGAIN. HE SAID HE DID NOT WANT IT IN HIS HALL AND SHE SAID IT WAS ONLY A BOX AND HE AGREED WITH HER.** NEITHER OF THEM SAID THE NEXT SENTENCE, WHICH WAS THAT IT WOULD BE IN THAT HALL UNTIL ONE OF THEM GAVE WAY, AND NEITHER OF THEM WAS GOING TO.
- **HE SAW A LIGHT IN THE FRONT ROOM OF THE HOUSE IT WAS FOR THAT AFTERNOON AND DID NOT GO OVER, AND HE HAS NOT PUT A HAND ON THAT DOOR IN FIVE YEARS, AND HE KNOWS THAT A LIGHT BEING ON IS NOT A REASON AND KNOWS IT IS NOT ONE.** THE MAN WHO LIVES THERE DOES NOT KNOW THAT ANYTHING CAME FOR HIM, AND THE HALL IS NARROW ENOUGH THAT HE NOW GOES DOWN IT SIDEWAYS.

## 6. Half a window, six years, and a wet morning

- **HE HAS DONE ONE HALF OF A SHOP WINDOW EVERY WEEKDAY MORNING FOR SIX YEARS AND NOBODY IN THAT SHOP HAS ANY IDEA, AND THE GLASS IS NOT CLEAN AFTERWARDS, IT IS ONLY CLEARER IN ONE PLACE, AND THE BLOOM COMES BACK OVER ABOUT THREE DAYS, AND NOBODY HAS EVER WONDERED ABOUT IT.**
- **SHE STARTED THE OTHER HALF ON THE TWENTY-NINTH OF OCTOBER AT TEN PAST SEVEN, AFTER HE HAD GONE TO WORK, AND HAS DONE IT ABOUT NINE TIMES, AND FROM THE ROAD THE TWO OF THEM READ AS ONE PERSON DOING ONE THING.**
- **HE STOPPED FOR ABOUT TWO SECONDS THE FIRST TIME HE SAW HER AND WENT ON AND HAS NOT MENTIONED IT SINCE, AND SHE HAS NOT MENTIONED IT, AND NEITHER OF THEM HAS EVER SAID TO THE OTHER THAT THEY KNOW.**
- **THE MAN IN HIS SIXTIES ASKED ON THE FIRST OF NOVEMBER WHO WAS DOING IT AND WAS GIVEN ONE HALF OF THE ANSWER AND SAID IT WAS GOOD FOR THE WINDOW, AND NEITHER OF THEM HAS MENTIONED THE OTHER HALF SINCE.** ON A WET MORNING NEITHER OF THEM DID IT AT ALL AND HE WENT TO WORK EXPECTING TO BE ANNOYED AT SOMEBODY AND WAS NOT, AND HE CANNOT ACCOUNT FOR THAT EITHER.

## 7. Nine words, thirty pounds, and no way to object

- **HE SAID WHAT WAS TRUE AND WHERE IT WAS TRUE AND NOTHING ELSE. THERE WAS NO WARNING BEYOND THE FACT, NO OFFER, AND NO STAYING, AND SHE SAID ONE WORD TO THE STREET AFTER HE HAD GONE.**
- **THERE WAS NOTHING IN IT FOR HER TO DECLINE, AND HE HAS BEEN OVER THAT MORE THAN ONCE AND CANNOT FIND THE SENTENCE SHE WOULD HAVE BEEN ABLE TO SAY NO TO. THAT IS WHY HE CANNOT RAISE AN OBJECTION NOW AND IT IS NOT MODESTY.**
- **SHE WENT AND LOOKED THAT AFTERNOON, FOUND HE WAS RIGHT, WORKED OUT WHAT IT WOULD COST, AND HAD IT DONE PROPERLY FOUR DAYS LATER OUT OF HER OWN MONEY, AT HER OWN PRICE, WITH HER OWN INSTRUCTIONS, AND TOLD NOBODY INCLUDING HIM.**
- **HE FOUND OUT FOUR DAYS LATER FROM A DISTANCE, BY SEEING THE RESULT AND UNDERSTANDING IT, AND THE ONLY THING AVAILABLE TO HIM WAS TO TELL HER SHE NEED NOT HAVE, WHICH WOULD HAVE MADE IT A THING BETWEEN THEM.** SHE HAS NOT TOLD HIM AND HE HAS NOT ASKED AND NEITHER IS GOING TO RAISE IT.

## 8. A man who stopped in the middle of a job, and a bill for all of it

- **THE DOOR SIDE WENT WELL AND WAS DONE IN UNDER TWO HOURS. THE LOCK SIDE WOULD NOT GO IN BECAUSE THE EDGE OF THAT DOOR IS TIMBER THAT HAS MOVED WITH THE WEATHER FOR EIGHT YEARS, AND THE PROPER WORK IS A MACHINE IN A VAN OR THE FRAME OUT OF THE WALL, AND HE HAS DONE BOTH AND IS NOT AFRAID OF EITHER.**
- **HE STOPPED IN THE MIDDLE AND HAS NEVER BEEN ABLE TO ACCOUNT FOR IT IN A WAY HE BELIEVES. HIS FIRST REASON WAS HIS HANDS AND HE DOES NOT BELIEVE THAT OF HIMSELF. THE REASON UNDERNEATH IS ONE HE WILL NOT SAY OUT LOUD, AND IT IS THAT THE JOB CAN BE FINISHED IN ABOUT TWENTY MINUTES ON ANY DRY DAY FOR THE WHOLE OF THE NEXT EIGHT MONTHS, AND THE ONLY THING IN ITS WAY IS NOISE IN A LANDING IN A BUILDING WHERE SOMEBODY LIVES, AND HE WAS NOT GOING TO CARRY THE TOOL UP TWO FLIGHTS TO MAKE IT ON A SATURDAY MORNING.**
- **SHE CAME IN AT ONE IN THE AFTERNOON, FOUND THE DOOR HUNG AND NOTHING IN THE FRAME WHERE THE LOCK SHOULD HAVE BEEN, ASKED NEXT DOOR ONE QUESTION AND GOT AN ANSWER, AND SAID NOTHING FURTHER.** SHE DID NOT TELEPHONE HIM AND DID NOT GO TO HIS VAN.
- **HE WENT BACK FOUR DAYS LATER WITH THE TOOL IN HIS BAG, HAVING KNOWN IT WAS IN THE BAG ON THE MONDAY, AND SHE OPENED THE DOOR BEFORE HE HAD KNOCKED. EIGHT WORDS EACH AND NOT ONE OF THEM ABOUT THE LOCK. HE STUDIED THAT DOOR'S EDGE FOR A MINUTE AND A HALF WITH HIS HANDS IN HIS POCKETS AND LEFT WITHOUT DOING ANYTHING TO IT.** SHE HAS NOT ASKED HIM AGAIN, AND HE TOOK THE SUM THEY HAD AGREED FOR THE JOB AND NEITHER OF THEM MENTIONED THE PART THAT WAS NOT DONE.

## 9. Two men, nine sentences, and nobody to ring

- **THEY FOUND THEMSELVES AT THE SAME WALL AT THE SAME TIME ON THE FOURTEENTH OF NOVEMBER AND NEITHER HAD COME THERE ON PURPOSE, AND IN ABOUT FOUR MINUTES THEY ESTABLISHED THAT THE PLATE ON THAT WALL NAMES A BUSINESS THAT HAS NOT EXISTED FOR SOME YEARS AND NEVER HAD ANYTHING TO DO WITH THE BUILDING IT IS ON.**
- **THEY BOTH WANTED IT OFF THE WALL AND NEITHER OF THEM DID ANYTHING ABOUT IT AND NEITHER OF THEM INTENDS TO, AND THE REASONS ARE THE SAME AND NEITHER OF THEM HAD TO SAY THEM.**
- **THE MAN IT BELONGS TO IS SOMEBODY NEITHER OF THEM KNOWS AND NEITHER HAS ANY BUSINESS APPROACHING. AND THE LAST PERSON WHO REMOVED ANYTHING FROM A WALL ON THAT STREET WAS PUT BACK ON IT BY A MAN IN A HI-VIS WHO WROTE A NAME AND A DATE ON A FOLDED PAPER AND PUT THE PAPER INSIDE A DOOR, AND ONE OF THE TWO OF THEM WAS TOLD ABOUT IT BY THE OTHER ON THAT PAVEMENT.**
- **ONE OF THEM SAID OUT LOUD THAT THERE IS NOBODY TO RING AND THAT WAS THE END OF IT. THEY DID NOT DISCUSS WHAT TO DO BECAUSE THERE IS NOTHING TO DISCUSS.** THE PLATE IS STILL ON THE WALL. IT WAS THERE ON THE FRIDAY AND ON THE SUNDAY AND ON THE SATURDAY AFTER, AND ON THE SATURDAY AFTER THE TWO OF THEM WERE INSIDE THREE HUNDRED YARD OF THAT CORNER TOGETHER AND NEITHER OF THEM SPOTTED THE OTHER. **NOTHING ON PAPER ANYWHERE IN THIS BOROUGH REFERS TO IT AND NOTHING EVER WILL.**

## 10. Nine people on a parade, and a door off a wall

- **NOT ONE OF THE NINE WAS THERE BECAUSE OF ANY OF THE OTHER EIGHT, AND THE SHOPS THAT WERE OPEN WERE OPEN BECAUSE THEIR OWNERS HAD DECIDED TO OPEN THEM.**
- **A SIDE DOOR THAT HAD BEEN HARD TO SHUT SINCE THE SUMMER CAME OFF ITS TOP HINGE AT ABOUT TEN PAST FIVE IN FRONT OF PEOPLE, AND IT IS NOT THE SORT OF NOISE ANYBODY RUNS FROM, AND ABOUT NINE PEOPLE HEARD IT AND FIVE OF THEM TURNED ROUND. THREE MEN GOT IT HUNG AGAIN IN ABOUT TWENTY MINUTES ON A LONGER SCREW, INTO BETTER BRICK, WITH THE PLATE ABOUT AN INCH AND A HALF FROM WHERE IT HAD BEEN. WHAT CAME AWAY IN PIECES WENT INTO A BAG, AND THAT BAG WENT INTO A BIN.**
- **IT IS HOLDING AND IT IS NOT RIGHT, THE MAN WHOSE DOOR IT IS HAS NOT BEEN TOLD, NOBODY TELEPHONED ANYBODY, AND THE ONLY THING SAID ABOUT IT ON THAT PARADE WAS ONE WORD BY THE WOMAN WITH THE PRAM, WHICH THE MAN WHO CAUSED IT DOES NOT KNOW ABOUT.**
- **THE FOUR ANSWERS WENT NOWHERE THAT AFTERNOON. FOUR IS STILL FOUR, NOBODY ADDED A FIFTH, NOBODY PUT ANY TWO OF THEM SIDE BY SIDE, AND NOBODY PUT THE QUESTION BEHIND THEM TO ANYBODY. THE FOURTH ANSWER WENT OUT OF A MOUTH AT TEN PAST NINE ON THE SEVENTEENTH OF NOVEMBER AND WAS ANSWERED WITH ONE SYLLABLE.** 
- **AT THE END OF A CORRIDOR IN A BUILDING BY THAT WATER THERE IS A ROOM, AND IT IS SHUT, AND IT HAS BEEN SHUT ALL WEEK. A BOOK ON A SHELF IN IT HAS NINETEEN ENTRIES IN IT AND HAS HAD THEM SINCE MARCH. THE SPACE RULED UNDER THE LAST LINE HAD BEEN OPEN FOR ONE THOUSAND FOUR HUNDRED AND FIFTY-TWO DAYS, WHICH IS NOT A FIGURE THAT ANYBODY IN THIS BOROUGH CARRIES ABOUT, AND NOBODY WENT ALONG THAT CORRIDOR AND NOBODY MARKED IT.** A GREEN STEEL STRUCTURE AT THE BACK OF THAT PARADE HAS A PADLOCK ON IT AND A DANGER SIGN AND A FOOT SQUARE OF GRAVEL IN IT, AND IT IS NOT A LOCK-UP AND NOT A ROOM WITH A BENCH, AND NOBODY WENT NEAR IT AND THE PADLOCK HAS NOT MOVED. **There is one thing about all of this that no person living in this borough could name, and it has not altered by so much as one day since the middle of August, and no one has said a word about it and no one is going to.**
