## 1. Nine foot of ground

- **SHE HAD IT IN OCTOBER AND DID NOT ASK FOR IT, AND HE HAS WANTED IT SINCE THE END OF OCTOBER AND HAS NEVER PUT ANYTHING ON IT, AND NEITHER OF THEM HAS EVER SAID A WORD ABOUT IT TO THE OTHER.** She had about eight pieces of a removal out of her mother's house put on that ground on a Tuesday in October because there was nowhere else in that street to put them, and she has not put a foot on it since and has not knocked on a door.
- **HE PUT HIS THINGS DOWN AGAINST THAT WALL ON THE TWENTIETH OF NOVEMBER AND TOOK THEM OFF AGAIN INSIDE TWO MINUTES, AND LEFT THE REST OF THE GROUND AS HE FOUND IT.** He could have done otherwise. He had his hands empty and nothing in the way.
- **THEY WERE BOTH WITHIN ABOUT TEN FOOT OF THAT GROUND INSIDE HALF AN HOUR OF EACH OTHER AND NEITHER OF THEM SPOKE, AND IT WAS STILL EMPTY AT SIX O'CLOCK.**
- **NEITHER OF THEM HAS THE OTHER'S HALF.** He has never set eyes on her. She has never seen where his things go or who lets them go there. They reached the same stopping place by different roads and neither has heard where the other one reached it.
- **HE KEEPS WHAT HE NEEDS TO STACK TWO STREETS OFF EVERY WEEKDAY, AND GETTING IT OUT AND BACK COSTS HIM ABOUT HALF AN HOUR A DAY HE DOES NOT HAVE, AND HE IS STILL DOING IT.**

## 2. A store door, and a jar

- **HE SHUT A DOOR ON A DRAUGHT IN A KITCHEN ON THE TWENTY-FIFTH OF NOVEMBER AND BEHIND IT WAS A STORE WITH ABOUT THIRTY BOXES IN IT AND TWO OF THEM ALREADY OPEN, AND HE HAS TOLD NO PERSON IN THIS BOROUGH WHAT HE SAW.**
- **WHAT HE CARRIES IS A RING IN THE DUST ON ONE OF THOSE BOXES, WHICH SOMETHING LEAVES BY STANDING IN ONE PLACE FOR A FORTNIGHT, AND THERE WAS NOTHING IN THAT ROOM TO LEAVE IT AND NOWHERE IN THAT ROOM FOR IT TO HAVE STOOD.** He did not go back and look. He has not opened that door again and he is not going to.
- **HE HAS DRIVEN PAST THAT BUILDING FOUR TIMES SINCE FROM THE FAR END OF THE STREET AND HAS NOT SLOWED DOWN, AND HE HAS NOT ASKED THE NEIGHBOUR A SINGLE QUESTION.**
- **SHE PUT THE BOXES TO HIM ON THE TWENTY-FIRST OF NOVEMBER AND HE GAVE HER A ONE-WORD ANSWER THAT WAS NOT THE ONE SHE WAS AFTER, AND SHE LET IT GO, AND NEITHER OF THEM HAS RAISED IT SINCE, AND SHE DOES NOT KNOW HE WAS EVER IN THAT STORE.**
- **HE HAS BEEN BACK TWICE SINCE, AND HAS DONE AND SAID EXACTLY WHAT HE DID AND SAID BEFORE, AND GONE HOME AT THE TIME HE ALWAYS GOES HOME.**

## 3. Six minutes the long way

- **SHE HAS BEEN GOING THE OTHER WAY TO WORK EVERY WEEKDAY SINCE THE MIDDLE OF NOVEMBER, WHICH IS ABOUT A HUNDRED AND THIRTY YARD AND SIX MINUTES, AND NOBODY ON THAT STREET HAS said one word to her about any of it.**
- **THE REASON IS A WOMAN IN ONE OF NINE HOUSES WHO USED TO STAND AT A GAP IN A WALL AT HALF PAST SEVEN EVERY MORNING AND HAS NOT BEEN THERE FOR ABOUT FOUR MONTHS, AND SHE HAS NEVER SPOKEN TO THAT WOMAN AND HAS NEVER SPOKEN TO ANYBODY ABOUT HER.**
- **BETWEEN FOUR AND NINE PEOPLE ARE ON THAT STREET IN THAT HALF HOUR AND EVERY ONE OF THEM HAS SEEN HER WALK IT, AND ON THE TWENTY-SECOND OF NOVEMBER A MAN WHO USUALLY SAYS GOOD MORNING SAID GOOD MORNING AND NOTHING ELSE.**
- **SHE WILL NOT OPEN THE SUBJECT HERSELF, AND SHE KNOWS A THING DONE TEN TIMES IS A HABIT, AND BY THE MIDDLE OF THAT MONTH IT WILL NOT BE A DECISION ANY MORE.**
- **THERE IS NOTHING TO UNDO, BECAUSE SHE WAS THE ONLY PERSON KEEPING ANYTHING.** If she went back the other way in the morning, the street would not have noticed by the end of the month and would have stopped noticing inside two months altogether.

## 4. A door, and a fortnight

- **FOR SIX YEARS HE TOOK THAT DOOR THROUGH WITH HIM AND LET IT SHUT BEHIND HIM, AND FOR FOUR MONTHS SHE LET IT GO EVERY TIME, AND NEITHER OF THEM HAD EVER PUT EITHER HALF OF IT TO THE OTHER.**
- **ON THE FOURTH OF DECEMBER SHE HELD IT OPEN FOR HIM AND IT SHUT ON ITS OWN BEFORE HIS HAND GOT TO THE FRAME, AND HE WORKED OUT FROM THOSE TWO SECONDS THAT SHE HAD DONE IT FIRST.**
- **HE WAITED FOURTEEN DAYS AND THEN LET IT GO HIMSELF, DELIBERATELY, IN THE MIDDLE OF THE STAIR, AND WENT UP THE PASSAGE WITH THE NOISE BEHIND HIM.**
- **SHE HEARD IT AND DID NOT GO BACK, AND SHE HAS SINCE WORKED OUT THAT SHE WAS THE FIRST AND HE KNOWS SHE WAS THE FIRST AND NEITHER OF THEM HAS SAID A WORD ABOUT ANY OF IT IN FIVE WEEKS.**
- **THE ONLY WORDS THEY HAVE EXCHANGED SINCE THE FOURTH OF DECEMBER ARE "EVENING" AND ABOUT NINE OTHERS, NONE OF WHICH WAS ABOUT THAT DOOR.**
- **NEITHER WILL BE THE ONE TO SAY SO, AND THE REASONS ARE NOT THE SAME: SHE WILL NOT TURN IT INTO AN AGREEMENT IN A BUILDING OF FOURTEEN FLATS, AND HE CANNOT STAND THERE AND FIND OUT WHETHER BEING GLAD ABOUT IT IS A THING HE IS GLAD ABOUT.**

## 5. A true answer to the wrong question

- **ON THE TENTH OF DECEMBER, AT TWENTY TO NINE IN THE MORNING, SHE ASKED HIM WHETHER ANYBODY ELSE WAS IN THAT BUILDING AT NIGHT, AND HE SAID "NOT THAT I'VE SEEN," AND HE MEANT IT.**
- **WHAT HE HAD ACTUALLY DONE IS GONE UP THAT STAIR IN DAYLIGHT ABOUT A HUNDRED AND FORTY TIMES AND BEEN IN IT IN THE EVENING TWICE.** He did not lift a grate, put anything down it, or put a hand in anything. He read it from about nine foot off and he could not have said so without claiming to have looked.
- **FOUR DAYS LATER HE WORKED OUT THAT SHE WAS ASKING ABOUT SOMETHING ELSE ENTIRELY**, because she sleeps at the front and that stair is at the back, and because there is a woman two floors above her who is about at all hours and a man below her who comes in very late twice a week.
- **HE CANNOT PUT THE ANSWER BACK AND THE ANSWER IS NOT FALSE AND WILL NEVER BE FALSE, WHICH IS THE WHOLE OF WHY HE CANNOT PUT IT BACK.**
- **SHE HAS ASKED HIM NOTHING AT ALL SINCE, AND NOT ONE OF THOSE ABSENCES HAS ANYTHING TO DO WITH HIM, AND HE IS NOT GOING TO GO AND TELL HER HE WAS THE WRONG PERSON BECAUSE HE DOES NOT KNOW WHAT THAT WOULD LEAVE HER WITH.**
- **THE MAN WHOSE PREMISES THAT IS CANNOT GET DOWN THE STEPS HIMSELF AND HAS NOT ASKED HIM ANYTHING EITHER, AND HE IS NOT AWARE OF ANY OF THIS.**

## 6. Number nine, worked out from outside

- **SHE HAS SPENT SEVEN WEEKS ESTABLISHING FROM THE OTHER SIDE OF THAT STREET THAT NUMBER NINE IS NOT EMPTY, OUT OF FOUR THINGS SHE CAN SEE OR HEAR, AND SHE HAS SAID IT TO NOBODY.**
- **THE FOUR THINGS ARE WASHING ON THAT ROOF FOUR DAYS OUT OF SEVEN, A BLIND THAT COMES DOWN HALF AN INCH EVERY AFTERNOON AND NEVER MOVES, A SOUND THROUGH THE PASSAGE FOUR TIMES A FORTNIGHT, AND A WOMAN AT NUMBER EIGHT WHO HAS A KEY FOR THE YARD AND HAS NOT LOOKED ACROSS ONCE.**
- **SHE HAS ALSO ESTABLISHED THAT THE MAN WITH THE CUP GOES AT THAT SHOP DOOR AND THAT TWICE SHE WAS ALMOST CERTAIN HE HAD A KEY, AND HE HAS SAID NOTHING TO HER IN SEVEN WEEKS AND WOULD NOT KNOW HER NAME.**
- **SHE CANNOT TELL THE WOMAN AT NUMBER EIGHT BECAUSE HOW SHE KNOWS IS THAT SHE HAS BEEN WATCHING THAT BUILDING SINCE OCTOBER, AND SHE CANNOT PUT IT TO THE MAN WITH THE CUP EITHER, FOR THE SAME REASON AND A WEAKER ONE, AND THERE IS NOBODY ELSE ON THAT STREET SHE COULD PUT IT TO.**
- **she has been carrying it since early November and and it has weighed on her every day and will weigh on her tomorrow, AND THE BUILDING HAS NOT CHANGED.**

## 7. A wire in a joint, twice

- **ON THE TENTH OF DECEMBER AT TWENTY PAST EIGHT A MAN IN HIS FORTIES BENT A PIECE OF WIRE AND TWISTED IT INTO THE JOINT BESIDE THE SEVENTH SLAB IN A PATH BETWEEN TWO BLOCKS, AND TOLD NOBODY.**
- **ON THE TWELFTH AT HALF PAST FIVE IN THE EVENING A MAN IN HIS THIRTIES FOUND IT HAD GONE PROUD AGAIN AND DID EXACTLY THE SAME THING WITH A PIECE OF WIRE FROM THE BOTTOM OF HIS OWN BAG, AND TOLD NOBODY, AND HE HAS SINCE SPENT EVERY DAY WONDERING WHO DID IT FIRST IN DAYLIGHT.**
- **HE HAS RULED OUT EVERYBODY HE KNOWS AND HE HAS ALSO RULED OUT ANYBODY OUT OF EITHER BLOCK BECAUSE HE CANNOT STAND HAVING BEEN WATCHED FOR NINE YEARS, AND THAT IS WHERE HE STOPS.**
- **A CAR LIFTED THE SLAB OUT OF THE PATH ON THE SUNDAY THE SIXTEENTH AND LEFT IT OFF THE PATH FOR THREE DAYS.** A woman on the first floor of that block found the gap on the Tuesday afternoon, looked at it, and kept it to herself, and is not going to raise it.
- **ON THE WEDNESDAY HE PUT THE SLAB BACK AND PUT HIS OWN WIRE IN AGAIN, BECAUSE A MAN WHO FINDS SOMEBODY HAS DONE THE EXACT THING HE DID CANNOT DO IT DIFFERENTLY AFTERWARDS.**
- **NOBODY IS KEEPING ANYTHING, THERE IS NO LIST OF THAT GROUND, AND THE WHOLE OF WHAT HE DID WILL COME UP AGAIN BEFORE LONG, AND ONE OF THOSE TWO MEN WILL LOOK AT IT WHEN IT DOES AND ONE WILL NOT.**

## 8. A wall, and a sentence about it

- **HE DID THE WHOLE OF A LENGTH OF WALL EXCEPT THE FOOT OF IT, AND THE FOOT OF IT IS THE PART THAT IS UNDER THE PIPE, AND HE IS NOT A MAN WHO TAKES PIPES OFF WALLS EASILY BUT HE IS NOT A MAN WHO CANNOT EITHER.**
- **HE REPORTED THE JOB FINISHED ON THE FRIDAY, FROM A LADDER, TO A MAN WHO WROTE IT DOWN AND WENT AWAY, AND IT WAS INVOICED AND PAID IN FULL. The man from the company was in that building about four minutes and does not know it and is not going to be in it again.**
- **HE HAS NOT GONE BACK IN THE FORTY DAYS SINCE, HAVING THOUGHT OF IT ABOUT NINE TIMES, AND THE REASON IS NOT THAT THE PIPE IS DIFFICULT AND HE HAS TAKEN PIPE OFF WALLS ABOUT THIRTY TIMES.**
- **SHE SAW THE JOIN ON THE MONDAY TWENTY-FOURTH, WENT BACK UP TO HER FLAT, WORKED OUT WHAT THE ONLY USEFUL QUESTION WOULD BE, AND DECIDED NOT TO ASK IT, AND HAS BEEN THROUGH IT TWICE SINCE AND ARRIVED WHERE SHE DID THE FIRST TIME.**
- **THE REASON HE WILL NOT SAY IS THE FOUR FOOT OF THAT WALL FURTHER UP THAT NOBODY HAS EVER PROPERLY LOOKED AT, AND THAT ANY MENTION OF THE FOOT OF IT WOULD HAVE PUT SOMETHING ELSE ON A DOCKET IN A BUILDING THAT NOBODY IN THIS BOROUGH IS RESPONSIBLE FOR.**
- **WHAT SHE COULD HAVE TO ASK IS NOT WHY HE LEFT IT. IT IS WHETHER THAT PIPE WANTS DOING, AND THAT IS A DIFFERENT QUESTION, and she is not going to be the person who PUTS IT.**

## 9. Four inches, and the wrong foot

- **SHE SAW HIM CROSS A STEP OVER RUNNING WATER TWICE, ON THE SECOND AND THE SIXTEENTH OF DECEMBER, FROM HER OWN FRONT WINDOW, AND ON THE FIRST OCCASION SHE DID NOT KNOW IT WAS A THING AT ALL.**
- **ON THE TWENTY-NINTH OF DECEMBER SHE DID IT AT TEN PAST NINE AND GOT IT WRONG**, because half of what he does does not transfer to her body at all, and she came down into four inch of moving water because of that.
- **HE WAS NINE FOOT BEHIND HER AND DID NOT SLOW AND DID NOT LOOK UP AND HAS NEVER ONCE LOOKED UP IN THAT STREET.**
- **SHE HAS BEEN OVER IT NINE TIMES SINCE, FOUR OF THEM RIGHT, and is not going to let that put her off, AND WHAT SHE SAID TO HERSELF ABOUT IT IS THAT A MAN WHO CROSSES THAT WATER WITHOUT STOPPING IS A MAN WHO IS NOT WATCHING HER, AND THAT IS THE PART THAT IS KEEPING HER AT IT.**
- **SHE HAS ALSO WORKED OUT WHAT HE WOULD HAVE THOUGHT OF HER IF HE HAD LOOKED UP, AND SHE DOES NOT LIKE THE ANSWER, AND SHE IS GOING TO GO ON CROSSING IT ANYWAY.**

## 10. A Thursday, and iron off a wall

- **NINE PEOPLE WERE on that parade in that stretch of the morning AND NOT ONE OF THEM WAS THERE BECAUSE OF ANY OF THE OTHER EIGHT.**
- **A PAINTED LENGTH OF IRON CAME OFF THE FRONT OF A PREMISES AT THE TOP END AT HALF PAST TWELVE, HIT NOBODY, WAS HEARD BY ABOUT EIGHT PEOPLE AND TURNED ROUND BY ABOUT TWO, AND WAS NOT A SOUND ANYBODY RAN FROM.**
- **THREE MEN HAD IT BACK UP IN ABOUT TEN MINUTES ON DIFFERENT FIXINGS AND LONGER SCREWS, OUT OF LINE WITH WHERE IT HAD BEEN, AND THE STEP IT PROTECTS IS PROTECTED, AND IT WILL NOT LOOK RIGHT FROM the way a person who knew the wall would notice STOOD THERE BEFORE THE THIRD OF JANUARY.**
- **NOBODY RANG ANYBODY, THE OWNER OF THAT PREMISES WAS NEVER TOLD, SHE CAME IN AT ABOUT TWO AND PUT HER HAND FLAT ON IT AND WENT IN, AND THE ONLY WORD SAID ABOUT IT AT THAT TOP END WAS ONE WORD FROM THE WOMAN WITH THE DOG, AND THE MAN WHO WAS STANDING THERE WHEN SHE SAID IT DID NOT HEAR IT.**
- **THE FOUR ANSWERS WENT NOWHERE THAT AFTERNOON. FOUR IS STILL FOUR, NOBODY ADDED A FIFTH, NOBODY PUT ANY TWO OF THEM SIDE BY SIDE, AND NOBODY PUT THE QUESTION BEHIND THEM TO A PERSON.**
- **AT THE END OF A PASSAGE IN A BUILDING BY THAT WATER THERE IS A ROOM AND A BOOK ON A SHELF IN IT WITH NINETEEN ENTRIES IN IT AND THE SPACE UNDER THE LAST LINE HAD BEEN OPEN ONE THOUSAND FOUR HUNDRED AND NINETY-NINE DAYS WHEN THE THIRD OF JANUARY CAME, AND NOBODY WENT ALONG THAT PASSAGE AND NOBODY MARKED IT.** A small building at the top end of that parade is shut and has been for some time and there is nothing in it worth the opening, and nobody went near it that afternoon and the padlock is where it has always been. **There is one thing about all of this that no person living in this borough could name, and it has not altered by so much as a day since the middle of August, and no one has said a word about it and no one is going to.**

## 1. The woman and the animal behind the wall

- **SHE HAS HAD IT SHUT IN SINCE BEFORE CHRISTMAS AND HAS GIVEN NOBODY A REASON.** There is a woman next door who would have taken it in and was not asked, and there was an arrangement about the door that has simply stopped.
- **HE WENT THE OTHER WAY FOR A FORTNIGHT AND THEN STOPPED, AND HE HAS NOT ASKED HER OR ANYBODY ELSE WHAT BECAME OF IT.** He was not being cautious. He has never known where it went because he has never been on that side of the wall at that hour in his life.
- **SHE HAS SEEN IT TWICE FROM HER OWN FRONT WINDOW AND HAS NOT LEFT THE HOUSE EITHER TIME.** She works afternoons and is out from one.
- **WHAT EACH OF THEM IS CARRYING IS HALF OF SOMETHING AND THE OTHER HALF IS ON THE FAR SIDE OF A BOUNDARY WALL.** He thinks there is a cat in a street somewhere. She thinks there is a man who noticed. Neither of them has said a word and neither is going to.

## 2. The two people under the top floor

- **HE HAD A THEORY ABOUT A NOISE AND WAS WRONG IN A DIRECTION HE CANNOT EXPLAIN TO ANYBODY.** Six years of lying in a bed under it produced a woman asleep. She was not asleep.
- **SHE HAD A THEORY ABOUT A MAN ON THE GROUND FLOOR AND WAS WRONG IN THE SAME DIRECTION.** Eight months of lying awake listening produced a man in bed by one. He was at the top of the stairs at twenty to three.
- **EACH OF THEM LEARNED ONE THING ON ONE NIGHT AND HAS CARRIED IT ALONE SINCE.** What he learned is where she goes. What she learned is that she goes.
- **NEITHER WILL RAISE IT WITH HER AND THE TWO REASONS ARE NOT THE SAME, AND THE SECOND ONE IS WORSE THAN THE FIRST.** He does not want to be the reason a person starts listening to a stair. She decided last autumn that somebody lying awake since half past two is entitled to be left alone.
- **SHE IS IN THAT BUILDING AND AWAKE MOST OF THOSE HOURS AND BOTH OF THEM KNOW SHE IS.** That is the part neither of them can put to anybody.

## 3. The noise at half past five

- **HE DID IT FOR NINE YEARS BEFORE ANYBODY SAID ANYTHING AND HE IS STILL DOING IT.** She asked once and he stopped for a week.
- **SHE SAID SEVEN WORDS AND HAS SAID NOTHING SINCE, AND HE KNOWS EXACTLY HOW LONG IT HAS BEEN.** There is a change in the way she says good morning to him and he has noticed it and has not asked what it means.
- **HE RESUMED IT KNOWING THAT SHE CAN NO LONGER ASK, AND THE KNOWING IS WHAT HE HAS DONE IT ON.** He worked out the reason she will not ask without being told it.
- **HE MOVED SOMETHING ABOUT HIS OWN VEHICLE AFTERWARDS AND HAS PUT IT BACK TWICE.** He has no account of that he would give a person.
- **THE PERSON WHO COULD HAVE INTERVENED AND WAS NEVER ASKED IS THE OWNER OF THAT FLAT, AND HE HAS NOT BEEN TOLD ANY OF IT.**

## 4. The side of the landing

- **SHE CHOSE A SIDE OF A MAN IN 2013 AND HAS NEVER EXPLAINED WHY, INCLUDING TO HIMSELF, INCLUDING IN THE SIX YEARS SINCE.** The reason involved something she wanted to say once.
- **HE TOLD HER, PLAINLY AND WITHOUT ANY EDGE, THAT HE HEARS HER ON THAT SIDE AND HAS FOR A QUARTER OF A CENTURY.** He has been repeating everything she says and has been blamed for nothing.
- **HE THEN TOLD HER THAT HE HEARD HER IN 2013 AS WELL, WHICH SHE HAS NOW SPENT FIVE MONTHS REGARDING.** She does not know whether that minute and a half in 2013 was two people talking or one person talking to a wall, and she cannot find out without giving away why she picked that side.
- **SHE IS GOING TO KEEP THAT SIDE AND NOBODY IN THAT BUILDING IS AWARE THAT SHE HAS DECIDED ANYTHING.** The man on the ground floor sees them two or three times a day and has never wondered.
- **HE IS NOT CROSSING HER FOR IT.** He came back down a step to tell her, which is not something he had planned to do.

## 5. The thing on the kerb

- **HE PUT SOMETHING OUT OF HIS OWN HOUSE EVERY WEEKDAY FOR SIX YEARS AND WALKED ON, AND A WOMAN FOUR DOORS AWAY BROUGHT IT BACK IN EVERY DAY OF THAT WITHOUT EITHER OF THEM MENTIONING IT.** It belonged to his mother, it is not good, and it will not go in the room he sleeps in.
- **ON ONE MORNING IN JANUARY HE LEFT IT AND WALKED ON AND DID NOT COME BACK.** He has driven past it and has not got out of the vehicle on that side of that road since.
- **SHE CAME OUT AT ONE AND DID NOT TOUCH IT.** She has been through her reasons twice and has told them to nobody, and one of the reasons is about herself and not about the twenty-fifth of January.
- **HE WILL NOT ASK HER WHY SHE USED TO TAKE IT IN AND SHE WILL NOT ASK HIM WHY HE USED TO PUT IT OUT.** Asking either would turn six years of a habit into a thing that happened between them.
- **HE HAS NO REASON HE WOULD GIVE A PERSON FOR THE WAY HE NOW PARKS AND HE HAS BEEN DRIVING PAST IT EVERY DAY SINCE.**

## 6. The two minutes and the window

- **HE HAS DONE THE SAME THING OUTSIDE HIS OWN HOUSE EVERY MORNING FOR SIX YEARS AND NOBODY HAS EVER ASKED HIM AND HE WILL NOT BE ASKED.** It began in 2013 and it has a reason in another town eight miles off that he has never given to anybody.
- **SHE HAS BEEN AT A WINDOW SHE LIKES FOR SIX YEARS AND DID NOT KNOW UNTIL THE SEVENTEENTH OF JANUARY THAT SHE WAS WATCHING A PERSON.** She has never spoken to him and does not know what he is called.
- **HE LOOKED UP ONCE, FOR ABOUT A SECOND, AND SHE DID NOT MOVE, AND NEITHER HAS RAISED IT IN THIRTEEN DAYS.** There is no arrangement here because no words have passed between them.
- **SHE IS NOT GOING TO STOP AND HE IS NOT GOING TO LOOK UP, AND BOTH OF THEM HAVE DECIDED THAT WITHOUT DISCUSSING IT.** If she stops he will understand why. If he looks up there is nothing on her side of the glass to answer with.
- **WHAT HE GETS OUT OF THOSE TWO MINUTES IS NOT SOMETHING HE WOULD DESCRIBE AS SORROW AND WOULD BE ANNOYED AT ANYBODY WHO DID.**

## 7. The machine and the two floors

- **THE OLDER OF THE TWO WOMEN HAS BEEN LIVING UNDER IT FOR TWO YEARS AND NINE MONTHS AND HAS TOLD NO PERSON IN THAT BUILDING OR OUTSIDE IT, INCLUDING A LIE.** She complains about other things loudly and has never raised this one.
- **THE YOUNGER HAS BEEN UNDER IT SINCE CHRISTMAS AND HAS ALSO TOLD NOBODY, AND WHAT SHE TOLD HERSELF WAS WRONG IN A WAY THAT DOES NOT MATTER.** The noise is the machine and not the man in the kitchen below her.
- **A MAN AT THE BACK OF THAT BUILDING CHANGED A PART AND MOVED A TIMER ON A TUESDAY IN JANUARY AND WAS THINKING ABOUT THE PART.** He is not doing either of them a favour and he does not know they exist.
- **BOTH WOMEN FOUND OUT WITHIN A FORTNIGHT OF EACH OTHER AND NEITHER KNEW THAT THE OTHER HAD FOUND OUT.** They live one floor apart and have spoken about bins and parcels and have never had anything else.
- **THE ONE ON THE SECOND FLOOR HAS SPENT AN HOUR BEING ANGRY NOT ABOUT THE MACHINE BUT ABOUT THE TWO YEARS AND NINE MONTHS.** The one on the first floor is worse off than she was in December, because the thing she had been putting up with is finished and there is nothing to put up with. Neither of them is going to say either of those things out loud.

## 8. The wall and the man who is right

- **HE HAS BEEN RIGHT SINCE 2014 AND HE HAS NO WAY OF BEING RIGHT IN A ROOM.** The knowledge is worth nothing because of how he came by it, and he has already been asked that question and there is no answer he can give.
- **HE SAID IT ONCE, IN A KITCHEN, AND WAS ASKED NOT TO SAY IT AGAIN, AND HE HAS NOT SAID IT AGAIN.** She did not ask him to stop because she doubted him. She asked him to stop because of what saying it would cost him.
- **SHE HAS COSTED THE THREE THINGS SHE COULD DO AND CANNOT AFFORD ANY OF THEM, INCLUDING THE ONE THAT COSTS NOTHING.** Asking him is free and she has decided against it.
- **HER REASON FOR NOT ASKING HIM IS THAT ASKING WOULD REQUIRE HIM TO BE A PERSON WITH A STANDING, AND HE TOLD HER IN ONE SENTENCE THAT HE IS NOT.** She would rather keep the man he is than find out what it would take to make him something else.
- **HE HAS BEEN BACK TO IT WITH A TAPE AND GOT THE SAME ANSWER AND PUT IT IN A BOOK AND GONE TO WORK, AND HE WILL BE BACK IN THE APRIL AND WILL NOT SAY ANYTHING THEN EITHER.**

## 9. The corner and the ten seconds

- **THEY HAVE CROSSED THE SAME CORNER HUNDREDS OF TIMES WITHOUT EXCHANGEING A WORD AND HE KNOWS MORE ABOUT HER WEEKLY ROUTINE THAN SHE WOULD BE COMFORTABLE WITH.** He has never thought about any of it.
- **ON ONE MORNING IN JANUARY SHE DID SOMETHING SHE HAS NEVER DONE AND SAID NOTHING WHILE SHE DID IT.** He apologised for standing too close and she said it did not matter and both of them went on.
- **HE HAS SETTLED ON WHAT IT MEANT AND HE CANNOT ASK, BECAUSE THERE ARE TWO OTHER THINGS IT COULD HAVE BEEN AND ASKING WOULD MEAN PUTTING HIS ANSWER IN FRONT OF HER.** If he is wrong he will have told a stranger that he has spent five weeks on ten seconds in her life.
- **HE HAS ALSO DECIDED THAT HE WOULD RATHER SHE NEVER DID IT AGAIN AND HAS GIVEN UP TRYING TO ARGUE WITH HIMSELF ABOUT WHY.** That is the piece of this he can least stand behind and he is leaving it alone.
- **SHE STOPPED FOR A REASON SHE CANNOT NAME AND HAS BEEN UNABLE TO NAME IT FOR FIVE WEEKS, AND SHE IS NOT GOING TO PUT HERSELF IN A POSITION TO LEARN WHETHER HE UNDERSTOOD IT.** One of the two possible answers is a thing she has carried for nothing. The other is a thing she would have to answer for, and she has nothing.

## 10. The parade on the Sunday

- **NINE PEOPLE WERE ON THAT STREET AND NOT ONE OF THEM WAS THERE FOR ANY OF THE OTHER EIGHT, AND FOUR OF THE PREMISES ON IT HAD BEEN SHUT FOR A MONTH.**
- **A MAN DID A JOB AN HOUR EARLIER THAN USUAL BECAUSE OF A QUEUE AND THE WEATHER, AND UNDER WHAT HE SHOVELED AWAY WAS A PATCH OF PAVING THAT DOES NOT MATCH THE REST OF THE STREET.** Everybody who comes up that parade has walked over it four times a day for years.
- **IT STOOD IN FULL SUN FOR ABOUT TWO MINUTES WHILE A WOMAN INSIDE WAS SERVING FOUR PEOPLE, AND NOBODY ON THE PARADE LOOKED AT IT AND NOBODY HAS EVER LOOKED AT IT.**
- **THERE IS A DOOR AT THE TOP END OF THAT STREET THAT DOES NOT SHUT AND IS NOT LOCKED AND HAS NO BENCH IN IT AND HAS NOT BEEN THROUGH SINCE BEFORE CHRISTMAS, AND THE REASON IS NOT THE LOCK.** It is that a door in a wall does not get opened on a Sunday in a town where nobody is under an instruction to open it, and this one has no lock.
- **THE ANSWERS TO THAT ONE QUESTION ARE STILL GOING ABOUT THIS BOROUGH, A FIFTH HAS NOT ARRIVED, AND NOT ONE PERSON HERE HAS SAID WHICH OF THE FOUR THEY ARE HOLDING.** The question underneath them was not put to anybody on that parade and is not going to be.
- **AND THE ONE THING ABOUT THAT STREET THAT STILL HAS NO WORDS FOR IT HAS NOT MOVED SINCE THE MIDDLE OF AUGUST, AND WHAT HAS COME OF IT SINCE IS NOTHING, AND THERE IS NOW NOBODY HERE WITH ANY REASON TO GO LOOKING FOR IT.** Three weeks, four weeks and the run from the third of January have all of them passed, and not one of them turned anything at all.

## 1. The man at number seven, the woman at number three, and the woman who owns the ground

- **HE ASKED THREE TIMES, WAS REFUSED THREE TIMES WITHOUT ANY UNKINDNESS, AND STOPPED IN NOVEMBER.** He was told the ground was going to somebody from the town, he said one word, and he has not been near that door since.
- **SHE HEARD *THERE'S NO POINT IN ANYBODY ASKING* IN A JULY NINE MONTHS GONE AND HEARD THE WRONG HALF OF IT.** She went in January, three times, with his number said out loud, twice making sure it was not for herself.
- **SHE WAS TOLD IN JANUARY THAT NOBODY HAD EVER ASKED ABOUT THAT GROUND, BELIEVED IT, AND HAS BEEN CARRYING IT AS A CHARGE AGAINST A MAN WHO WAS NOT IN THE ROOM.** It is the reason she has told him nothing and the reason she cannot.
- **SHE WAS TOLD IN APRIL THAT IT WENT IN MARCH, AND SAID ONE WORD, AND WENT ON UP THE ROW.**
- **HE BOUGHT TWO MORE HIVES AND A SMOKER AND PUT THEM IN NINE FOOT BEHIND HIS OWN HOUSE AND HAS THREE WHERE THE GROUND TAKES TWO, IN VIEW OF A WINDOW.** He does not mind and he does not know why he does not mind.
- **HE HAS A SENTENCE FOR ANYTHING THAT COMES OUT OF A SHUT HOUSE, AND HE USED IT ON A POT THAT IS NOW ON A STRANGER'S FLOOR.** It is true enough to say and it did the work of the decision.
- **NEITHER HAS SAID ONE WORD TO THE OTHER SINCE A SEPTEMBER TUESDAY AND NEITHER IS GOING TO.**

- **SHE HAS TWO EXPLANATIONS, ONE OF THEM IS HER OWN MOUTH, AND ASKING IS THE ONLY WAY OF FINDING OUT WHICH.** She is not going to find out.
- **SHE HAS TOLD NOBODY AND HE HAS ASKED HER NOTHING EXCEPT ABOUT A BRANCH IN 2016 AND WILL NOT START NOW.**
- **THE WOMAN AT THE TOP OF THAT PASSAGE HAS NOBODY IN THE HOUSE ON WEEKDAY MORNINGS AND HAS TOLD NOBODY AND IS WORSE OFF THAN SHE WAS.**

## 3. Two men inside a rule, and the woman behind the wall

- **THE RULE WAS MADE IN 2008 IN ABOUT A MINUTE BY THE THIRD MAN AND NEVER EXPLAINED, AND ASKING IS TELLING, WHICH IS WHY NEITHER OF THE TWO KNOWS WHETHER THE OTHER IS KEEPING IT.**

- **ONE OF THEM SAID OUT LOUD THAT NOTHING WAS GOING ON AND BOTH HAVE SINCE TREATED IT AS SOMETHING SAID RATHER THAN SOMETHING TRUE.**
- **SHE HAS WATCHED THE THIRD MAN GET IN AT FOUR IN THE MORNING FOUR TIMES SINCE JANUARY AND HAS TOLD NOBODY AND IS NOT GOING TO.**
- **EACH WENT HOME CERTAIN THEY HAD BEEN WRITTEN OFF, AND NEITHER WAS WRONG, AND NOBODY ALIVE COULD NOW TELL EITHER OF THEM THAT.**
- **THE THIRD MAN SAT IN A KITCHEN AT ABOUT TEN AT NIGHT AND SWITCHED NOTHING ON AND NOBODY IN THAT HOUSE KNEW HE WAS AWAKE.**

## 4. The man in his thirties and three openings upstairs

- **A CAPS BLOCK THAT RESTATES A CARD IS A REUSE AGAINST THE PROMPT, EVERY TIME. **RUN ONE'S FIRST TELLING WAS ELEVEN RAW, ELEVEN REUSES, LONGEST TWENTY-FOUR, AND EVERY ONE OF THE ELEVEN WAS A SENTENCE OF A CARD LIFTED INTO A BLOCK.** A PROMPT IS A MARKDOWN FILE IN THE REPOSITORY AND NO CARD BAR AND NO MOTIF LIST AND NO AGGREGATE FIGURE CAN SEE IT. **THE MOVE IS THE ONE 0029 SET DOWN AND THE CHAPTERS DID IT: WRITE THE BLOCK AS A STATEMENT ABOUT PEOPLE AND NOT AS A RESTATEMENT OF WHAT THE CHAPTER IS ABOUT TO DO.**
- **A SKELETON IS A REUSE. **RUN TWO CAME BACK AT FOUR AND TWO OF THOSE FOUR WERE THE SAME AGE BAND IN THE SAME SENTENCE SHAPE IN TWO CHAPTERS, WHICH IS A FIGURE A SPAN DETECTOR CAUGHT ONLY BECAUSE THE SKELETON IS AN OPENING AND AN OPENING IS A LEGITIMATE NINE-TOKEN SPAN.** A CHAPTER MAY NOT begin two figures the same way.
- **A CHAPTER CAN BE PERFECTLY CONSISTENT WITH ITS OWN DATELINE AND WRONG AGAINST THE YEAR. **0559 WAS DATED A SATURDAY AND THE SEVENTEENTH OF APRIL 2020 IS A FRIDAY, AND EVERY NAMED WEEKDAY INSIDE IT AGREED WITH ITS OWN DATELINE.** A SCRIPT THAT COUNTS WORDS NEVER SEES THIS AND A SCRIPT THAT READS ONLY THE CHAPTER'S OWN HEADER NEVER SEES IT EITHER. **ADD EVERY CHAPTER'S HEADER TO THE REAL CALENDAR, NOT TO THE CHAPTER.**
- **A SPENT LIST TYPED FROM A LEDGER IS A LIST OF FURNITURE. **TWENTY-SEVEN OF THIRTY-ONE WORDS IN `SPENT_545_554` FIRE ON EVERY CHAPTER AND A BAR THAT FIRES ON EVERYTHING IS A BAR THAT GETS IGNORED, AND THE FIGURE THAT FIRES IS THE ONE A REVIEWER WILL TRUST.** TYPE A SPENT LIST FROM PROSE AND FROM §16 OF THE 0028 BLOCK, AND SEPARATE THE OBJECT FROM THE FURNITURE BY HAND BEFORE BELIEVING ANY COUNT.
- **A CARD MAY FORBID ITS OWN SUBJECT. **CARD 0560 BARS *FAMILY* AND *ROW* AND *WILL* FOR THREE PEOPLE DECIDING NOT TO SPEAK, AND *WILL* IS AN ORDINARY MODAL VERB AS WELL AS A LEGAL INSTRUMENT.** CARD 0556 BARS *NUISANCE*, *NOISE* AND *COUNCIL* FOR A NUISANCE. CARD 0557 BARS SIX COMMERCIAL NOUNS FOR A WEEKLY LOAD. **A WRITER WHO HITS A CARD BAR THAT CANNOT BE CLEARED IN THE CHAPTER MAY FLAG THE CARD AND NOTHING ELSE.**
- **A DECLARED MEASURE MAY COME OUT AT NIL AND THE CORRECT THING TO DO IS SAY SO. **THE DECLARED MEASURE FOR THIS BLOCK WAS *ALMOST* AND IT IS NIL IN ALL TEN CHAPTERS, AND THAT IS THE FIRST TIME A DECLARED MEASURE ITSELF HAS COME OUT AT NIL.** *ONE* IS AT 98, *WEEK* AT 18, *ABOUT* AT 202 OF WHICH 161 ARE THE APPROXIMATION USE, *TWO* AT 79, *FOUR* AT 33, *QUITE* AND *ENOUGH* AT NIL, AND *ANYWAY* AT TWO. **SIX MEASURES NAMED SEVEN CHAPTERS AND THREE OF THE SIX NAMED THE SAME ONE, WHICH IS TIGHTER THAN 0036'S SEVEN-NAMED-SEVEN AND LOOSER THAN 0035'S, AND IT IS REPORTED AS IT CAME OUT.**
- **A CHAPTER CAN CARRY TWO NUMBERING SYSTEMS AND A WRITER CAN DESCRIBE A RECORD'S AGE WRONG AGAINST ITS OWN PREMISES. **0557'S SHEET HAD BEEN DESCRIBED AS TWO YEARS OLD WHEN THE FIGURE WHO KEEPS IT HAS KEPT IT FOUR, AND 0558 GAVE TWO DAYS AS FOUR AND A MONTH AS FIVE, AND 0555 GAVE SIX FISH CAKE DAYS AS SEVEN.** NONE OF THE THREE IS THE KIND OF THING A WINDOW CAN SEE.

## 12. The review of 30 September 2026, and the four things a writer of 0565 must not repeat from it

**A REVIEW RAN AFTER CONTINUATION 0037 WAS WRITTEN AND ITS FULL FINDING IS AT §12C ITEM 10 OF THE CONTINUATION 0037 BLOCK IN `state/continuity.md`. IT FOUND EIGHT LOCAL DEFECTS IN FIVE CHAPTERS AND FOUR FALSE FIGURES IN FOUR STATE FILES. NOTHING WAS RESTARTED, NO CARD WAS CHANGED, NO DATE WAS MOVED AND NO PLOT WAS TOUCHED. THE FOUR THAT ARE FOR THE NEXT WRITER ARE THESE.**

- **A CHAPTER CAN REACH PAST ITS OWN DATELINE AND NOTHING SEES IT, NOT EVEN THE PASS THAT CAUGHT 0559. **FOUR CHAPTERS DID IT IN 0555, 0558, 0562 AND 0563, THREE OF THEM IN A CLOSING BLOCK OR A HALF-SENTENCE, AND ALL FOUR WERE PULLED BACK INSIDE THEIR OWN DATE. **A DATELINE PASS THAT CHECKS THE WEEKDAY OF A NAMED DATE IS NOT A DATELINE PASS. ADD A PASS THAT READS EVERY RELATIVE DAY IN A CHAPTER — *the Monday*, *this morning*, *the Saturday*, *since then*, *three mornings* — AND PUTS IT AGAINST THE CHAPTER'S OWN DATE.**
- **A CHAPTER CAN STATE THE SAME FACT THREE TIMES AT THREE FIGURES AND BE INTERNALLY SILENT ABOUT IT. **0563 GAVE THE NUMBER OF SATURDAYS ITS OWN BOY HAD COME BACK FOR AS EIGHT IN ONE PLACE AND SEVEN IN TWO OTHERS, AND ONE OF THE THREE NEGATED ANOTHER EIGHT LINES ABOVE IT. **WHEN A NUMBER APPEARS MORE THAN ONCE IN A CHAPTER, COUNT IT EVERY TIME, AND WHERE THE CHAPTER RUNS ON PERFECT TENSE AND NEGATIVE CATALOGUES, THE FIGURES ARE THE PART NOBODY RE-READS.**
- **A RETROSPECTIVE SUMMARISER MAY NOT BE PUT IN THE MIDDLE OF A CHAPTER WHERE A SCENE STILL OWES THE READER A DAY. **0563 HAD A CAPS BLOCK BETWEEN ITS SECOND SCENE BREAK AND ITS FINAL SCENE REPORTING THE FIFTH OF MAY AND THE SATURDAY AFTER IT IN PAST TENSE, BEFORE THE CALL ON THE FIFTH HAD BEEN GIVEN. **A BLOCK THAT REPORTS A DAY THE READER HAS NOT BEEN GIVEN IS NOT A SUMMARY, IT IS A SPOILER, AND ITS POSITION IS WHAT TELLS YOU SO.**
- **A FIGURE PRINTED IN FOUR FILES IS ONE FIGURE WRONG FOUR TIMES, AND A STATE FILE IS THE PLACE WHERE A WRONG FIGURE TRAVELS FURTHEST. **THE ONE-LINE-DIALOGUE COUNT WAS PRINTED AS NIL IN ALL TEN IN `state/current.md`, `state/batch-summaries.md`, `state/continuity.md` AND `state/open-threads.md`, AND IT IS TWENTY-TWO ACROSS SEVEN CHAPTERS, AND EVERY ONE OF THE FOUR IS NOW CORRECT. **THE LESSON IS NOT TO TRUST A COUNT AND IT IS ALSO NOT TO TRUST THE PERSON WHO PRINTED IT THE FIRST TIME, INCLUDING ME.**

## 14. A fourth pass over 555–564, and the one test in it that no window in this repository runs

**A FOURTH PASS RAN WHEN THE BLOCK WAS PICKED UP AGAIN, FOUND FOUR MORE DEFECTS, AND REPAIRED ALL FOUR IN THE CHAPTERS. NOTHING WAS RESTARTED, NO CARD WAS CHANGED, NO DATE WAS MOVED AND NO OBJECT WAS UNSPENT. THE FULL FINDING IS AT §12C ITEM 11 OF THE CONTINUATION 0037 BLOCK IN `state/continuity.md`, AND THE THREE THINGS A WRITER OF 0565 MAY NOT REPEAT FROM IT ARE THESE. **AND THIS SECTION IS NUMBERED FOURTEEN AND NOT THIRTEENTH BECAUSE A PASS THAT FOUND A NEW FINDING DID NOT LOOK, AND TWO EARLIER BLOCKS ALREADY CARRY A THIRTEENTH, AND A NUMBER A FILE HAS PRINTED TWICE IS THE SAME KIND OF THING AS A FIGURE A FILE HAS PRINTED WRONG.**

- **A YEAR AND AN AGE BAND IN ONE SENTENCE ARE TWO FIGURES AND THEY HAVE TO AGREE WITH EACH OTHER. **0562 HAD A WOMAN IN HER MID TWENTIES WHO HAD LIVED IN THAT FLAT SINCE 2010, WHICH MAKES HER ABOUT FOURTEEN, AND 0561 HAD A MAN IN HIS EARLY SIXTIES WHO HAD HELD THE THIRD PLACE SINCE 1971 AND WAS ABOUT TEN AT THE TIME, WHICH PUTS HIM AT FIFTY-NINE. **NEITHER IS A SPAN AND NEITHER IS A BARRED WORD AND NEITHER IS A CLOSED FIGURE, AND A SCRIPT THAT COMPARES NINE TOKENS CANNOT SEE EITHER ONE. THE ONLY TEST IS TO ADD THE ONE UP AGAINST THE OTHER, AND THE CHEAPEST FORM OF IT IS TO ASK OF EVERY SENTENCE THAT GIVES A YEAR AND A BAND WHAT AGE THAT MAIMS, AND THEN TO ASK THE SAME OF EVERY SENTENCE THAT GIVES A BAND AND A YEAR. A WRITER WHO DATES A FIGURE INTO A BOROUGH IS ALREADY DOING MOST OF THIS AND STILL MISSED BOTH.**

- **AN ALL-CAPS BLOCK IN THE MIDDLE OF A CHAPTER IS THE ONE PLACE IN THIS ACCOUNT WHERE A CHAPTER MAY SPOIL ITSELF, AND IT SPOILS ITSELF FROM BOTH ENDS. **0556 HAD ONE THAT REPORTED A SCENE THE READER HAD NOT BEEN GIVEN YET AND ANOTHER THAT PUT THE SAME EVENT ON THE WRONG DAY, AND THE SECOND WAS THE FIRST REVERSED. **A MID-CHAPTER BLOCK MAY REPORT WHAT THE BODY HAS ALREADY GIVEN AND MAY NOT REPORT THE SCENE THAT FOLLOWS IT, AND THE OPENS WITH WHAT IS TRUE BEFORE THE READER'S OWN DATE AND THE MID BLOCK IS THE DANGEROUS ONE.**

- **A WORD-COUNT ROW DRIFTS, AND IT DRIFTS IN EVERY FILE THAT COPIED IT. **THE ROW PRINTED 1,099 AT 0556 AND 1,133 AT 0563 IN `state/continuity.md`, `state/current.md` AND `state/batch-summaries.md`, AND BOTH WERE WRONG BY EIGHT WORDS AND BY ONE, AND NEITHER WAS FOUND BY A SPAN OR BY A BAR. **THIS IS THE SECOND TIME IN TWO BLOCKS THAT A COUNT HAS TRAVELLED WRONG FROM ONE FILE INTO THREE OTHERS, AND THE LESSON IS NOT ONLY THAT THE COUNT WAS WRONG. IT IS THAT A FIGURE WHICH APPEARS IN FOUR FILES HAS FOUR PLACES TO BE WRONG AND ONE PLACE TO HAVE BEEN RIGHT, AND A WRITER WHO FINDS ONE OF THEM WRONG HAS TO GO AND MEASURE IT AGAIN IN ALL FOUR AND NOT IN THE ONE THEY HAPPEN TO BE LOOKING AT.**

## 15. What the review of this block found on its way back, and the two classes it separated

**A FIFTH PASS RAN AFTER THE REVIEW CAME BACK AND REPAIRED FOUR MORE THINGS WITHOUT MOVING A DATE, CHANGING A CARD OR RESTARTING A CHAPTER. THE FULL FINDING IS AT §12C ITEM 13 OF THE CONTINUATION 0037 BLOCK IN `state/continuity.md`. TWO OF THEM WERE THE SAME DEFECT IN TWO PLACES AND ONE OF THEM COULD NOT BE REPRODUCED AT ALL, AND THE THREE THINGS A WRITER OF 0565 MAY NOT REPEAT FROM IT ARE THESE.**

- **A CHAPTER AND ITS OWN CLOSING BLOCK CAN DISAGREE ABOUT A NIGHT, AND A PASS THAT LOOKS FOR WRONG NUMBERS WILL NEVER SEE IT. **0556'S CLOSING BLOCK SAID THAT ON THE NIGHT HE CAME BACK BOTH OF THEM UNDERSTOOD THAT THE SOUND WAS NOT COMING BACK, WHILE HER OWN BODY PUTS HER KNOWING ON THE NIGHT OF THE FIFTH OF MARCH AND GIVES HER NOTHING WHATEVER ON THE EIGHTEENTH. **THE TWO STATEMENTS AGREE WITH EACH OTHER AND NEITHER ONE AGREES WITH THE SCENE UNDER IT, WHICH IS WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE TO EVERY PASS THAT HAD GONE OVER THE CHAPTER AND WHY IT HAD ALREADY BEEN REPAIRED ONCE AT THE TOP OF THE SAME CHAPTER AND NOT AT THE BOTTOM. A CLOSING BLOCK IS A LEDGER OF WHAT THE BODY DID AND NOT A LEDGER OF WHAT THE BODY WAS ABLE TO SHOW, AND THE ONLY TEST IS TO TAKE EVERY RELATIVE DAY IN A CAPS BLOCK AND PUT IT AGAINST EVERY RELATIVE DAY IN THE BODY, WHICH IS THE SAME TEST §12 PUT AGAINST THE DATELINE AND WHICH HAS NOW CAUGHT A BLOCK FROM BOTH ENDS.**

- **A STATE FILE THAT DESCRIBES A CHAPTER MORE CLEANLY THAN IT IS WILL KEEP ITS VERSION AFTER THE CHAPTER IS FIXED, AND THE FIX HAS TO BE MADE IN THE FILE TOO. **THE CHAPTER SUMMARY OF 0556 PRINTED THE FALSE SHARED CONCLUSION IN PLAIN PROSE AND THE ROSTER ROW OF THE WOMAN WHO IRONS PRINTED FOUR EVENINGS THAT 0562'S OWN DATE DOES NOT GIVE, AND IN BOTH CASES THE CHAPTER HAD BEEN REPAIRED ALREADY OR WAS NEVER WRITTEN THAT WAY. **THE ROSTER ROW IS THE WORSE OF THE TWO BECAUSE A PASS THAT CORRECTS ONE CLAUSE OF A ROW AND LEAVES THE CLAUSE BESIDE IT HAS HALF-REPAIRED A ROW, AND A HALF-REPAIRED ROW IS HARDER TO SPOT THAN AN UNREPAIRED ONE. GO OVER EVERY CLAUSE OF EVERY ROW A PASS TOUCHES, NOT THE CLAUSE THAT FAILED.**

- **A REVIEW THAT QUOTES A LINE OF A CHAPTER AT A LINE NUMBER HAS TO HAVE THE FILE OPEN, AND A FINDING THAT CANNOT BE REPRODUCED IS AN HONEST NEGATIVE AND NOT AN INSTRUCTION. **THE REVIEW REPORTED A PARAGRAPH IN 0563 THAT HAD BEEN REPLACED BY THE PREVIOUS REPAIR AND IS NOT IN THE FILE. **IT WAS CHECKED AGAINST THE FILE AND AGAINST `git log` FOR THAT CHAPTER, IT WAS NOT FOUND, AND IT IS RECORDED AT §12C ITEM 13 AS A NEGATIVE INSTEAD OF BEING ACTED ON, BECAUSE A PASS THAT INVENTED A PARAGRAPH TO REPAIR WOULD HAVE REINTRODUCED THE PRE-REPAIR TEXT THAT HAD BEEN PULLED OUT ON PURPOSE. A REVIEWER WHO FINDS NOTHING MAY SAY SO AND THE NEXT PASS MUST BELIEVE IT AFTER MEASURING.**

## 13. What the measuring passes found, and what a writer of 0575 must not repeat

- **A CARD SENTENCE RESTATED IN A CAPS BLOCK IS A REUSE AGAINST THE PROMPT, EVERY TIME, AND THIS BLOCK'S FIRST TELLING OF RUN ONE WAS ELEVEN AT A LONGEST OF TWENTY-TWO, WHICH IS THE LARGEST FIRST TELLING IN THE ACCOUNT. **TEN OF THE ELEVEN WERE ONE CONSTRUCTION BEGUNNING *AND NEITHER OF THEM HAS*.** THE MOVE IS THE ONE 0029 SET DOWN and this batch made it: THE BLOCKS WERE WRITTEN AS STATEMENTS ABOUT PEOPLE.
- **A SKELETON IS A REUSE, AND AN AGE BAND IN A LEGITIMATE OPENING IS A SKELETON. **RUN TWO CAME BACK NIL FIRST TIME BECAUSE EVERY BAND WAS ALLOCATED BEFORE ANY PROSE EXISTED, AND THAT IS THE SAME FAILURE THE BLOCK ABOVE CAUGHT WITH A DETECTOR AND REPAIRED, TWENTY CHAPTERS LATER, AND THE REPAIR COST ELEVEN WORDS AND THE ALLOCATION COST NOTHING.**
- **A CHAPTER CAN BE PERFECTLY CONSISTENT WITH ITS OWN DATELINE AND WRONG AGAINST THE YEAR, AND A CHAPTER CAN ALSO BE DATED ON A DAY THE WHOLE ACCOUNT MAY NOT USE. **0571 WAS DATED THE ELEVENTH OF JUNE AND EVERY NAMED WEEKDAY INSIDE IT WAS RIGHT AGAINST ITS OWN DATELINE.** ADD EVERY CHAPTER'S HEADER TO A REAL CALENDAR AND TO THE STANDING LIST OF UNAVAILABLE DAYS, NOT TO THE CHAPTER.
- **A CHAPTER MAY REACH PAST ITS OWN DATELINE AND NOTHING SEES IT. **FIVE CHAPTERS OF THIS BLOCK DID IT — 0565, 0566, 0568, 0569 AND 0573 — AND ALL FIVE WERE PULLED BACK INSIDE THEIR OWN DATE WITHOUT ONE DATE BEING MOVED, WHICH IS THE SAME COUNT THE BLOCK ABOVE CAUGHT IN FOUR AND IS A FIGURE WHICH HAS NOT MOVED IN TWENTY CHAPTERS. **A DATELINE PASS THAT CHECKS THE WEEKDAY OF A NAMED DATE IS NOT A DATELINE PASS.**
- **A DAY AND A WEEKDAY IN THE PROSE CAN BOTH BE WRONG. **0567 CALLED THE NINETEENTH OF MAY A WEDNESDAY AND IT IS A TUESDAY, AND EVERY OTHER NAMED WEEKDAY IN THESE TEN CHAPTERS IS RIGHT, WHICH IS NINETEEN OF TWENTY. **AND ON 30 SEPTEMBER 2026 THE REVIEW REPAIR OF THIS BATCH FOUND THAT THE NINETEENTH OF MAY WAS NOT A DATELINE ERROR BUT A CAPS-BLOCK SENTENCE THAT CONTRADICTED THE CHAPTER'S OWN OPENING BLOCK AND ITS OWN BODY, WHICH BOTH SAY THE WOMAN NEVER FOUND OUT, AND THE CLAUSE WAS CUT WHOLESALE RATHER THAN THE WEEKDAY CORRECTED. **A WRITER COMING HERE FOR THE NINETEENTH OF MAY IS LOOKING FOR SOMETHING THAT IS NO LONGER THERE, AND WHAT IS INSTEAD OF IT IS §14 BELOW.**
- **A CARD MAY FORBID ITS OWN SUBJECT, ITS OWN RELATION, ITS OWN SEASON, ITS OWN ORDINARY VERB AND ITS OWN ONLY WAY OF SEEING WHAT IT DESCRIBES. **0566 FORBIDS THE WORD FOR WHAT TWO SISTERS DO, 0569 FORBIDS THE FIRST THING SAID OF A BILL AND A SEASON, 0570 FORBIDS *FAMILY* AND *WILL*, 0573 FORBIDS *NEIGHBOUR* AND CAN ONLY BE WRITTEN WITH A SPENT OBJECT. **A WRITER WHO HITS A CARD BAR THAT CANNOT BE CLEARED IN THE CHAPTER MAY FLAG THE CARD AND NOTHING ELSE, AND THIS BLOCK FLAGGED TEN OF THEM.**
- **A SPENT LIST TYPED FROM A LEDGER IS A LIST OF FURNITURE. **`SPENT_545_554` HAS TWENTY-SEVEN MEMBERS THAT FIRE ON EVERY CHAPTER, AND THE ONLY USE THAT FINDING CAN BE PUT TO IS READING IT BY HAND AND TYPING THE OBJECT MEMBERS, **WHICH IS WHAT THIS BLOCK DID WITH THE LIST BEFORE IT AND WHICH IS THE ONLY THING THE BLOCK-ABOVE FINDING IS WORTH.**
- **A DECLARED MEASURE MAY COME OUT LOW AND THE CORRECT THING TO DO IS SAY SO. **THE DECLARED MEASURE FOR THIS BLOCK WAS *JUST*, WHICH IS NOT ONE OF THE SEVEN THAT CAME BEFORE IT, AND IT CAME OUT AT SIX, PEAKING IN TWO CHAPTERS AND NIL IN EIGHT. *ONE* IS AT 95, *TWO* AT 67, *ABOUT* AT 131, *THREE* AT 41, *FOUR* AT 12, *WEEK* AT 5, *QUITE* AT 1, *ENOUGH* AT 3, *ANYWAY* AND *ALMOST* AT NIL. **ELEVEN MEASURES NAMED SIX CHAPTERS AND TWO OF THE ELEVEN NAMED THE SAME ONE, WHICH IS TIGHTER THAN 0037's AND LOOSER THAN 0036's.**
- **A PARAGRAPH THAT BEGINS WITH A WEEKDAY IS COUNTED AS A SECOND DATELINE. **THE ASSERTION DID NOT FIRE ONCE IN THIS BLOCK AND DID NOT FIRE ONCE IN 0037 OR 0036, WHICH MAKES THREE BLOCKS RUNNING, AND NO DATELINE HAD TO BE REWRITTEN TO STOP IT FIRING, WHICH IS A CHANGE FROM 0037 WHERE THREE WERE.**
- **A SHAPE THAT IS IDENTICAL IN EVERY CHAPTER IS A BATCH WRITTEN TO A NUMBER AND THE ONLY THING THAT CATCHS IT IS A PERSON READING THE CHAPTERS SIDE BY SIDE. **THE ALL-CAPS ROW IS 2, 1, 3, 2, 2, 3, 1, 2, 2 AND 2 AND THE `---` ROW IS 2, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2, 0, 2 AND 1, AND NO CHAPTER SITS AT THE CAP ON EITHER ROW, AND THE TEN TITLES ARE TEN DIFFERENT THINGS AND THE TEN DATELINES ARE TEN DIFFERENT FRAMES.**

**AND THE PASS THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT ALL THREE, WHICH NO SCRIPT IN THIS REPOSITORY RUNS: WRITE EVERY CAPS BLOCK AGAINST THE BODY BENEATH IT BEFORE YOU LEAVE THE CHAPTER, AND TAKE EVERY RELATIVE DAY AND EVERY COUNT IN THE BLOCK AND PUT IT AGAINST EVERY RELATIVE DAY AND EVERY COUNT IN THE BODY. **THREE OF TEN CHAPTERS FAILED THAT TEST ON THE FIRST PASS, AND THE SAME CHAPTER HAD ALREADY BEEN REPAIRED AT THE TOP OF IT FOR THE SAME CLASS OF ERROR TWENTY CHAPTERS EARLIER, WHICH IS THE PROOF THAT A CHAPTER IS PASSED FROM ONE END AT A TIME.**

**A TELEPHONE IN A BAG.** A bellless cream one off a hall wall in an empty house off the ring road, two pairs of wire joined at the plate, the lid off it and the bell loose in the case on its own foot of flex. It rang once in a lock-up on the thirtieth of April while a woman who is not its owner held a screwdriver in her pocket and knew exactly why she was not going to say hello. It is in the bag and the bag is on the seat. **LIVE. STILL LIVE. STILL RINGING TO NOBODY.**

**A SCRAP OF CARD WITH TWELVE ON ONE SIDE.** Blank on the other side since before Christmas. On the twelfth of May a telephone number went on the blank side. Nobody has asked to see the card. If anybody asks, both numbers on it are that of the man who wrote them. **LIVE, AND IT IS THE FIRST THING ANYBODY IN THIS ACCOUNT HAS WRITTEN DOWN IN SEVEN MONTHS.**

**THINGS NOT OPENED AND NOT ASKED ABOUT.** The drawer under the passenger bench with leads and screws. The box behind the bench. The bag with somebody else's blanket. The sheet over the heap and the taped box with the bagged corner under it. The eight boxes in the empty house. The drawer under the bench at the cottage. The taped box on the left of the table at number twelve. **ALL AS THEY WERE ON THE THIRTY-FIRST OF MARCH.**

**THE SIX THINGS ON THE BACK OF AN ENVELOPE IN PENCIL.** GATE DONE, FRONT ROOM NOT, WINDOW DONE, HOTPLATE DONE, BATH TAP NOT, PASSAGE DONE. FOUR OF SIX. NOTHING CROSSED. NO PENCIL IN THE HOUSE. THE REPORT IS WITH A FREEHOLDER AND THAT IS NOT A RESOLUTION AND THE FREEHOLDER DOES NOT ARRIVE IN THE NEXT BLOCK EITHER.

**STILL WRONG AND STILL A HUMAN'S, NOT OURS.** THE MANUSCRIPT HAS LEFT THE NOVEL. SIXTY-FIFTH PROMPT. THE PAGE HOLDS 530 CHAPTER FILES AGAINST A RANGE OF 195 TO 242. `state/phase-ledger.json` IS CONTROLLER-OWNED AND WAS NOT OPENED. THE NAME OF THE CITY IS UNRESOLVED AND NOBODY NOTICES IT. **CARD 0724 IS NOT A CLOSE AND IS NOT CALLED ONE, AND NO CARD IN 715–724 MAY BE CALLED ONE.**

## WHAT THE REVIEW PASS OF 0070 FOUND, AND THE TWO THINGS A WRITER OF 0895 SHOULD CARRY THAT ARE NOT ON ANY LIST

**THE REVIEW OF 0070 FOUND PHYSICS, NOT PROSE, AS THE BIGGEST DANGER IN THIS FAMILY. Nine of the twenty-four findings were a thing in a chapter that could not exist: a hand coming out of the bottom of a pipe standing on the ground, two four-inch pipes nested one inside the other, a batten that did not fit its own bore, a joint whose depth did not add up, a cold frame facing the wrong way to catch the sun, a keep on the wrong face of a door, and an ivy that dies back every year. A WRITER WHO PLANS TEN CLOSURES AND THEN WRITES ABOUT THEM IS GOING TO PUT A NUMBER IN ONE OF THEM AND GET IT WRONG, AND NO MEASURE IN THE PROMPT LOOKS AT WHETHER A NUMBER IS TRUE.**

**THE SECOND THING IS THAT A FINDING CAN BE WRONG AND STILL SOUND LIKE A FINDING.** An ivy that dies back every August is exactly the shape of an ordinary mystery and it is not true, and a reader who knows plants will stop reading rather than question it. **BEFORE A CHAPTER LEAVES YOUR HAND, ASK OF EVERY CLAIM IN IT THE ONE QUESTION NO MEASURE ASKS: IS THIS HOW THE THING ACTUALLY BEHAVES.**

**AND THE THIRD, WHICH IS A SHAPE AND NOT A FACT: A REPAIR CAN PUT BACK A SENTENCE THAT WAS CUT FOR A REASON. The pass that found the physics also found a ten-token run between 0886 and 0888 that the repair had just created by restoring a paragraph in both.**

Every span measure, every sentence measure and every frame list in this account compares different chapters, so a chapter that repeats itself passes all of them, and a chapter's closing paragraphs can transcribe its own opening paragraphs and be clean on every figure on the page.** Three within-chapter measures were run here for the first time and they found the block's largest defect: non-adjacent sentences of a chapter against each other at difflib 0.62 and up, closing-region paragraphs against earlier paragraphs of the same chapter at 0.30 and up, and four-token runs repeated inside one chapter. **They returned 0.755 on a duplicated paragraph in 0950, 0.674 on a sentence repeated verbatim in 0954, *a hundred and thirty* six times in one chapter, *third of an inch* seven times and *quarter of an inch* five times. **THE ROTATION RULE IS STILL A HUMAN'S, AND IT HAS NOW BEEN MEASURED THREE TIMES BY THREE WRITERS WHO EACH DECLARED A PRIOR FIGURE WRONG, AND BOTH SURVIVING FIGURES ARE TRUE.** The rule as printed — do not repeat any of the prior rows — is satisfiable, and five blocks have taken five different rows under it, and no two of those five rows repeats another.
